# Binary rotation certificates: actual verification and remaining machine bridge

CTB-24/FDSA-5-93 requires an explicitly encoded rotation-distance decision problem
with polynomial-size witnesses and polynomial verification. The fixed-width
binary predecessor, measured partial rotations, actual structural equality,
finite-word encodings and linear bit/path/move prefix parsers have accepted
Lean owners. The restored author continuation adds actual stack tree and complete
input parsers, the binary-fuel streaming checker, attained-minimum encoded
witnesses and a complete input/certificate verifier. Its word-level contracts
state exact raw acceptance, a witness bound `2*M^2`, and work at most
`32*(M+W+1)^2` for every raw word pair. The expanded author draft adds the actual
fixed-four-bit codec and `verifyBitsRun`: its binary contracts state exact raw
acceptance, a bit witness bound `I^2`, and work at most `40*(I+C+1)^2` for every
raw bit pair. Here `M,W` count symbols and `I,C` count input/certificate bits.
These descriptions identify source definitions and theorem claims. Exact-candidate
build/audit and independent Standards and Spec outcomes for the expanded draft
remain pending until matching delivery evidence is supplied; earlier outcomes
retain their recorded scopes. Receiving acceptance remains separate and is not
inherited from the foundations. The source-required computational-model
cost-simulation/NP bridge remains unfinished. No new source row is qualified:
Chapter 5 remains 92/94, with
FDSA-5-92 and FDSA-5-93 open. [CTB](../textbooks/CTB.json) owns the complete
requirements and progress.

Cumulative source integration through 084 is tracked in
[issue #660](https://github.com/VladimirMarko/conaled/issues/660). Seed085 restores
its accepted published prerequisite `bc95f503ccbf043136c6699992388f750270e8e6`.
That earlier acceptance covers the predecessor/execution/encoding/linear-parser
foundations; it does not cover the new parser/stream/witness/verifier/codec/binary-wrapper

retains receiving acceptance under #659. The author prepares this increment on

these foundations nor the expanded author increment completes FDSA-5-93.

## Declared structural observation

All new programs return `Resources.Measured value Nat`. The tariff charges:

- one entry/dispatch per activation of each named recursive primitive or
  parser/checker state, covering its finite local constructor/tag distinctions;
- one per newly constructed list cons or tree node;
- one per returned `some`, `none`, or Boolean literal.

Nil, Unit and finite tag constants, projections, tuple/record/control packaging,
aliases and reuse of an already returned value are free. Returning a recursive
result directly constructs no additional result. `Measured.bind` and natural
addition used only to accumulate observations are measurement machinery.

This is an explicit source-event observation. It is not compiler instrumentation,
allocation measurement, bit complexity or machine time. Variable traversals,
reconstruction, binary borrowing and structural comparison are actual programs;
none is replaced by an uncharged whole-operation oracle. Mathematical node
counts, decoded natural values and lengths occur in contracts and proofs, not as
unaccounted runtime work in these primitives.

## Implemented fixed-width predecessor

[BinaryCounter/FixedWidth](../../Applications/Resources/BinaryCounter/FixedWidth.lean)
reuses the existing little-endian `Bits` and independent mathematical `value`.
Leading high zeros are permitted. Empty and nonempty all-zero words both denote
zero. The executable `decFixedRun` never calls `value`, normalizes its width, or
expands the encoded natural into a unary list.

Its complete equations bind the actual returned recursive Option:

| Input/recursive outcome | Actual result | Work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty word | `none` | 2 |
| `true :: tail` | `some (false :: tail)` | 3 |
| `false :: tail`, recursive failure | `none` | recursive work + 2 |
| `false :: tail`, recursive success `ys` | `some (true :: ys)` | recursive work + 3 |

The true branch reuses the untouched higher-bit suffix. A borrowed prefix is
reconstructed only after the recursive predecessor succeeds. Existing `decBits`
retains its distinct canonicalizing contract: it maps `[true]` to `some []`,
whereas the new operation returns `some [false]`.

The public proofs establish, for every bit word `bs`:

- failure iff `value bs = 0`;
- every actual successful result `ys` has `ys.length = bs.length` and
  `value bs = value ys + 1`;
- positive value has an actual successful result, without canonicality;
- actual work is at most `3*bs.length+2`.

The arithmetic is independent of the implementation. At a true low bit,
`1+2*v` becomes `2*v`. At a false low bit, recursive success gives `v=w+1`,
and the returned true low bit has value `1+2*w`; thus `2*v=(1+2*w)+1`.
These equations also supply positivity where natural subtraction would need it.

Two exact whole-result theorems make early termination explicit. An all-zero word
of width `b` fails with work `2*b+2`. A word consisting of `r` low zeros followed
by one and any higher suffix returns `r` ones followed by zero and that unchanged
suffix, at work `3*(r+1)`. Numeric magnitude may vary arbitrarily in the reused
suffix without affecting that executed work.

## Implemented partial rotation and reconstruction

[RotationCertificate/Execution](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/Execution.lean)
uses the existing `RotationDirection`, `RotationMove`, `applyAt?` and `applyMove?`.
All rotations and positioned callbacks remain polymorphic in an arbitrary label
type and universe; they require no equality, ordering, inhabitance, cache or
legality assumption on raw inputs.

`rotateRun` executes the two legal root patterns, binding both newly constructed
nodes into the actual returned Option. Success costs 4: entry, two nodes and
`some`. An illegal root returns `none` at cost 2. Its value erases exactly to
`direction.apply?`, including every malformed root.

`applyAtRun` executes an actual measured callback. An empty position charges one
entry and calls it even at nil. A nonempty position at nil returns `none` at work
2 without inspecting the remaining path. At an ancestor it follows the selected
child, binds its actual result, and either propagates failure with 2 extra units
or reconstructs the original parent and untouched sibling with 3 extra units.
Both branch recurrences and raw callback erasure are public. `applyMoveRun` is a
free specialization to `rotateRun`, not a second rotation semantics.

The successful-depth theorem is derived from the actual partial operation:

`applyMove? move source = some target -> move.position.length + 2 <= source.numNodes`.

Each traversed ancestor contributes one node; a legal root rotation requires two
more. The premise is actual success, not a certificate field asserting a bound.
Measured success transports this law and existing node preservation/inversion
through the proved raw erasure. Successful work is exactly `3*d+5` for path
depth `d`. For **every** raw move/tree, actual work is at most `3*N+3`, where
`N` is source node count. This includes arbitrarily long supplied paths: traversal
stops at the first missing node.

The recurrences also explain the two failure forms. If the path reaches an
illegal root after `d` nonempty ancestors, work is `2*d+3`. If it instead reaches
nil while branches remain, work is `2*d+2`. Here `d` counts reached ancestors,
not the unvisited supplied suffix. The connected cases retain both distinctions.

## Implemented structural equality

`eqTreeRun` compares Unit-labelled shapes by actual constructor inspection and
left-first short-circuit recursion. Nil/nil and constructor mismatch each cost 2.
Two nodes charge one entry and compare the left subtrees. A false left result
returns a false literal at one extra unit; a true left result executes and
returns the right result directly. It never invokes a whole-tree equality oracle
and assigns it one unit.

The proofs give actual Boolean value `decide (source = target)`, work at most
`3*source.numNodes+2` for every target, and exactly that work for self-comparison.
The asymmetrical bound is intentional: an unmatched target subtree can be
arbitrarily large and is not visited after a constructor mismatch. The self case
sums both child costs and one entry, giving
`(3*L+2)+(3*R+2)+1 = 3*(L+R+1)+2`.

## Connected cases and minimum-versus-route separation

[MeasuredRotationCertificate](../../Examples/MeasuredRotationCertificate.lean)
connects the public contracts to independently fixed literal and arbitrary-input
cases. Receiving #660 accepts these foundations with a complete whole-library
build and exhaustive proof audit. This does not qualify the full FDSA-5-93
source row or supply its remaining computational-model correspondence.

The bit cases are empty failure at 2; `[1] -> [0]` at 3; `[0,1] -> [1,0]` at 6;
`[0,0,1] -> [1,1,0]` at 9; `[1,0,0] -> [0,0,0]` at 3; and three zero bits failing
at 8. Arbitrary suffix, width, returned-value and positivity clients consume the
public general theorems.

Write `E` for nil, `U` for a singleton, `L2` and `R2` for the two-node chains,
`L3` for the left three-node chain and `B3` for the balanced three-node shape.
Equality costs are 2 for `E/E`, 5 for `U/U`, 8 for `L2/L2`, and 4 for the
left-first mismatch `L2/R2`. Arbitrary skipped right trees and arbitrary target
subtrees retain these mismatch observations. A root-right move on `L2` succeeds
at positioned work 5; the opposite illegal move costs 3. A root-right rotation
at the left child of `B3` fails at 5. A nonempty position at `E` fails at 2,
independently of its remaining length. Callback clients at nil demonstrate both
success and failure, and both parent branches use the actual replacement tree.

The existing stale-position example is now connected to measured execution:
root-right maps `L3` to `B3`, while right-at-left is legal on the original `L3`
but illegal on the reached `B3`. Each move must be checked in its current state.

The previously missing normalization separator is also concrete and proved:

- `rightPositions L3 = [[],[]]` and `rightPositions B3 = [[]]`;
- `connectionMoves L3 B3 = [rootRight,rootRight,rootLeft]`, length 3;
- the displayed route actually succeeds;
- one root-right move and distinct endpoints prove `Shape.distance L3 B3 = 1`;
- `distance_spec` supplies an attained trace of length 1, strictly shorter than
  the normalization route.

Thus a threshold-one completeness proof cannot simply submit the normalization
route. The verifier's completeness construction below selects the attained
minimum, while its acceptance contract permits a non-shortest certificate
whenever that certificate's own length fits the supplied threshold.

## Implemented finite-alphabet codes and accumulator emitters

[Encoding](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/Encoding.lean) fixes
`Tag = Fin 16` and `Word = List Tag`, with distinct symbols:
`E=0`, `N=1`, `sep=2`, `bit0=3`, `bit1=4`, `endInput=5`, `rotL=6`, `rotR=7`,
`pathL=8`, `pathR=9`, `endMove=10`; codes 11 through 15 are invalid syntax.
The separate [BitCodec](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/BitCodec.lean)
owner now supplies actual four-bit packing and complete unpacking, described
below. All sixteen symbols are preserved by that representation, including the
five reserved syntax values; the reached syntax parser owns their rejection.
This finite alphabet still needs an actual machine implementation and numerical
simulation before it yields a machine-time conclusion.

The independent mathematical codes are now defined:

- preorder tree: `E -> [E]`, `node () l r -> [N] ++ treeCode l ++ treeCode r`;
- input: first tree, separator, second tree, separator, its actual little-endian
  bit tags, then `endInput`;
- move: direction tag, branch tags in order, then `endMove`;
- certificate: actual move words concatenated in execution order, with implicit EOF.

Their exact proved lengths are `2*N+1` for a tree;
`2*Ns+2*Nt+b+5` for an input with bit width `b`; `path.length+2` for one move;
and the sum of those move lengths for a certificate. Empty and high-zero bit
words remain distinct words, even when their independently decoded values agree.

The actual measured emitters use an accumulator suffix. Tree emission first
binds the actual emitted right suffix into left emission, then constructs the
parent N cons; nil constructs an E cons. Bit and path emission bind their actual
recursive result before constructing the current symbol. No executable body
uses a specification append as an uncharged whole-list callback.

| Actual emitter | Proved returned value | Exact structural work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `emitTreeRun t tail` | `treeCode t ++ tail` | `4*N+2` |
| `emitBitsRun bs tail` | `bitTags bs ++ tail` | `2*b+1` |
| `emitPathRun p tail` | `pathTags p ++ tail` | `2*d+1` |
| `emitMoveRun m tail` | `moveCode m ++ tail` | `2*d+3` |
| `emitCertificateRun ms tail` | `certCode ms ++ tail` | `2*W+1` |
| `emitInputRun s t bs` | `inputCode s t bs` | `2*M-1` |

Here `d` is path length, `W` the certificate word length and `M` the input word
length; none of these mathematical sizes is computed by the emitters. The move
emitter is a free nonrecursive adapter around path emission and two actual
conses, so it has no additional recursive-entry charge. Certificate emission
adds its own entry per move. Input emission has its specified wrapper entry and
constructs all three delimiter conses. Its subtraction-free cost theorem is
`cost+1 = 2*M`, justified by the exact positive input length; it also exposes the
natural subtraction form.

## Implemented linear prefix parsers

[LinearParser](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/LinearParser.lean)
contains actual bit, path and move parsers. A bit/path parser dispatches on its
next symbol. Its delimiter returns the empty decoded list and the exact supplied
suffix at work 2; EOF or a foreign symbol returns none at work 2. An element tag
calls the parser on the actual tail. Recursive failure adds entry+none, or 2;
success binds the actual decoded tail and suffix, reconstructing cons+some under
that entry, or 3. No unvisited suffix is scanned after either terminal case.

The move parser recognizes a direction, calls the actual path parser and returns
its actual path and suffix inside the existing `RotationMove` record. Its own
dispatch and returned Option add 2; record/pair packaging is free. It decodes
syntax only and does not claim the move is legal on a supplied tree.

The complete public recognition statements quantify over every raw word:

```
parseBitsRun raw returns some(bs,rest)
  iff raw = bitTags bs ++ [endInput] ++ rest
parsePathRun raw returns some(path,rest)
  iff raw = pathTags path ++ [endMove] ++ rest
parseMoveRun raw returns some(move,rest)
  iff raw = moveCode move ++ rest
```

These are equivalences to the independently defined codes, not only roundtrip
checks on encoder outputs. Complete whole-result prefix equations also prove
the exact returned suffix and work for any encoded value followed by arbitrary
material. Applying the actual parser to equal prefixes proves uniqueness of
both decoded value and suffix. Separate roundtrip theorems feed actual measured
emitter outputs directly to the actual parsers.

| Parser | Exact successful work | Bound for every raw word |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bits of width `b` | `3*b+2` | `3*raw.length+2` |
| Path of length `d` | `3*d+2` | `3*raw.length+2` |
| Move at depth `d` | `3*d+4` | `4*raw.length+2` |

Failure bounds include missing delimiters, foreign symbols and reserved tags.
Successful consumption is exact: bit/path parsing consumes decoded length+1;
move parsing consumes `position.length+2`. Consequently an actual successful
move parse consumes at least two symbols and strictly shortens the unconsumed
suffix. These facts about the executed parser justify the stream's termination
proof without computing a runtime suffix length.

[RotationCertificateCodecs](../../Examples/RotationCertificateCodecs.lean) retains
independently fixed literal words/costs and general clients. Empty, singleton and
two-node tree emitters cost 2,6,10. The empty-tree input word has length 5 and
emission cost 9; the one-step two-node input with threshold `[1]` has length 14
and emission cost 27. The decoder checks root and one-branch moves at 4 and 7;
missing move delimiters cost 4 or 6, and a leading foreign symbol costs 2.
Both directions/branches, arbitrary foreign suffixes, every reserved code 11–15,
redundant high zeros, exact consumption and prefix uniqueness are included.
Decoded root and nonroot moves can still be illegal on the selected tree; those
cases consume the existing actual partial executor and its distinct work.

## Implemented stack tree parser and complete input parser

[TreeParser](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/TreeParser.lean)
provides the actual preorder parser. Its `TreeFrame` values await a left child or
retain an actual returned left child while awaiting the right. `resumeTreeRun`
recurses on the pending frames and constructs each closed parent from the actual
children. `parseTreeLoop` recurses only on its actual input-list tail; it never
computes a suffix length or reparses a consumed prefix. The free `done`/`next`
control result separates these two structural recursions.

The source proofs use a mathematical `stackPrefix`, which is absent from the
executable body. `resumeTreeRun_prefix` supplies both completed-tree and
continued-stack identities. Input-list induction gives soundness under arbitrary
frames; tree induction gives complete consumption under arbitrary frames and
suffixes, retaining a continuation that itself fails. The potential
`2*frames.length` pays for repeated resumes and yields the arbitrary-input bound.
The detailed derivation below remains with this mathematical owner.

The public recognition statement is an equivalence for every raw word:

```
(parseTreeRun raw).1 = some (t, rest) iff raw = treeCode t ++ rest.
```

`parseTreeRun_code` records the whole returned result and exact work.
`parseTreeRun_consumed_length` and `parseTreeRun_rest_length_lt` give the exact
consumed prefix and strict suffix decrease. `parseTreeRun_prefix_injective`
determines both the decoded tree and suffix from equal codes.
`parseTreeRun_emit` feeds the actual accumulator emitter result into this parser.

[InputParser](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/InputParser.lean)
binds the actual tree/separator/tree/separator/bit results, then checks the
actual final suffix for EOF. Its `ParsedInput` retains both Unit-labelled trees
and the original little-endian bit word, including empty and redundant high-zero
representations. Its complete recognition statement is

```
(parseInputRun raw).1 = some (s, t, bs) iff raw = inputCode s t bs.
```

Wrong or missing separators, missing tree subterms, foreign/reserved symbols,
missing bit delimiters and material after `endInput` reject. The tree parser
leaves any suffix untouched; the input parser requires the entire encoded input.
`parseInputRun_code_append` and `parseInputRun_trailing` expose the exact final
EOF decision: an arbitrary nonempty trailing suffix changes the result to none
without changing the work spent on the encoded prefix. No trailing traversal
occurs. All failure branches stop at their failed component.

| Actual parser | Exact successful work | Bound for every raw word |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tree of size `N` | `7*N+3` | `5*raw.length+2` |
| Complete input with tree sizes `Ns,Nt` and bit width `b` | `7*Ns+7*Nt+3*b+15` | `20*(raw.length+1)` |

The input wrapper charges one entry. Each separator parser charges one entry
and one returned Option; the final EOF checker does the same. A newly propagated
none costs one. Beyond the two tree parsers and bit parser, successful overhead
is `1+2+2+2=7`. Their three fixed constants add `3+3+2=8`, giving the full constant
**15**. Tree frames, control and tuple packaging remain free. All these formulas
are declarations in the new source; validation and independent review are tied
to the exact delivered candidate.

`parseInputRun_length` gives `M=2*Ns+2*Nt+b+5` after any actual successful parse;
`parseInputRun_sizes_le` bounds both node counts and bit width by `M`.
`parseInputRun_injective` distinguishes all three encoded fields, and
`parseInputRun_emit` connects the actual input emitter directly to the actual
parser. These observations are mathematical consequences of parsing, not
uncharged runtime size traversals.

[RotationCertificateParsing](../../Examples/RotationCertificateParsing.lean)
connects the new public contracts to the retained independent cases. Arbitrary
suffixes accompany literal empty/singleton/two-node tree costs 3/10/17; `[N]`
and `[N,E]` fail at 4 and 7, and `[E,rotR]` returns nil and its untouched foreign
suffix at 3. Every reserved tag 11–15 rejects at tree start and in the full input,
including a threshold-region case that leaves an arbitrary tail uninspected.
The complete empty input costs 15 and the two-node threshold `[1]` input costs
46. Missing/wrong/repeated delimiters, missing children, trailing material,
redundant high zeros and distinct words with equal numeric thresholds are retained.
Universal clients consume recognition, work, suffix, uniqueness and emitter
roundtrip contracts; parse-then-emit restores the actual raw input, and tree
emission followed by parsing has combined work `11*N+5`.

Input syntax intentionally accepts unequal-size endpoint trees. The connected
empty-to-singleton example parses at 22 and separately excludes any successful
mixed rotation trace by node preservation. The actual stream's acceptance theorem
connects this distinction to its final structural equality: unequal sizes cannot
accept, although syntax parsing succeeds. A complete extra certificate move is
another move to charge and check, even after the current tree equals the target;
no separate input-size traversal or early equality pass is performed.

## Actual streaming checker and complete raw acceptance

[Streaming](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/Streaming.lean)
defines `checkStreamRun bs current target certificate`. EOF charges the stream
entry and invokes actual `eqTreeRun`. A nonempty word first executes
`decFixedRun bs`; zero rejects before parsing. It then runs the actual move
parser, executes its returned move on the current tree, and recurses using the
actual returned predecessor bits, reached tree and unconsumed suffix. Every
failure returns immediately. No full-certificate parse precedes this stream,
and no list fold keeps traversing after failure.

The recursion is justified by `parseMoveRun_rest_length_lt` on each successful
parse. Ordinary measured bind passes actual values but does not expose the
argument's equality to its earlier result. The source therefore matches the
entire actual parser pair with an equation, retains its returned observation,
and adds that observation to the continuation. This supplies the proof of strict
suffix decrease without inserting a runtime check or another parser. The length
measure occurs only in the termination proof. The executed body calls neither
length, decoded numeric fuel, a code function, a node counter nor distance.

`checkStreamRun_nil`, `checkStreamRun_cons`, `checkStreamRun_no_fuel`,
`checkStreamRun_parse_failure`, `checkStreamRun_move_failure` and
`checkStreamRun_step` expose whole-result equations. Let `D`, `P`, `A`, `Q` and
`S` denote the actual predecessor, parser, positioned-move, equality and recursive
stream observations at their reached inputs:

| Reached branch | Actual result | Stream work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Certificate EOF | equality's returned Boolean | `Q+1` |
| Nonempty, predecessor fails | false | `D+2` |
| Predecessor succeeds, parser fails | false | `D+P+2` |
| Parser succeeds, positioned move fails | false | `D+P+A+2` |
| All three stages succeed | recursive stream's returned Boolean | `D+P+A+S+1` |

The local-failure constant counts one entry and one new false. Reusing equality
or a recursive result constructs no new Boolean. `checkStreamRun_zero` exposes
numeric-zero rejection without making `value` executable; the stronger
`checkStreamRun_replicate_false` returns false at `2*b+4` for every nonempty raw
certificate and an all-zero word of width `b`, without inspecting that certificate.

The public contract is an equivalence for arbitrary raw words and arbitrary
little-endian bit lists, including redundant high zeros:

```
(checkStreamRun bs s t cert).1 = true iff
  exists moves, cert = certCode moves and applyMoves? moves s = some t
    and moves.length <= value bs.
```

`checkStreamRun_sound` uses strong induction on the actual certificate suffix
length. At success it reconstructs the encoded move prefix, uses the actual next
tree, and prepends that move to the recursive semantic trace. The predecessor
identity is `value bs = value returnedBits + 1`. `checkStreamRun_complete` uses
trace induction; a nonempty bounded trace gives positive fuel and therefore an
actual predecessor result. The empty trace is handled by actual final equality.
`checkStreamRun_iff` joins these directions. It assumes neither valid syntax,
legality, positive fuel, equal endpoint size nor a canonical bit representation.

## Attained-minimum encoded witnesses and the explicit language

[Witness](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/Witness.lean) keeps
mathematical witness selection separate from execution. Its `Yes input` language
is an explicit input code of two shapes of a common size `n` and an actual bit
word `bs`, with `Shape.distance s t <= value bs`. `yes_iff_trace` identifies this
language with encodings of successful mixed traces within that threshold. The
reverse direction obtains equal node counts from actual successful execution;
there is no assumed size-check field or circular verifier-correctness premise.

For every successful trace, `certCode_length_le_of_applyMoves` proves

`(certCode moves).length <= moves.length * s.numNodes`.

Each legal position has `position.length+2 <= n`, and successful prefixes
preserve the actual current tree's node count. These facts account for every
move word in the concatenated certificate. `minimum_certificate_bound` selects
an attained minimum from `Shape.distance_spec`; the same trace has length equal
to distance and encoded size at most `n*(2*n-2)`. Thus it fits both the supplied
threshold and the universal distance bound. A prescribed normalization route
would not give the first guarantee; the retained three-node example separates
the two constructions.

`yes_small_trace` combines this minimum with the explicit input-length bound to
obtain a trace within the threshold whose certificate has length at most
`2*input.length^2`. The inequality includes empty and singleton shapes, for which
the attained trace is empty. Neither this witness choice nor `n`, input length,
numeric threshold or distance is computed by the verifier.

## Complete verifier and uniform source-work bound

[Verifier](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/Verifier.lean)
defines `verifyRun input cert` by charging its wrapper entry and binding the
actual complete input parser. Parser failure returns one new false and does not
inspect the certificate. Success passes the returned source, target and original
bit word to `checkStreamRun`, reusing its actual returned Boolean.

| Public source contract | Claim |
| --- | --- |
| `verifyRun_accept_iff` | Acceptance on arbitrary raw words iff the input and certificate are their exact independent codes and the decoded mixed trace succeeds within the threshold. |
| `verifyRun_sound` | Actual acceptance implies the independent `Yes input` language. |
| `verifyRun_complete_small` | Every `Yes input` has an actually accepted certificate of length at most `2*input.length^2`. |
| `yes_iff_exists_certificate` | `Yes input` iff some raw certificate is accepted by this verifier. |
| `verifyRun_work_all` | Every raw input/certificate pair has work at most `32*(input.length+cert.length+1)^2`. |
| `verifyRun_trailing_input` | Any nonempty input suffix after a complete code rejects without inspecting that suffix's tail or the certificate. |
| `verifyRun_emit_trace` | The actual input and certificate emitters feed an accepted successful bounded trace directly to the actual verifier. |

The work argument is pointwise on every raw word, including malformed and
overlong certificates. Write `b` for bit width, `n` for current source node count,
`W` for certificate-symbol length and `K=3*b+3*n+12`. The stream induction uses
`decFixedRun_cost_le`, `parseMoveRun_cost_le`, `applyMoveRun_cost_le` and
`eqTreeRun_cost_le`. It generalizes the actual bits, source, target and word;
its target-size bound is intentionally absent because equality short-circuits
within the source-size envelope.

| Branch | Bound before recursive composition |
| --- | --- |
| EOF | `3*n+3` |
| Decrement fails on a nonempty word | `3*b+4` |
| Parsing fails | `3*b+4*W+6` |
| Positioned execution fails | `3*b+3*n+4*W+9` |
| Successful prefix with path length `d` | local work at most `3*b+3*n+3*d+10`, then the recursive work |

For nonempty words, `(3*b+3*n+8)+4*W <= K*W` pays for every terminal failure.
For successful parsing, the exact returned suffix satisfies `W=d+2+W'`; the
parser costs exactly `3*d+4`. Width and node preservation identify the recursive
coefficient with `K`. Local work is at most `K*(d+2)`, so the induction hypothesis
on the returned suffix yields

`checkStreamRun work <= (3*b+3*n+12)*W + 3*n+6`.

This accounts for disjoint consumed prefixes directly from the actual parser's
length equation, without assuming a trace-count bound or scanning any suffix.
It also implies the earlier at-most-`W` attempt route retained below. A bound
on rotation count alone would omit parsing, binary borrowing, path traversal,
reconstruction and equality.

For an actual successful input parse, the parser bound is `20*(M+1)` and the
returned sizes satisfy `n,b <= M`. Including the wrapper gives at most
`6*M*W+12*W+23*M+27`. Input failure is smaller and independent of the certificate.
For `z=M+W`, use `6*M*W <= 3*z^2` and `12*W+23*M <= 23*z` to derive the stated
`32*(z+1)^2` envelope. No successful-parsing premise appears in `verifyRun_work_all`.
If the executed helper tariff changes, recalculate its coefficient while
retaining this full malformed-input scope.

## Actual fixed-four-bit codec and complete raw recognition

[BitCodec](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/BitCodec.lean)
separates independent mathematical `tagBits`/`wordBits` from executable
`packTagRun`, `packWordRun`, `decodeTagRun` and `unpackWordRun`. A tag uses four
bits in least-significant-first list order. The actual encoder and decoder use
finite sixteen-way dispatch; their executable bodies do not call a variable
`testBit`, division, the mathematical `value`, or a whole-word specification
encoder. The theorem `tagBits_value` identifies the numeric meaning of the
independent table. It is not an executable numeric decoder.

| Tag | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bits in list order | `0000` | `1000` | `0100` | `1100` | `0010` | `1010` | `0110` | `1110` |

| Tag | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 13 | 14 | 15 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bits in list order | `0001` | `1001` | `0101` | `1101` | `0011` | `1011` | `0111` | `1111` |

One tag packing charges one dispatch and four new conses: `packTagRun_eq`
returns `(tagBits tag ++ suffix, 5)` for an arbitrary unchanged bit suffix.
The Boolean cons payloads and finite tag constants add no separate return
charge. `packWordRun` first binds the actual recursively packed tail, then
packs its current tag onto that returned tail and charges its own entry.
Its empty case returns the supplied suffix at cost one. Thus, writing `N` for
the word length, `packWordRun_eq` states

```text
packWordRun word suffix = (wordBits word ++ suffix, 6*N+1).
```

`wordBits_length` gives exactly `4*N` prefix bits; `wordBits_append` preserves
block order. An arbitrary suffix can itself be incomplete: preserving that
suffix is an encoder contract, not a promise that complete unpacking accepts it.

`decodeTagRun` returns the appropriate finite tag at cost one for every four
Boolean arguments. `tagBits_decodeTagRun` recovers those same four original
bits. Tags 11 through 15 therefore survive decoding. Rejecting them in this
codec would contradict the public roundtrip for arbitrary `Word = List (Fin 16)`.

The complete decoder has five structural cases: empty, one bit, two bits,
three bits, and four heads followed by `raw`. Empty returns `(some [],2)`;
each partial ending returns `(none,2)`. In the four-head case it executes
`unpackWordRun raw` first. A failed suffix adds only entry plus a new `none`,
for two. A successful suffix executes the actual `decodeTagRun` and constructs
one cons and one `some`, for entry plus three, or four. Consequently
`unpackWordRun_cons4` states the exact whole-result recurrence:

```text
unpackWordRun (b0 :: b1 :: b2 :: b3 :: raw) =
  match unpackWordRun raw with
  | (none, c)      => (none, c+2)
  | (some tail,c)  => (some ((decodeTagRun b0 b1 b2 b3).1 :: tail), c+4).
```

The decoder reaches the end before constructing earlier tags. The failed-return
saving does not mean it left that raw suffix unvisited.

`unpackWordRun_tagBits` uses the finite table to replace the decoded head by
its original tag. Induction on a mathematical encoded prefix then gives the
stronger `unpackWordRun_prefix`, for every raw suffix and both outcomes:

```text
unpackWordRun (wordBits prefix ++ raw) =
  match unpackWordRun raw with
  | (none, c)        => (none, c + 2*prefix.length)
  | (some suffix,c)  => (some (prefix ++ suffix), c + 4*prefix.length).
```

The resulting source contracts retain all raw inputs and incomplete suffixes:

| Contract | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| `unpackWordRun_code` | `unpackWordRun (wordBits word) = (some word,4*N+2)`. |
| `unpackWordRun_sound`, `unpackWordRun_iff` | `(unpackWordRun raw).1 = some word` iff `raw = wordBits word`, with no validity premise. |
| `wordBits_injective` | Different symbol words have different bit codes, including zero blocks and high zeros. |
| `unpackWordRun_none_iff` | Failure iff `raw.length % 4` is nonzero. Every complete block is a valid codec value. |
| `unpackWordRun_short` | Any positive length below four fails at cost two. |
| `unpackWordRun_partial` | An arbitrary encoded `N`-tag prefix followed by one to three bits fails at cost `2*N+2`. |
| `unpackWordRun_cost_le` | Work is at most `raw.length+2` for every raw bit list. |
| `pack_unpack_eq` | Binding actual packing with empty suffix to actual unpacking returns `(some word,10*N+3)`. |
| `packWordRun_of_unpacked` | Repacking any actually returned word reproduces every original raw bit, at cost `6*N+1`. |

Soundness and malformed-length recognition use the decoder's five-shape
structural induction, including arbitrary raw suffixes. The four-head success
case combines the recursive suffix code with `tagBits_decodeTagRun`; no numeric
oracle or existence-based decoder is introduced. The uniform observation proof
uses the same cases: adding four input bits pays for either the two-unit failed
return or the four-unit successful return. This explains both its universal
scope and its exactness on complete encodings.

The actual packed emitters are free nonrecursive compositions of the previous
measured emitter and `packWordRun ... []`. `emitPackedInputRun_eq` returns
`wordBits (inputCode s t bs)` at exact cost `8*M`: the nonempty word emitter
costs `2*M-1`, and packing costs `6*M+1`. `emitPackedCertificateRun_eq` returns
`wordBits (certCode moves)` at cost `8*W+2`, from `2*W+1` plus `6*W+1`.
Their value and cost projections are public contracts. They bind actual
intermediate results; the mathematical codes identify those results in proofs.

## Binary verifier, independent language and universal observation

[BinaryVerifier](../../Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/BinaryVerifier.lean)
defines `verifyBitsRun inputBits certBits` with one wrapper entry and this
actual order:

1. Execute complete `unpackWordRun inputBits`.
2. On a returned word, execute `parseInputRun word` and bind its actual fields.
3. Only successful input syntax permits complete `unpackWordRun certBits`.
4. On a returned certificate word, call `checkStreamRun` with the returned
   original bits, source, target and certificate word, reusing its Boolean.

Each local decoder or input-parser failure creates one new false. The wrapper
does not call `verifyRun` and reparse the input; it composes the actual parser
and stream directly. Input decoding and syntax failures preserve arbitrary
unvisited certificate bits. Complete certificate decoding is eager: a partial
final block can reject before any fuel decrement, move parse, rotation or target
comparison. Token-stream untouched-tail results therefore do not imply an
untouched bit tail in this adapter.

Let `U,P,V,S` be the actual costs of reached input decoding, input parsing,
certificate decoding and streaming respectively. The whole-result equations are:

| Contract and reached branch | Returned result | Exact work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verifyBitsRun_input_none` | false after input decoding failure | `U+2` |
| `verifyBitsRun_parse_none` | false after input syntax failure | `U+P+2` |
| `verifyBitsRun_certificate_none` | false after certificate decoding failure | `U+P+V+2` |
| `verifyBitsRun_success` | the actual stream Boolean | `U+P+V+S+1` |

For exact codes of word lengths `M,W`, `verifyBitsRun_code_value` identifies
the Boolean with `(verifyRun input cert).1` for every pair of symbol words.
Successful input syntax gives exact work
`4*M+4*W+4+(verifyRun input cert).2` by `verifyBitsRun_code_of_some`.
Input syntax failure skips an arbitrary bit certificate and gives
`4*M+2+(verifyRun input []).2` by `verifyBitsRun_code_of_none`.
There is one wrapper entry in these expressions, not a second word-verifier
call or an extra input parse. `verifyBitsRun_packed_value` identifies the Boolean
when the actual `packWordRun` results supply both arguments.
`verifyBitsRun_emit_trace` connects the actual packed input and certificate
emitters to acceptance of every successful bounded trace.

The independent language is

```text
BinaryYes inputBits := exists word, inputBits = wordBits word and Yes word.
```

It uses the existing distance-based `Yes`; it is not defined by executable
acceptance. `verifyBitsRun_accept_iff` says every raw accepting pair consists of
exact complete codes of an accepting word pair. Composing the word iff yields
`verifyBitsRun_accept_iff_trace`: there exist actual source/target trees, original
binary fuel and a move list such that input and certificate bits are their exact
codes, `applyMoves? moves source = some target`, and
`moves.length <= value bs`. No syntax, canonical-width, positive-size or
successful-decoder premise narrows this raw-input equivalence.

`verifyBitsRun_sound` gives `BinaryYes` from acceptance. For completeness,
`verifyRun_complete_small` supplies a certificate of `W <= 2*M^2` symbols for
each `Yes` word. Exact packing lengths give input bits `I=4*M` and certificate
bits `C=4*W`, so

```text
C = 4*W <= 8*M^2 <= 16*M^2 = I^2.
```

`verifyBitsRun_complete_small` retains this bit witness bound together with
actual acceptance, including empty shapes and noncanonical binary fuel.
`binaryYes_iff_exists_certificate` then gives the independent language iff
existence of a raw accepted bit certificate. The witness proof uses the
already attained minimum; the executable decoder and verifier compute no
minimum distance or decoded natural threshold.

For universal work, write `I=inputBits.length`, `C=certBits.length`. The codec
bound is `raw.length+2` without a validity premise. A successful input decode
gives an exact word code, hence `I=4*M` and `M<=I`; similarly certificate
success gives `C=4*W` and `W<=C`. Combining the four actual branches yields:

| Branch | All-raw upper bound |
| --- | --- |
| Input decoding fails | `I+4` |
| Decoded input fails syntax | `21*I+24` |
| Certificate decoding fails | `21*I+C+26` |
| Both decoders and the input parser succeed | `32*(I+C+1)^2+I+C+4` |

The middle bounds use `parseInputRun_cost_le`, namely `20*(M+1)`. In the last
case, the word wrapper's actual parser/stream observation is bounded by
`verifyRun_work_all`; the two decoders add at most `I+C+4`. Each branch lies
below `40*(I+C+1)^2`, giving `verifyBitsRun_work_all` for every raw pair,
including malformed input and certificate bits. These are declared source-event
bounds, not a proof that forty machine steps implement a corresponding event.

## Retained derivation of the implemented tree parser

This derivation was preserved from the 20 November 2026 codec preparation. The
new TreeParser source now realizes its recursions, invariants and work arguments.
Its formal proof bodies and connected cases are the validation inputs; this
derivation explains their mathematics and does not replace checking or review.

### A structurally recursive stack tree parser

Use concrete frames `needLeft` and `needRight leftTree`. Define a free control
result `done tree` or `next frames`. These are control packaging, not charged
Option returns.

`resumeTreeRun frames t` recurses structurally on frames:

- Empty frames: return `done t`, charging the resume entry1.
- `needLeft :: outer`: return `next (needRight t :: outer)`, charging entry1
  and the replacement frame cons1.
- `needRight l :: outer`: construct the actual node(l,t), charge entry1 and
  node1, then resume the shorter outer stack with that returned node.

`parseTreeLoop raw frames` recurses structurally on the actual input list:

- EOF or foreign tag returns none at2.
- N charges entry1 and a `needLeft` cons1, then parses the actual tail.
- E charges entry1 and binds `resumeTreeRun frames nil`. A `done t` produces
  the one final `some(t, actual tail)` at1; `next frames'` parses the actual tail
  with frames'. Returning that recursive result directly constructs no Option.

No loop body computes a suffix length or reparses a consumed prefix. There is
no problematic mutual recursion: resume only traverses frames and returns
control; the input loop invokes itself only on its structural list tail.

### Soundness invariant with an independent prefix description

Define a mathematical `stackPrefix`, never used by the executable parser:

```
stackPrefix [] = []
stackPrefix (needLeft :: outer) = stackPrefix outer ++ [N]
stackPrefix (needRight l :: outer) = stackPrefix outer ++ [N] ++ treeCode l
```

The resume proof has two precise outcomes:

```
resume frames t returns done u
  -> stackPrefix frames ++ treeCode t = treeCode u
resume frames t returns next frames'
  -> stackPrefix frames ++ treeCode t = stackPrefix frames'
```

Both follow by structural frame induction. In the needRight branch, the
induction consumes exactly the independently defined code of node(l,t).
Then input-list induction gives the useful general soundness invariant:

```
parseTreeLoop raw frames returns some(u,suffix)
  -> stackPrefix frames ++ raw = treeCode u ++ suffix.
```

For N, the pushed-frame prefix supplies the consumed N. For E, substitute the
corresponding resume identity; `next` then uses the tail induction hypothesis.
The empty stack gives the desired forward prefix theorem. A converse for
arbitrary stacks is unnecessary.

### Completeness and exact successful work

Let `finishRun frames t rest` mean the actual measured resume followed by its
control branch: done creates the final some, next invokes the input loop on rest.
There is no extra helper-entry charge if this is only the named expression
already used by the E arm, rather than an extra executed state.

The source uses tree induction for the whole-result consumption equation

```
parseTreeLoop (treeCode t ++ rest) frames
  = let actual := finishRun frames t rest
    (actual.value, (7*t.numNodes+1) + actual.cost).
```

The nil tree contributes its E-loop entry1. For a node, the N entry/push gives2,
left consumption gives `7*L+1`, needLeft resume/replacement gives2, right
consumption gives `7*R+1`, and needRight resume/node gives2 before resuming the
outer frames. Their sum is `7*(L+R+1)+1`. This derivation binds actual intermediate
results and does not erase failed suffix continuations.

For empty frames, finish costs2 (resume entry and final some), so every encoded
tree followed by arbitrary material returns precisely its tree and that material
with cost `7*n+3`. Together with soundness this proves the exact suffix iff,
round trips and code injectivity, without assuming a parsing oracle.

### Uniform work, including malformed input

Structural frame induction proves two amortized resume inequalities:

```
done result at cost c: c <= 2*frames.length+1
next frames' at cost c: c+2*frames'.length <= 2*frames.length+2.
```

The input-list induction uses these inequalities to obtain
`parseTreeLoop raw frames` work `<=5*raw.length+2*frames.length+2`.
The N branch adds2 and one frame; a continued E branch spends its resume cost
against the decreased/replaced frame potential. A completed E branch stops and
retains the arbitrary suffix. Empty initial frames give `<=5*raw.length+2`.

Keep the previously fixed malformed cases: `[N]` fails at4, `[N,E]` fails at7,
and `[E,rotR]` returns nil with unchanged foreign suffix at3. Reserve all expected
values before coding. If an actual helper design changes these costs, account
for its executed events and update the derivation explicitly, never weaken the
full semantic or polynomial requirement to accommodate a proof failure.

The InputParser source now binds actual tree/separator/tree/separator/bit
results and checks the actual final suffix for EOF. Its complete-input recognition,
roundtrip, exact `7*ns+7*nt+3*b+15` work and universal raw bound are described above;
failures stop at the failed component. Retain compilation, exact-candidate audit
and both independent review outcomes with the matching delivered candidate.

## Retained verifier protocol and independent cases

The following specification and literal expectations were fixed before checker
implementation. Their original mathematical content remains here alongside the
new source owners. The predecessor, execution and linear-parser cases retain
their earlier acceptance scope; parser/stream/witness/verifier source and cases
have separate matching validation and review evidence. The coefficients below
record the prepared derivation realized by the current source contracts, not an
independent build, audit, review or receiving-acceptance receipt.

### 3. Implemented streaming protocol and complete public conclusions

The retained protocol for `checkStreamRun bs current target certificate` is:

1. Charge its entry. Empty certificate calls actual `eqTreeRun`.
2. On nonempty certificate, first execute `decFixedRun bs`; zero returns false
   without parsing a move.
3. Parse exactly one move. Failure returns false. On success apply that move to
   the **current returned tree**; failure returns false.
4. Recurse using the returned predecessor bits, returned tree, and returned
   unconsumed certificate suffix. No equality check is run before the final EOF.

This intentionally specifies failure order. Do not use a list fold that still
traverses its suffix after an Option accumulator has failed. No full certificate
parse occurs before this streaming execution. A pure complete-certificate
decoder may be a separate useful client, but must not replace the actual stream.

The exact semantic contract is:

```text
(checkStreamRun bs s t cert).1 = true ↔
  ∃ moves, cert=certCode moves ∧ applyMoves? moves s=some t ∧ moves.length≤V bs.
```

The source derives this contract from decrement arithmetic and partial execution,
retaining fixed width after every success. `verifyRun input cert` charges its
wrapper entry, executes the input parser, returns false on failure, and otherwise
calls this stream. The original intended public theorem shapes below are now
represented by `verifyRun_accept_iff`, `verifyRun_sound`,
`verifyRun_complete_small` and `verifyRun_work_all`:

```text
accept_iff:
  (verifyRun input cert).1=true ↔
  ∃ s t bs moves, input=inputCode s t bs ∧ cert=certCode moves ∧
    applyMoves? moves s=some t ∧ moves.length≤V bs

sound: (verifyRun input cert).1=true → Yes input
complete_small: Yes input → ∃ cert, cert.length≤2*input.length^2 ∧
  (verifyRun input cert).1=true

work_all: (verifyRun input cert).2 ≤ 32*(input.length+cert.length+1)^2
```

These formulas preserve the independently specified claim shapes; their current
Lean owners are named above. They are not acceptance receipts. Their pointwise
scope includes malformed and overlong input/certificate words. The prepared
coefficient route, rather than a whole-bound premise, was: with decoded source size n,
bit width b and certificate length W, at most W nonempty stream attempts occur.
Their successful parsings consume disjoint prefixes; total move-parser work is
at most `4W+2`. Decrement work per attempt is at most `3b+2`, move work at most
`3n+3`, stream entries at most `W+1`, and terminal equality/false at most `3n+2`.
Thus the deliberately slack stream target

`work ≤ (3b+3n+12)*W + 3n+6`

follows from actual component recurrences and node preservation after successful
prefixes. Valid input gives n,b≤M. Add the input parser and verifier entry to
obtain at most `6MW+12W+23M+27`; invalid input rejects within the input-parser
envelope. Writing `z=M+W`, use `6MW≤3z²` and `12W+23M≤23z` to obtain the stated
`32(z+1)²`. Recalculate if helper implementation adds charged events; preserve
the universal polynomial requirement even if a larger coefficient is needed.

For the witness bound choose the **attained minimum** from `Shape.distance_spec`.
It is at most k and at most `2n-2`. Every successful move has path length+2≤n,
so `|certCode moves|≤n*(2n-2)≤2n²≤2M²`. Empty/singleton shapes use the empty
trace. Neither this witness choice nor `V`, distance, n, M or W is computed by
the verifier. The inequality is a theorem about its explicitly represented data.

### 4. Independent literal cases fixed before coding

Let `U=node () E E`, `L2=node () U E`, `R2=node () E U`,
`L3=node () L2 E`, `B3=node () U U`, and `R3=node () E R2`.
Root moves encode `[rotR,endMove]` or `[rotL,endMove]`; right-at-left encodes
`[rotR,pathL,endMove]`. Costs in the checker table concern `checkStreamRun`,
excluding the separately charged input parser/wrapper.

| Fixed-width input | Expected Option | Exact cost |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `[]` | none | 2 |
| `[1]` | some `[0]` (not `[]`) | 3 |
| `[0,1]` | some `[1,0]` | 6 |
| `[0,0,1]` | some `[1,1,0]` | 9 |
| `[1,0,0]` | some `[0,0,0]` | 3 |
| `[0,0,0]` | none | 8 |

| Structural/parser case | Expected result and observation |
| --- | --- |
| Tree codes | `E:[E]`; `U:[N,E,E]`; `L2:[N,N,E,E,E]`; `R2:[N,E,N,E,E]`. |
| Tree prefix `[E,rotR]` | some `(E,[rotR])`, cost 3; the foreign suffix is untouched. |
| Tree `[N]`; `[N,E]` | none, costs 4 and 7. No fabricated missing child. |
| Move `[rotR,endMove]`; `[rotR,pathL,endMove]` | Root/right-at-left, costs 4 and 7. |
| Move `[rotR]`; `[rotR,pathL]`; `[endMove]` | none, costs 4, 6, 2. |
| Bits `[endInput]`; `[bit0,bit0,endInput]`; `[bit0,bit0]` | some empty / some two zero bits / none; costs 2/8/6. |
| Equality `E,E`; `U,U`; `L2,L2`; `L2,R2` | true/true/true/false, costs 2/5/8/4. Last case skips both right subtrees after the left mismatch. |
| Root right on L2; root left on L2 | some R2 / none, positioned costs 5/3. |
| Right-at-left on B3 | none, positioned cost 5; root right rotation on the reached U is illegal. |
| Nonempty path at E | none, cost 2, independent of remaining path length. |

| Source → target; bits; certificate | Expected stream result and exact cost |
| --- | --- |
| E→E; `[]`; empty | true, 3 |
| U→U; `[]`; empty | true, 6 |
| L2→R2; `[]`; empty | false, 5 |
| L2→R2; `[]`; any nonempty word | false, 4; neither parser nor move/equality executes |
| L2→R2; `[1]`; root right | true, 22 |
| L2→R2; `[1]`; root left | false, 12; illegal rotation stops before equality |
| L2→L2; `[1]`; right then left | false, 19; second zero-fuel failure skips parsing that move |
| L2→L2; `[0,1]`; right then left | true, 38; a legal non-shortest witness is allowed |
| L2→R2; `[0,0,1]`; root right | true, 28; longer borrow, no unary expansion |
| L3→R3; `[0,1]`; root right then right-at-left | false, 33; second move was legal initially but is illegal in the reached B3 |
| L3→B3; `[1]`; root right | true, 25 |
| L3→B3; `[1]`; normalization connection route | false, 19; actual route is right/right/left at root, length 3, while distance is 1 |
| E→U; `[]`; empty | false, 3; unequal sizes need no explicit size pass |

The last stale-path and short-witness cases connect respectively to
`RotationDistanceExample.stale_position_fails` and `initially_legal_moves.1`.
For the latter, `rightPositions L3=[[],[]]` and `rightPositions B3=[[]]`, so
`connectionMoves L3 B3` has exactly the displayed three moves. One actual root
move and distinct endpoints establish distance one. This fills the maintained
paper's previously missing concrete normalization-route separator.

Independent full-wrapper calibration: `verifyRun (inputCode E E []) []` is expected true
with cost `1+15+3=19`. The one-step L2→R2 instance with `[1]` has input length
14, parser cost 46, stream cost 22, hence total 69. Input trailing any tag after
endInput rejects. Reserved tags, repeated separators, an early endMove, missing
tree branches, and a path with arbitrarily many branch tags before its delimiter
must all satisfy `work_all`. Appending any suffix after the stale-path failure
changes neither its Boolean nor stream cost; no suffix parse occurs. With
threshold `[1]`, appending a second move of arbitrary path length after the
first successful move also rejects before parsing that second move.

### Failure order, retained width and reached state

Let `RR`, `RL` and `RAL` denote the existing `rootRight`, `rootLeft` and
`rightAtLeft` fixtures, with `R3` the right three-node chain. The expected work
comes from the complete state equations above, not a post hoc adjustment to a
checker result.

| Independent specialization | Expected stream result and work | Distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arbitrary `bs`, EOF, `E` to `E` | true, `3` | EOF never decrements or normalizes fuel. |
| Arbitrary `bs`, EOF, `E` to any nonempty target | false, `3` | Target subtrees are unvisited after constructor mismatch. |
| All-zero width `b`, arbitrary trees and nonempty raw certificate | false, `2*b+4` | Zero fuel precedes parsing and equality, even when initial endpoints agree. |
| `true :: higher`, any reserved first move tag 11–15 and arbitrary tail | false, `7` | The foreign tag stops parsing before the tail, independently of both trees and higher bits. |
| `L2` to `L2`, `[true]`, `[RR]` | false, `18 = 13+5` | Equal initial endpoints do not authorize early acceptance; final EOF compares the reached `R2`. |
| `L2` to `R2`, `[true]` or `[true,false,false]`, `[RR]` | true, `22` | High-zero width need not affect a successful EOF run. |
| `true :: replicate r false`, `L2`, one `RR` then arbitrary nonempty raw suffix and arbitrary target | false, `2*r+19` | The next attempt reads retained zero width but no next-move symbol; numeric threshold alone does not determine work. |
| `replicate r false ++ true :: higher`, `L2` to `R2`, `[RR]` | true, `3*r+22` | Borrow length determines work; the untouched higher suffix may have any magnitude. |
| `[false,true]`, `L3`, `[RR,RAL]` then arbitrary raw suffix and arbitrary target | false, `33` | The second move is illegal on reached `B3`; neither target nor suffix is inspected. |
| `[false,true]`, `L3` to `R3`, `[RR,RR]` | true, `41 = 16+13+12` | A matching positive two-step case exercises the actual reached tree. |
| `[true,true]`, `L3` to `B3`, `[RR,RR,RL]` | true, `54 = 13+16+13+12` | The normalization route is allowed when its own length fits, although it is not a minimum. |

The stale-path case connects to `RotationDistanceExample.stale_position_fails`
and `initially_legal_moves`; the positive two-step case connects to

### Malformed paths and the traversal boundary

With `true :: higher`, a lone rotation direction without its delimiter rejects
at `9`, and one valid path branch without the delimiter rejects at `11`.
A direction followed by a reserved/nonpath symbol has the same `9` cost,
independently of the unvisited suffix; after one valid branch the cost is `11`.
More generally, a direction and `d` valid branch tags with no terminator reject
at `2*d+9`, without executing a move or final equality.

For `E` as source, a fully delimited nonempty position of length `d` followed by
arbitrary material rejects at `3*d+11`. The parser first reads and reconstructs
the complete path at `3*d+4`; positioned execution then fails at the missing
source root at `2`, and the suffix after the delimiter is unvisited. Only the
execution component is independent of path length. These malformed families
must specialize the same universal raw-word work theorem, not a valid-input
restriction.

### General clients and full wrapper calibration

The connected clients consume `checkStreamRun_iff` in both directions: actual
acceptance supplies the literal certificate code, legal trace and threshold
bound; a successful bounded trace supplies actual acceptance. Equal numeric
values of two bit words therefore imply equal stream Booleans for every raw
certificate, while their observations may differ. Unequal node counts force
rejection through `applyMoves?_numNodes`; syntax alone does not enforce that
condition. Actual emitter clients additionally use `emitCertificateRun_value`
and `emitInputRun_value`, with `verifyRun_emit_trace` providing the complete
composition.

An actual successful predecessor and positioned rotation give the one-move
acceptance calibration

`work = decrement_work + 6*position.length + 3*source.numNodes + 13`.

It follows from `checkStreamRun_step`, `parseMoveRun_code`,
`applyMoveRun_cost_of_some`, node preservation and `eqTreeRun_self_cost`.
The retained root-right two-node case establishes its hypotheses, so this
contract has a concrete nonvacuous instance.

The wrapper adds one entry to input-parser plus stream work on success, and two
to input-parser work on failure. The independent full-word expectations are:

| Input and certificate | Expected complete result and work |
| --- | --- |
| `inputCode E E []`, empty certificate | true, `19 = 15+3+1` |
| `inputCode L2 R2 [true]`, `[RR]` | true, `69 = 46+22+1` |
| Same one-step word with `[true,false,false]` | true, `75 = 52+22+1` |
| `inputCode E U []`, empty certificate | false, `26 = 22+3+1` |
| Empty raw input, arbitrary certificate | false, `6 = 4+2` |
| `inputCode E E [] ++ tag :: tail`, arbitrary certificate | false, `17 = 15+2` |

In general, trailing input rejects at
`7*source.numNodes+7*target.numNodes+3*bs.length+17`, independently of the
unvisited input tail and the entire certificate. This differs from trailing
certificate material: after input parsing succeeds, every further nonempty
certificate suffix is subject to the required decrement-before-parse protocol.
Retain arbitrary-word clients for `verifyRun_work_all` and the small-witness
contract alongside these exact cases. Compilation, exhaustive audit, independent
review and receiving acceptance remain facts about their matching delivered

## Independently fixed codec and binary-wrapper cases

These expectations were fixed from the finite table, recurrence and tariff
before the codec and wrapper implementation. They belong with
[RotationCertificateBinary](../../Examples/RotationCertificateBinary.lean),
whose expanded-candidate validation remains separate. Every four-bit value,
including tags 11 through 15, is a successful codec case. Syntax rejection is
exercised by composing its actual decoded result with the existing parsers.

### Fixed width, endian order and arbitrary suffixes

Each table block above has a tag roundtrip. In particular `1000` decodes to
one, `0100` to two, and `0001` to eight: these distinguish bit order from
numeric display order. Word block order also stays exact: `[0,1]` emits
`0000 1000`, whereas `[1,0]` emits `1000 0000`. Both words cost thirteen to
pack and ten to unpack. Packing every tag 0 through 15 in order produces
64 bits at cost 97 and unpacks at cost 66.

| Operation | Exact expected result/work |
| --- | --- |
| `packWordRun [] suffix` | the arbitrary unchanged suffix, work 1 |
| `packTagRun tag suffix` | its four table bits followed by the arbitrary unchanged suffix, work 5 |
| `packWordRun [tag] suffix` | the same prefix and suffix, work 7 |
| Unpack empty bits | `some []`, work 2 |
| Unpack any one, two or three bits | `none`, work 2 |
| Unpack any complete single block | its one tag, work 6 |
| Unpack any two complete blocks | their two tags in order, work 10 |
| An encoded `q`-tag prefix followed by one to three bits | `none`, work `2*q+2` |
| Actual pack then unpack with empty suffix | the original word, work `10*q+3` |

`[]`, `0000` and `0000 0000` all have numeric `BinaryCounter.value = 0`, but
unpack to different words at costs two, six and ten. Similarly `1000` and
`1000 0000` have equal numeric value one but preserve words `[1]` and `[1,0]`.
No numeric normalization can replace this fixed-width representation.
The arbitrary-suffix theorem includes a partial suffix: the packer preserves
it, and the complete decoder rejects it with the exact failed-return recurrence.

The pair `1111` and `1111 0` separates successful tag decoding from suffix
failure. The first returns tag15 at cost six; the second fails at cost four.
An eager-head variant that decodes tag15 before discovering the final partial
block would add an extra dispatch. These costs record the actual tail-first
recurrence, not monotonicity in raw length or an untouched-tail claim.

### Binary wrapper branches and the accepted rotation

Let `I0` be the 20-bit encoding of `inputCode E E []`. Let `I1` be the 56-bit
encoding of the two-node left-to-right rotation with threshold `[true]`:

```text
input tags: [1,1,0,0,0,2,1,0,1,0,0,2,4,5]
input bits: 1000 1000 0000 0000 0000 0100 1000 0000 1000 0000 0000 0100 0010 1010
cert tags:  [7,10]
cert bits:  1110 0101
```

Write `C1` for those eight certificate bits and let `residual` be any bit list
of positive length below four. The following expectations use the exact
four wrapper branches, not successful-code assumptions on arbitrary inputs.

| Input bits and certificate bits | Expected result/work | Reached costs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `I0`, empty certificate | true, 43 | `22+15+2+3+1` |
| `I1`, `C1` | true, 137 | `58+46+10+22+1` |
| `residual`, arbitrary certificate | false, 4 | decoder 2, entry/false 2 |
| Empty input bits, arbitrary certificate | false, 8 | decoder 2, parser 4, entry/false 2 |
| Encoded singleton reserved input tag, arbitrary certificate | false, 12 | decoder 6, parser 4, entry/false 2 |
| `I0`, `residual` | false, 41 | `22+15+2+2`; no stream |
| `I1`, `residual` | false, 108 | `58+46+2+2`; no stream |
| `I1`, `C1 ++ residual` | false, 112 | `58+46+6+2`; no first rotation |

For a reserved certificate singleton after `I1`, complete decoding succeeds
at six, the actual stream rejects at seven, and the wrapper rejects at
`58+46+6+7+1 = 118`. The reserved-symbol rejection belongs to reached move
syntax after actual fuel decrement. The codec itself must return the symbol.

The following parameterized clients retain arbitrary unvisited certificate
inputs or arbitrary full-block prefixes as appropriate:

- An encoded `q`-tag input prefix followed by `residual` rejects at `2*q+4`
  independently of the entire certificate. No input syntax is parsed.
- A valid input word of length `M` and actual parser cost `P`, with an encoded
  `q`-tag certificate prefix followed by `residual`, rejects at `4*M+P+2*q+6`.
  This is `2*q+41` for `I0` and `2*q+108` for `I1`.
- With `I0`, a completely encoded nonempty `N`-tag certificate rejects at
  `4*N+44`. The stream has zero fuel and costs four, but the complete decoder
  still costs `4*N+2`. Appending `residual` changes rejection work to
  `2*N+41`, before any stream call. This distinguishes untouched token tails
  from visited bit suffixes in the eager adapter.

On the accepted `I1,C1` pair the existing word verifier costs 69, while the two
actual decoders cost 58 and ten, giving 137 with one wrapper entry overall.
The packers alone cost 85 and thirteen. Composing the actual input emitter with
packing costs 112, and composing the actual certificate emitter with packing
costs eighteen. Feeding both actual emitted bit results to the binary verifier
therefore returns true with total work `112+18+137 = 267`. The public value
contracts identify these actual outputs; they do not replace intermediate
executions by an uncharged specification encoder.

The source clients `accepted_raw_bits_have_a_bounded_legal_trace`,
`small_bit_witness_and_its_uniform_work`, and
`arbitrary_incomplete_words_are_within_the_bound` retain complete raw acceptance,
