## Strict binary pair-framing implementation draft

The fixed preimplementation design and independent case plan above are retained
in full. Their first complete attempted source bodies now live in
`Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/BitPairFraming.lean` and
`Examples/RotationCertificateBitPairFraming.lean`. This section maps those bodies
to the fixed mathematics. Compilation, elaborated-contract inspection, axiom
audit, independent review and exact-candidate whole-library acceptance are
separate gates, whose actual outcomes belong to matching delivery evidence.
The existence of the attempted proofs does not establish that they compile or
qualify FDSA-5-93.

### Independent representation and raw domains

`escapeBits` emits `[false, bit]` for each first-coordinate bit; `frame` appends
one true flag and the entire unchanged certificate. `unframe` inspects the flag
position, consumes the following value only after a false flag, and returns all
bits after the first true flag as the second coordinate. Its definition does not
call the machine or the binary verifier.

`unframe_iff` identifies every successful raw input with exactly one
`frame input cert`. `unframe_none_iff` characterizes all failures as either an
escaped first coordinate with no delimiter or that escaped coordinate followed
by one lone false flag. The escape-prefix, arbitrary certificate-suffix, length
and injectivity laws are retained under `unframe_escape_append`, `frame_append`,
`frame_length` and `frame_injective`. This whole-pair representation is not
prefix-free: appending raw bits extends the certificate and is valid framing.

`resultCode` represents rejection by `[]` and a successful pair by
`none :: (input.map some ++ none :: cert.map some)`. The attempted
`resultCode_injective` proof separates both coordinates at a marker that cannot
occur in either mapped payload. The initial marker is part of the specified
format; no claim is made that it is individually necessary for injectivity.
`resultCode_length` records the successful payload length `I + C + 2`.

### Actual finite control and open phase contracts

The explicit `program` has four finite-alphabet stacks and the five labels
`scanPrefix`, `copyCert`, `emitCert`, `emitFirst` and `clearFirst`. Its only register
is `Option Bool`. Every callback reads finite register data; all unbounded work
uses actual gotos. Neither the parser result nor a list length is supplied to a
callback. `initList_eq` and `haltList_eq` expose the complete initialized and
reset terminal configurations.

The named `*_step_*` equations retain arbitrary incoming registers and all
untouched stacks. `emitFirst_iterate`, `clearFirst_iterate`, `emitCert_iterate`,
`copyCert_iterate` and `scanPrefix_iterate` connect those actual steps to full
halt configurations. Their arbitrary reverse accumulators and output suffixes
are part of the contracts. The scan theorem requires an initially empty
certificate-reverse stack; the actual failure path clears only firstReverse.
It preserves old output. The example owner includes a concrete nonempty
certificate-reverse counterexample to dropping that hypothesis.

`runSteps` is a proof-side recurrence and is absent from program callbacks.
`machine_run` targets `some (haltList machine (resultCode (unframe raw)))` for every
raw input. `runSteps_frame` gives `2*I + 2*C + 4`; the two malformed-prefix theorems
give `2*q + 2`; `runSteps_le` gives `2*N + 2` universally. These counts include
copying, reversal, EOF observations, marker pushes, cleanup, reset and halt.
`outputsInTimeExact`, `outputsInTime` and the constructed
`computableInPolyTime` carry the actual machine evidence with polynomial `2*X+2`.
The additional step after halt returns outer `none` and is excluded from the
successful terminal-result contract.

### Reached workspace and connected verifier

`stackCells` sums all four actual stack lengths. `credit` assigns one unit to
scanPrefix and emitFirst, two to copyCert and emitCert, and zero to clearFirst
and halt. `step_potential_le` quantifies over arbitrary configurations and
actual successful transitions; `reaches_potential_le` transports the inequality
along actual TM2 reachability. `reachable_stackCells_le` yields `N+1` from the
literal initialization. The example owner supplies the four-transition path
for raw `[true]`, whose two output markers witness the necessary extra cell.
These are reached machine-cell claims, not physical allocation or TM1 bounds.

`verifyFramed` matches the actual `unframe` result and supplies its returned
fields to `(verifyBitsRun input cert).1`; failure returns false. The frame,
all-raw acceptance, legal-trace, soundness and accepted-certificate equivalence
contracts are `verifyFramed_frame`, `verifyFramed_accept_iff`,
`verifyFramed_accept_iff_trace`, `verifyFramed_sound` and
`binaryYes_iff_exists_framed_certificate`. Actual packed emitters feed that
client through `verifyFramed_emit_trace`.

The existing independently defined `BinaryYes` supplies an accepted certificate
with `C <= I^2`. `frame_length_le_square` and `verifyFramed_complete_small` retain
the same certificate and establish framed length at most `(I+1)^2`.
`outputsInTime_small` gives actual framing time at most `2*(I+1)^2+2`;
`reachable_framed_stackCells_le` bounds every reached framing configuration by
`(I+1)^2+1`. The connected complete-small example uses one outer certificate
existential for acceptance, size, a constructed timed record and every reached
configuration. It does not exchange that witness between claims.

### Discriminating connected cases and remaining bridge

The example owner retains the independently fixed EOF, lone false flag,
true-as-value, arbitrary certificate tail, nonpalindromic order and width cases.
It follows the actual four-step rejection/cleanup of `[false, true]`, preserves

rejects the incomplete four-bit certificate with source observation 112.
No one of these observations is substituted for another cost model.

All earlier twelve author Lean owners, the complete prior paper and every fixed

#### Why this component comes next

`Streaming.checkStreamRun` already executes the width-preserving predecessor on
every nonempty decoded certificate suffix, before parsing a move. Its fuel is an
actual little-endian `List Bool`, including redundant high zeros. Two actual
stacks suffice to realize that primitive without first settling a serialization
of arbitrary trees. The open continuation interface then fits the actual stream
branch that needs it, while preserving all represented tree and parser state.

The complete source input parser is a larger next step. In `TreeParser.lean`,
`TreeFrame.needRight left` holds an arbitrary `BinaryTree Unit`; neither that
field nor an arbitrary frame can be put in finite machine control or used as a
finite stack alphabet. A machine parser must first choose and maintain a finite
serialization of completed subtrees and pending frames, account for their
transfer/reversal, and align the result with the representations later used by
rotations and equality. The predecessor avoids making that consequential choice
prematurely and directly removes one compulsory verifier transition.

This choice follows the repository's explicit-tail and composition direction:
`docs/agents/architectural-quality.md`, `docs/agents/formal-development.md`,
`.agents/skills/example-driven-development/SKILL.md`, and ADRs0001,0006,0010.
Protected arbitrary stacks and caller state are retained in the theorem, rather
than recovered from a closed example. Expected cases and a post-handoff
counterexample are fixed independently of implementation.

#### Existing source and pinned target interfaces

The relevant existing owner is
`Applications/Resources/BinaryCounter/FixedWidth.lean`, namespace
`Resources.BinaryCounter`:

```lean
decFixedRun : Bits → Measured (Option Bits) Nat
```

It executes on the supplied bit list, never computes `value`, and preserves the
untouched higher suffix at the first true bit. Public contracts to reuse are:

* `decFixedRun_nil`, `decFixedRun_true`, `decFixedRun_false`;
* `decFixedRun_none_iff`, `decFixedRun_exists_iff`;
* `decFixedRun_some_spec`, `decFixedRun_some_length`,
  `decFixedRun_some_value`;
* `decFixedRun_cost_le`;
* `decFixedRun_replicate_false width`, with complete result
  `(none, 2 * width + 2)`;
* `decFixedRun_first_true zeros tail`, with complete result

`Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/Streaming.lean` exposes the actual
`checkStreamRun`, `checkStreamRun_nil`, `checkStreamRun_cons`,
`checkStreamRun_no_fuel`, `checkStreamRun_replicate_false`,
`checkStreamRun_parse_failure`, `checkStreamRun_move_failure`,
`checkStreamRun_step`, `checkStreamRun_iff` and `checkStreamRun_cost_le`.
Its order is EOF equality; otherwise actual binary decrement; then actual move
parse; then actual execution; then recurse on the returned bits, tree and suffix.

The target is the pinned Mathlib API in
`Mathlib/Computability/TuringMachine/StackTuringMachine.lean`:

```lean

Turing.TM2.Cfg Γ Λ σ
Turing.TM2.stepAux
```

`Stmt` has `push`, `peek`, `pop`, `load`, `branch`, `goto`, `halt`.
`peek` passes an actual stack's `head?` to a callback without changing the stack;

with that present label. One `TM2.step` executes one fixed finite statement body.
Our blocks contain at most six primitive statement constructors on a selected
branch. All unbounded repetition crosses an actual `goto` boundary.

The target state-transition API is
`Mathlib/Computability/StateTransition.lean`:

```lean

StateTransition.EvalsToInTime.trans
```

The record is Type-valued: it contains an actual `steps` and an actual iterate
equality, together with `steps_le_m`. Construct such evidence with `def`, or prove
the equality first and package it in a `def`. Its `.trans` returns the sum of
the second and first time bounds. This component's finish is a present caller
configuration; it is not `none` and it is not a halted `haltList`.

`Turing.FinTM2` and `TM2ComputableInPolyTime` remain useful for the eventual
complete machine. `FinTM2` explicitly bundles finite stack indices, labels and

Here all stack alphabets are explicitly finite. An open component does not

because it neither controls the caller's time nor promises its final output.
The actual `TM2.step` prefix evidence is the compositional result needed now.

#### Independent predecessor meaning

Write `F^k` for `List.replicate k false` and `T^k` for
`List.replicate k true`. These are mathematical notation in this note, not
instructions supplied to the machine.

Use a finite result tag:

```lean
inductive Result
  | positive
  | zero
```

An independent relational specification `PredSpec original result final` has
exactly these two families:

```text
PredSpec (F^k ++ true :: tail) positive (T^k ++ false :: tail)
PredSpec (F^b)                zero     (F^b)
```

This specification retains the original all-zero word on failure. It distinguishes
zero-width from every positive width, retains all redundant high zeros, and
changes only the visited low prefix on success. Every bit word belongs to one
family: scan leading false bits until the first true, or the end. The families
are disjoint and determine a unique result and final word.

For convenient theorem endpoints, a proof-side function `predSpec` computes that
independent result without using `decFixedRun`:

```lean
predSpec [] = (.zero, [])
predSpec (true :: tail) = (.positive, false :: tail)
predSpec (false :: tail) =
  match predSpec tail with
  | (.positive, ys) => (.positive, true :: ys)
  | (.zero, ys) => (.zero, false :: ys)
```

Prove `predSpec_iff` against `PredSpec`, and then the source correspondence:

```text
(decFixedRun fuel).1 = some ys  ↔ predSpec fuel = (positive, ys)
(decFixedRun fuel).1 = none     ↔ predSpec fuel = (zero, fuel)
```

The output always has the input width. On positive outcome its value is exactly
one less; on zero outcome the value is zero and the supplied list is unchanged.
The numerical `value` appears only in semantic theorems. `predSpec`, `PredSpec`,
all arithmetic and all list lengths are absent from machine callbacks.

The restoring failure behavior is intentional. `decFixedRun` has no returned
word on `none`, so a destructively cleared zero stack would suffice for an
isolated Boolean rejection. Returning the original word with empty auxiliary
stack supplies a stronger composable interface and makes both paths conserve
represented cells. Its required cleanup is actual execution, charged below.

#### Generic finite machine interface

Fix the following before quantifying over input lists or represented state:

* a finite protected stack index type `K`, with `DecidableEq K`;
* a family `Γ : K → Type`, with `Fintype (Γ k)` for every `k`;
* a finite type `Λ` of additional caller labels;
* a finite type `R` of caller register states;
* an arbitrary caller body for each external label in the common statement
  language.

Neither `R` nor `Γ k` may be instantiated with an unbounded tree, word, natural
counter or continuation closure that hides such data. Unbounded represented
values reside in actual stack lists over finite alphabets. Finite caller state
is carried unchanged and never inspected by the owned blocks.

The proposed public types and aliases are:

```lean
inductive LocalStack | fuel | borrowed
abbrev StackId (K : Type) := LocalStack ⊕ K

alphabet Γ (Sum.inl .fuel) = Bool
alphabet Γ (Sum.inl .borrowed) = Unit
alphabet Γ (Sum.inr k) = Γ k

inductive Phase | borrow | restoreTrue | restoreFalse
abbrev External (Λ : Type) := Result ⊕ Λ
abbrev Label (Λ : Type) := Phase ⊕ External Λ
abbrev Registers (R : Type) := Option Bool × R

abbrev Statement Γ Λ R :=
  Turing.TM2.Stmt (alphabet Γ) (Label Λ) (Registers R)
abbrev Cfg Γ Λ R :=
  Turing.TM2.Cfg (alphabet Γ) (Label Λ) (Registers R)
```

All these alphabets, label types and control states have explicit finite
instances induced by the parameters. The two `Result` labels are distinct,
independently of any caller label choice, and external labels are disjoint from
the three internal phases. In particular, an accidental caller exit equal to
`borrow` is not expressible.

Provide ergonomic constructors `phaseLabel`, `resultLabel`, `callerLabel` for
the three corresponding injections. `cfg` exposes every actual stack:

```lean
cfg (label : Option (Label Λ)) (regs : Registers R)
    (fuel : Bits) (borrowed : List Unit)
    (protected : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) : Cfg Γ Λ R
```

The complete actual program is:

```text
program caller (inl phase) = block phase
program caller (inr label) = caller label
step caller = Turing.TM2.step (program caller)
next caller state = state.bind (step caller)
```

`caller : External Λ → Statement Γ Λ R` is fixed once, but no behavior, time,
termination, output or preservation assumption is made about its bodies.
The owned block definitions do not call those host functions; they emit the
corresponding external label. The actual prefix proof stops at that label.

The constructor interface also covers an independently presented ambient
program. Expose `program_eq_of_agrees`: if `ambient` has exactly `block phase`
at every owned `phaseLabel phase`, then

```text
ambient = program (fun external => ambient (Sum.inr external)).
```

Function extensionality over the disjoint sum proves this reconstruction. Thus
the open theorems apply to arbitrary ambient programs with explicit owned-body
agreement, not merely clients written syntactically using this constructor.
No condition on external bodies is added. Fix the ambient program before
quantifying arbitrary raw data and caller stores.

If convenient, a finite-machine bundle may package this same program with chosen
entry and initial finite state. Such packaging is not needed for the open
contracts and must not introduce a special halting wrapper as their sole client.

#### Actual predecessor statement bodies

The local register contains only an optional Boolean. `storeBit` overwrites it
with the actual popped bit and retains the second, caller-state projection.
`storeBorrowed` maps `none` to `none`, and `some ()` to `some false`, retaining
caller state. It records presence, never a count. `reset r = (none, r.2)`.
`jump label = .load reset (.goto (fun _ => label))`.

The following statement skeleton is fixed; constructor/type spelling may be
made idiomatic during elaboration without changing its transitions:

```text
borrow:
  pop fuel storeBit
  branch local.isSome
    (branch local.getD(false)
       (push fuel false; jump restoreTrue)
       (push borrowed (); jump borrow))
    (jump restoreFalse)

restoreTrue:
  pop borrowed storeBorrowed
  branch local.isSome
    (push fuel true; jump restoreTrue)
    (jump positive)

restoreFalse:
  pop borrowed storeBorrowed
  branch local.isSome
    (push fuel false; jump restoreFalse)
    (jump zero)
```

Here the semicolons describe nested `Stmt` constructors, not a host interpreter.
There is no `halt`, whole-list operation, arithmetic counter, numeric fuel
oracle, `List.length`, `value`, `predSpec` or `decFixedRun` in any callback.
The largest selected branch contains one pop, two Boolean branches, one push,
one finite reset and one goto. Restore branches have at most five constructors.

Every entry may have arbitrary stale local register contents. The pop overwrites
them before the branch uses them; every destination boundary has local `none`.
The caller-state projection and protected stacks are preserved even when the
entry configuration is not reachable from a preferred initial state.

#### Exact one-step and phase laws

In the equations below, `r` is any finite register state, `B` is any Unit list,
and `P` is any dependent family of protected stack lists. Each arrow is one
actual `step caller`, and each result is wrapped in outer `some`:

| Entry phase and actual local stacks | Next phase, fuel and borrowed stack |
| --- | --- |
| borrow; `[]`, `B` | restoreFalse; `[]`, `B` |
| borrow; `false :: raw`, `B` | borrow; `raw`, `() :: B` |
| borrow; `true :: tail`, `B` | restoreTrue; `false :: tail`, `B` |
| restoreTrue; `raw`, `() :: B` | restoreTrue; `true :: raw`, `B` |
| restoreTrue; `raw`, `[]` | external positive; `raw`, `[]` |
| restoreFalse; `raw`, `() :: B` | restoreFalse; `false :: raw`, `B` |
| restoreFalse; `raw`, `[]` | external zero; `raw`, `[]` |

All destination registers are `reset r`; all `P` are unchanged. These facts
should be public, with names `borrow_step_nil`, `borrow_step_false`,
`borrow_step_true`, `restoreTrue_step_nil`, `restoreTrue_step_cons`,
`restoreFalse_step_nil`, `restoreFalse_step_cons`.

The reusable cleanup/restore equations are for arbitrary existing fuel, not only
the canonical fuel reached from borrow:

```text
restoreTrue with raw, B
  -- |B| + 1 steps --> positive with T^|B| ++ raw, []

restoreFalse with raw, B
  -- |B| + 1 steps --> zero with F^|B| ++ raw, []
```

They preserve arbitrary `r.2` and `P`, reset the local register and do not execute
the external positive/zero statement. Names: `restoreTrue_iterate`,
`restoreFalse_iterate`.

#### Generalized represented-prefix run

An existing borrowed stack is meaningful: `m = B.length` tokens represent low
zeros already removed from the logical original word. Thus borrow entry
`raw, B` represents

```text
logical original = F^m ++ raw.
```

Every Unit list equals the replicate of its length, so this covers arbitrary
actual Unit lists without an extra element-content hypothesis. It does not say
that a nonempty borrowed stack may be ignored when interpreting the fuel.

Use the proof-side exact count:

```text
runSteps [] = 2
runSteps (true :: tail) = 2
runSteps (false :: raw) = runSteps raw + 2
```

The principal `borrow_iterate` target is:

```text
let result := predSpec (F^B.length ++ raw)
(next caller)^[runSteps raw + B.length]
  (some (cfg (some (phaseLabel borrow)) r raw B P))
 = some (cfg (some (resultLabel result.1))
     (reset r) result.2 [] P).
```

This is an actual iteration equality for the actual program, not a relation to
an assumed evaluator. It is proved by structural induction on `raw`, using the
one-step laws and the generalized restore equations. The false branch pushes
one token and recurs on the shorter actual suffix; the represented logical
word is unchanged. The true branch uses the actual retained higher tail.

The distinguished explicit families, with arbitrary `P`, `r` and initial
borrowed length `m`, are:

| Remaining fuel | Logical original | Handoff fuel and result | Exact additional steps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `F^k ++ true :: tail` | `F^(m+k) ++ true :: tail` | `T^(m+k) ++ false :: tail`, positive | `2*k + m + 2` |
| `F^b` | `F^(m+b)` | `F^(m+b)`, zero | `2*b + m + 2` |

For the top-level predecessor/source correspondence, **the borrowed stack is
empty**. Then success at first true position `k` takes `2*k+2`; all-zero fuel
of supplied width `b` takes `2*b+2`, restoring the entire word. Empty fuel takes
two steps (borrow EOF and empty restore exit). A true head takes two steps
(replace with false and empty restore exit), irrespective of the higher tail.

Public conveniences `borrow_run`, `borrow_run_first_true`,
`borrow_run_replicate_false`, `borrow_run_of_some`, `borrow_run_of_none` expose
the empty-scratch result, explicit families, and existing-source hypotheses.
The `_of_some` endpoint uses exactly the `ys` returned by `decFixedRun`; `_of_none`
keeps exactly the original fuel. No output word is reconstructed from numeric
value in either the machine or the correspondence.

#### Reached-state representation, local space and first exit

For borrow runs begun from represented logical word `original`, the useful
phase invariant is:

* Borrow: `original = F^m ++ fuel`, with `m = borrowed.length`.
* RestoreTrue: for some `m,j,tail`,
  `original = F^(m+j) ++ true :: tail`, `borrowed.length = m`, and
  `fuel = T^j ++ false :: tail`.
* RestoreFalse: for some `m,j`, `original = F^(m+j)`,
  `borrowed.length = m`, and `fuel = F^j`.
* Positive exit: `PredSpec original positive fuel` and borrowed is empty.
* Zero exit: `PredSpec original zero fuel` and borrowed is empty.

All cases also retain the same caller register state and protected stacks.
The local register may be arbitrary only at step0 and is `none` after every
positive number of owned steps. This invariant connects the actual changing
representation to the independent predecessor meaning. It is not imposed as a
premise on the seven one-step laws or the restore helpers, which hold for all
their actual configurations.

Expose the fuel part as a predicate `FuelRepresents original c`, using the five
phase/exit cases above; it is false at unrelated caller labels and at a halt.
Prove `fuelRepresents_step` for every actual owned transition whose starting
configuration satisfies it. A reached-state `borrow_prefix_represents` theorem
then retains this invariant at every actual prefix through the handoff, starting
from `F^B.length ++ raw`. This supplies a represented-state theorem in addition
to the final run equality. Protected-stack and caller-state frame facts are
proved independently and conjoined for clients; they are not smuggled into a
semantic hypothesis about the machine.

For an arbitrary configuration `c`, define actual occupied cells by

```text
stackCells c = |c.fuel| + |c.borrowed| + Σ k : K, |c.protected k|.
```

Every actual transition whose source label is owned conserves this number
exactly. A false borrow moves one cell from fuel to borrowed. A true borrow
replaces one fuel cell by one fuel cell. A restore token moves one cell back to
fuel. Empty tests and exit jumps change no stack cells. Thus no extra cell is
needed even on rejecting all-zero runs. Entry data may already occupy arbitrary
protected workspace; the theorem preserves that exact amount, not a bound that
silently assumes protected stacks are empty.

Define `LocalStep caller c d` to mean that `c` has one of the three owned phase
labels and `step caller c = some d`. Prove actual local-step preservation of
`stackCells`, every protected stack and the caller-state projection, then lift
it along `Relation.ReflTransGen (LocalStep caller)`. A terminal external target
may be included; no outgoing caller step is in this relation.

For exact time-indexed prefixes, define proof-side `phaseSteps`:

```text
phaseSteps borrow raw B = runSteps raw + B.length
phaseSteps restoreTrue raw B = B.length + 1
phaseSteps restoreFalse raw B = B.length + 1.
```

The `phase_prefix` contract for every `n ≤ phaseSteps phase raw B` produces a
present actual reached configuration, preserves all the quantities above, and
states that every `n < phaseSteps phase raw B` still has an owned phase label.
The exact final configuration is the appropriate previously stated handoff.
This proves first exit, not only arrival after a possibly earlier caller visit.

A direct proof uses a proof-only `remainingSteps c`: at an owned phase it is the
corresponding `phaseSteps` on the actual fuel and borrowed stacks; at every
external or halted label it is zero. The seven concrete step laws give

```text
owned c.l → remainingSteps c > 0
LocalStep caller c d → remainingSteps c = remainingSteps d + 1.
```

Conversely, positive `remainingSteps` means an owned label. For the false borrow,
`runSteps (false::raw) + |B|` equals
`runSteps raw + |()::B| + 1`; the true and EOF borrow branches reduce to the
restore count plus one; every restore token or final jump also reduces by one.
Induction on the prefix length therefore yields a present state with remaining
rank `initialRank - n` and a `ReflTransGen LocalStep` path. It proves all shorter
prefixes internal, canonical local registers after the first transition, and
all frame/space facts by the local-step lemmas. This rank never appears in a
statement callback or executable control decision.

Also expose `phase_prefix_caller_independent`: two arbitrary caller-body
functions give identical actual iterates from the same phase configuration
for all `n ≤ phaseSteps phase raw B`. They have the same statement/label types;
their external bodies may disagree everywhere. The proof uses ownership and
first exit, so it does not execute either caller at the endpoint.

**Quantifier boundary:** unrestricted `TM2.Reaches` under an arbitrary caller
continues after handoff. A caller can then push, pop, halt or loop. Therefore
global conservation or protected-stack preservation for all unrestricted
reachable states would be false. Restrict conservation to the local relation
or to actual prefixes through the proved handoff. The connected cases must
include a caller that pushes after the handoff, demonstrating this distinction.

#### Exact time, source comparison and composition data

The proof-side count has these laws:

```text
runSteps (F^k ++ true :: tail) = 2*k + 2
runSteps (F^b) = 2*b + 2
runSteps raw ≤ 2*raw.length + 2.
```

For successful input of width `b`, `2*k+2 ≤ 2*b`; for all-zero input the bound
`2*b+2` is attained. With `m` already borrowed tokens, the uniform remaining
bound is `2*raw.length + m + 2`, at most
`2*(raw.length+m)+2` in the logical represented width.

The exact source cost gives a useful, proved primitive simulation:

```text
runSteps fuel ≤ (decFixedRun fuel).2.
```

On success this compares `2*(k+1)` actual TM2 transitions with the source's
`3*(k+1)` event charge; on failure both are `2*b+2`. This follows from actual
transition proofs and the existing exact source equations. It is not a blanket
identification of source events with machine time, and does not transfer any
other parser/executor tariff without its own proof.

Construct `borrowInTime` and a uniform `borrowInLinearTime` as actual
`StateTransition.EvalsToInTime` data, for arbitrary caller, finite caller state,
protected stacks and all raw fuel. Generalized scratch evidence uses the count
`runSteps raw + B.length`; empty-scratch evidence has bound `2*raw.length+2`.
The exact iteration equality remains public, since a time-bound record alone
need not promise that its stored step count is the intended first-exit count.

If the caller has separately proved actual evidence from the reached handoff
configuration to `finish` in time `T`, combine the component's evidence with it
using `StateTransition.EvalsToInTime.trans`. The resulting bound is
`T + componentBound`, and both records concern the same `step caller` and the
same intermediate configuration. Merely naming a continuation does not assert
its correctness or polynomial time. No presumed caller certificate is bundled
as an unproved `polynomialTime` field.

#### Actual decoded-stream dispatch by specialization

The stream owner does not duplicate the predecessor blocks. Instantiate its
protected stack family with:

```text
Protected K = Unit ⊕ K
protectedAlphabet (inl ()) = Tag          -- Fin16
protectedAlphabet (inr k)  = Γ k.
```

The designated Unit-indexed protected stack is the already decoded certificate
`Word`. Other protected stacks can hold finite encodings of the current tree,
target tree, parser scratch, original input, and any other caller context.

Use additional predecessor caller labels:

```lean
inductive DispatchLabel | inspectCertificate | atEnd
abbrev ExtraLabel Λ := DispatchLabel ⊕ Λ
inductive Exit | atEnd | positive | zero
```

The full label and statement types are the generic predecessor types with
`ExtraLabel Λ` substituted. Define `inspectLabel`, `atEndLabel`,
`positiveLabel`, `zeroLabel`, and `callerLabel` as their disjoint injections.
`positiveLabel` means handoff to actual future move parsing; `zeroLabel` means
handoff to actual future rejection; `atEndLabel` means handoff to actual future
tree equality. Their supplied bodies are not executed by this component.

Let `caller : (Exit ⊕ Λ) → Statement ...` supply these external bodies and any
additional labels. `callerHandler caller` maps predecessor positive/zero to
their supplied bodies, maps the additional `atEnd` label to its supplied body,
delegates other user labels, and gives only `inspectCertificate` this fixed body:

```text
peek certificate storePresence
branch local.isSome
  (jump genericBorrowLabel)
  (jump atEndLabel)
```

`storePresence` maps `none` to local `none`, and `some tag` to local `some false`;
it discards the finite Tag value and preserves caller register state. The branch
sees only presence. The goto reset makes all handoff/boundary local registers
canonical. The entire stream program is definitionally

```text
FixedWidthMachine.program (callerHandler caller).
```

Generic predecessor phase/iterate/frame/time results therefore apply unchanged
to this program. The stream proof adds one peek transition, not a second
implementation or an assumed simulation between unrelated programs.

The stream owner also provides `program_eq_of_agrees` for arbitrary ambient
programs agreeing on the three generic blocks and the fixed inspection block.
Extract its positive, zero, atEnd and user bodies as the caller parameter and
reconstruct the program by cases on the finite disjoint label constructors.
This matches the generic open ownership contract and permits future independently
defined verifier programs to use it by body agreement.

There are four owned labels in this component: inspectCertificate and the
three predecessor phases. `atEnd`, positive, zero and all additional caller
labels are external here. Even when a caller's atEnd body starts another helper,
the dispatch-prefix theorem stops before executing it.

#### Dispatch semantics, exact counts and context

Define an independent proof-side `dispatchSpec fuel cert`:

```text
cert = []:
  (atEnd, fuel)
cert is nonempty:
  map predecessor positive/zero to the corresponding Exit,
  retaining the exact word returned by predSpec fuel.
```

This does not inspect the first tag's value, decode a move, compare trees or read
fuel on the EOF branch. Define a proof-side count `dispatchSteps`:

```text
dispatchSteps fuel [] = 1
dispatchSteps fuel (tag :: raw) = runSteps fuel + 1.
```

The top-level `dispatch_run` starts with empty borrowed scratch and proves the
actual iterate at that count equals `some` of the `dispatchSpec` handoff, with
the complete certificate and all other stacks unchanged, borrowed scratch empty
and local register reset. The exact branch families are:

| Certificate | Supplied fuel | Handoff | Exact TM2 steps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[]` | any fuel | atEnd; fuel unchanged | `1` |
| `tag :: raw` | `F^k ++ true :: tail` | positive; `T^k ++ false :: tail` | `2*k+3` |
| `tag :: raw` | `F^b` | zero; original `F^b` restored | `2*b+3` |

All nonempty-certificate cases quantify over arbitrary tag and entire suffix.
Thus a reserved/malformed move tag and arbitrary long suffix still take only
this local fuel-dependent prefix. No move-parser callback is executed on zero.
The source/target can even be equal: nonempty input still goes through fuel and
eventually parsing; only the empty-certificate branch selects equality.

The one-step `dispatch_step_nil` is stronger than the top-level theorem: EOF
preserves arbitrary existing borrowed scratch as well as arbitrary fuel. This
follows from the actual peek body, which touches neither. The generalized
`dispatch_run_cons` with arbitrary borrowed stack `B` reaches the predecessor
outcome for `F^B.length ++ fuel`, empties `B`, and takes
`1 + runSteps fuel + B.length`. Do not specialize this to `decFixedRun fuel`
without the empty-scratch hypothesis. This is the same represented-prefix
discipline as the generic component.

The uniform top-level bound is

```text
dispatchSteps fuel cert ≤ 2*fuel.length + 3.
```

It is attained by every nonempty certificate with all-zero fuel. EOF remains
exactly1, even at huge supplied width. The source comparison for nonempty
certificate is `dispatchSteps fuel (tag :: raw) ≤ (decFixedRun fuel).2 + 1`.

The actual stream `stackCells` counts fuel, borrowed cells, all certificate tags
and all other protected cells. Inspect only peeks; generic steps conserve all
protected cells. Therefore every owned local transition conserves total cells
and every certificate cell exactly. Prove `dispatch_prefix` and
`dispatch_prefix_caller_independent` through the exact handoff just as for the
generic predecessor, with first-exit labels and arbitrary finite caller state.
Again there is no conservation claim for later arbitrary caller execution.

For the same direct prefix proof, set stream `remainingSteps` at inspection to
`1` when the actual certificate stack is empty, and to
`1 + runSteps fuel + borrowed.length` otherwise. At generic owned phases use
the generic remaining rank, and at external labels use zero. The two actual
peek laws and generic local laws make this rank decrease exactly one on every
owned step. This is proof-only classification of actual configurations, not a
runtime length or presence oracle. The empty/nonempty runtime decision remains
the single actual `peek` and finite branch shown above.

Provide `dispatchInTime` and `dispatchInLinearTime` as actual Type-valued
state-transition evidence. Combining these with separately established caller
execution adds `1` for EOF, or the actual predecessor time plus `1` otherwise.

#### Source-level connection to the existing streaming verifier

The actual machine endpoint and source continuation must agree, rather than
only sharing an informal label name. The stream owner imports the existing
`Streaming.lean` and proves the following connections without editing it.

1. AtEnd: `dispatch_run_nil` retains the supplied fuel and selects atEnd in one
   step. Existing `checkStreamRun_nil` gives
   `checkStreamRun fuel s t [] = CallCount.tick (eqTreeRun s t)`.
2. Zero: for `(decFixedRun fuel).1 = none`, `dispatch_run_of_none` selects zero,
   restores exactly fuel and retains the entire nonempty certificate. Existing
   `checkStreamRun_no_fuel` then gives complete source result
   `(false, (decFixedRun fuel).2 + 2)`, for arbitrary source and target trees.
3. Positive: for `(decFixedRun fuel).1 = some ys`, `dispatch_run_of_some` selects
   positive with exactly `ys`, keeping the complete nonempty certificate.
   A public `checkStreamRun_of_fuel` equation derived from
   `checkStreamRun_cons` exposes the actual continuation using that same `ys`:

```text
let continued :=
  bind (parseMoveRun (tag :: raw)) (fun parsed =>
    match parsed with
    | none => (false, 1)
    | some (move, rest) =>
      bind (applyMoveRun move s) (fun applied =>
        match applied with
        | none => (false, 1)
        | some next => checkStreamRun ys next t rest))
checkStreamRun fuel s t (tag :: raw)
  = (continued.1, 1 + (decFixedRun fuel).2 + continued.2).
```

This is a source equality, proved from the actual source definition and actual
returned fields. It does not execute the parser, rotations, equality or recursive
verifier inside a TM2 callback. The combined `dispatch_zero_stream` and
`dispatch_positive_stream` contracts pair actual machine handoff with these
source equalities. They make the already implemented verifier the client while
leaving its remaining machine phases explicitly open.

For a concrete represented-tree client, instantiate two protected alphabets as
`Tag` and initialize their actual lists with `treeCode s` and `treeCode t`.
The generic frame theorem preserves these lists for arbitrary trees. Tree data
are not stored in finite registers or a supposed finite `BinaryTree` alphabet.
Additional protected scratch and finite caller-state components are arbitrary.

The outer binary layer remains distinct. `BinaryVerifier.verifyBitsRun` executes
input decoding, actual input parsing, then complete certificate-bit decoding,
then `checkStreamRun`. Thus zero decoded fuel does not allow this component to
skip rejection of a partial final four-bit certificate block. For
`inputCode nil nil [false]` (six tags), the existing binary source result is:

* one raw certificate bit: `(false,48)` from certificate decode failure;
* one packed reserved certificate tag: `(false,57)`, reaching zero-fuel stream.

The latter sum is input decode26 + input parse18 + certificate decode6 +
zero-fuel stream6 + wrapper1. The former is26+18+2+2. These values are independent
expected source observations, not machine-transition counts. The no-tail-read
claim here is only about the already decoded certificate stack during this
dispatch/predecessor prefix. Complete eager bit decoding must still be paid by
the eventual composed verifier machine.

#### Proof decomposition and feasibility

1. Establish finite type instances, independent `PredSpec` and `predSpec`
   correspondence. Prove width/value source consequences through existing
   FixedWidth theorems. Fix the executable blocks independently of these proofs.
2. Expose full configurations and dependent-stack extensionality. Prove the
   seven one-step equations directly from `TM2.step`, including reset and all
   untouched stacks. This is the first check that the finite body implements
   the intended primitive rather than a specification oracle.
3. Prove generalized restore laws by induction on the actual Unit list. Prove
   generalized borrow by induction on the actual remaining fuel list. Derive
   exact raw families and source-aligned endpoints.
4. Prove local step frames and cell equality for arbitrary phase configurations.
   Establish the represented-fuel invariant and exact one-step decrease of the
   proof-only remaining rank. Prove first-exit/prefix results by prefix induction
   on that rank, using disjoint sums and positive internal phase durations.
   Derive caller independence, arbitrary-ambient reconstruction and timed data.
5. Instantiate the generic program with certificate among protected stacks.
   Prove the two peek equations, then use the generic results without copying
   predecessor code or proof. Add the stronger arbitrary-borrowed EOF equation,
   generalized nonempty equation, stream time/frame and source bindings.
6. Connect the independent cases to public theorems. Include an actual caller
   continuation step so composition is exercised and the scope counterexample
   remains visible. Obtain normal producer/client compiler results only after
   root implementation release, then the existing full audit/review gates.

The bounded implementation appears feasible with the pinned APIs. The main
proof-engineering work is dependent protected-stack extensionality and keeping
first-exit prefix lemmas general enough for arbitrary caller bodies. Neither
requires a new semantic assumption, a resource cap or a weaker claim. There is
no need for a machine-code compiler or tree representation in this increment.

Open implementation details are limited to Lean argument ordering and whether
prefix facts are packaged as a structure or conjunction. Preserve the full
mathematics either way. Do not replace prefix proofs by unrestricted reachability,
assume caller preservation, make caller exits halt, or weaken arbitrary contexts
to empty stacks to simplify elaboration.

* Positive and zero runs with already borrowed tokens, demonstrating both the
  represented-prefix law and the false empty-scratch specialization.
* Arbitrary stale optional-bit registers and arbitrary finite caller state;
  protected source/target/certificate/scratch stacks remain exact.
* EOF chooses equality in one step even with arbitrary fuel and borrowed
  scratch. A nonempty malformed/reserved tag never selects EOF merely because
  source equals target. Zero fuel hands off before parsing that decoded tag.
* An actual post-handoff caller push changes the total cells, refuting the
  tempting unrestricted global-preservation statement while leaving all valid
  prefix and additive-composition contracts intact.
* Equal numeric fuel with distinct high-zero widths, first-true positions and
  costs; two list encodings with the same mathematical value are not normalized.
* The48/57 outer binary source separator above, keeping eager bit decoding
  distinct from decoded-stream dispatch.

#### Remaining full verifier and mathematical obligations

This increment would remove a real fuel operation and its dispatch from the
machine bridge. It leaves actual finite representations and machine execution
for tree/input parsing, move parsing, tree rotations, equality, streaming control,
all error cleanup, and a complete final output. The existing decoder and framing
machines also need an actual representation-preserving quantitative composition
with those phases; output-code compatibility alone does not execute that glue.

A full proof must sum all phase bounds over actual reachable states, account for
represented workspace and retained source/target data, prove termination and
cleanup on every raw framed input, and reach the intended reset `haltList` before
claiming a complete `TM2ComputableInPolyTime` verifier. The untimed TM2-to-TM1
simulation still supplies no automatic numerical overhead theorem. The final
certificate-language/NP correspondence must be stated and justified against the
actual complete machine and existing independent language/witness bound.

The source-level all-raw cost and quadratic accepted-witness results remain
useful prerequisites, not replacements for those obligations. No row
qualification, acceptance or publication follows from this plan.

The pinned TM2 API was reread in `StackTuringMachine.lean`, `Computable.lean`, and
`StateTransition.lean`. `stepAux` executes a finite statement block to its `goto`
or `halt`; one such label activation is one `TM2.step`. A live caller label is
not a halt. `EvalsToInTime.trans` composes actual runs under the same step function,
with summed bounds. Its premise is not a source cost or an assumed callback time.

#### Independently fixed predecessor semantics

Write `F` for `false`, `T` for `true`, and `F^k` / `T^k` for literal replicated
bit lists. These are list words, not canonical numeric encodings. The source
program `decFixedRun` has these actual equations:

| Fuel | Source returned value | Source work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[]` | `none` | `2` |
| `T :: higher` | `some (F :: higher)` | `3` |
| `F^k ++ T :: higher` | `some (T^k ++ F :: higher)` | `3*(k+1)` |
| `F^b` | `none` | `2*b+2` |

Every successful returned list has the same length as the original and decreases
the independent mathematical `value` by exactly one. Failure is equivalent to
`value fuel = 0`, with no canonicality premise. `[]`, `[F]`, `[F,F]`, and every
longer all-zero word are distinct literal fuel words denoting zero. The machine
must retain those widths. Its failure exit restores the original fuel because
the source returns `none`, not a partially modified fuel word.

For positive fuel the preserved higher suffix is arbitrary, including redundant
high zeros and an arbitrary numeric magnitude. In particular, the initial true
head must stop borrowing without reading that suffix. The canonical `decBits`
operation is not a substitute: `[T]` must become `[F]`, not `[]`.

Every Bool list is a valid fuel representation. Zero is a semantic predecessor
failure, not malformed bit syntax. Every finite `Tag` is valid data on the
certificate stack at this stage, including reserved tags 11--15 and malformed
move prefixes. The dispatcher asks only whether that stack is empty.

#### Actual program conditions and open callers

The proposed local control has `borrow`, `restoreTrue`, and `restoreFalse` phases,
one owned Bool fuel stack, one owned Unit scratch stack, and a finite temporary
`Option Bool` register paired with a finite caller state. A scratch token
represents one low zero already removed from fuel. No source `value`,
whole-list equality, list length, natural counter,
or `decFixedRun` call is allowed inside an executable callback.

The selected core label shape is `Phase ⊕ (Result ⊕ callerLabels)`, with distinct
positive and zero result exits. These exits and caller labels are disjoint from
the owned phases. The dispatch adds inspection/equality through caller labels,
leaving the core bodies and their theorems reusable. All concrete index types,
label types, registers, and stack alphabets must have finite instances. An
additional caller stack family may be arbitrary finite typed stacks; unbounded
contents belong on those stacks, not in the finite register.

Each step uses only a finite `pop`/`peek` result, finite branches, constant pushes,
and a reset before `goto`. Callback parameters must be finite observations, not
closures over the input list. The actual code is fixed before the arbitrary fuel,
certificate, and caller stores are supplied. Avoid the weaker quantifier order
`for every input there exists a machine`.

The open theorem should quantify over an ambient program whose bodies on owned
labels equal the component bodies; caller bodies are arbitrary elsewhere.
The endpoint is the exact configuration at the selected live exit, with temporary
register reset, the caller state preserved, scratch empty where required, actual
returned fuel, and every unrelated stack unchanged. It must not execute the
caller's body as part of the handoff. Only the owned temporary register is reset;
the finite caller state is not silently overwritten with a default.

Stack indices must be disjoint by construction or stated assumptions. Aliasing
fuel, scratch, or certificate would invalidate these contracts. The auxiliary
stack alphabets must be explicitly finite rather than inferred from FinTM2's
input-alphabet-only finiteness field.

#### Independently recalculated phase counts

Conditional on the proposed outline:

1. `borrow` pops fuel. A false bit is transferred to one Unit scratch token and
   returns to `borrow`. A true bit is replaced by false and goes to `restoreTrue`.
   EOF goes to `restoreFalse`.
2. Each nonempty restore step pops one scratch token, pushes the appropriate
   constant bit onto fuel, and stays in that restore phase.
3. An empty-scratch restore step resets the finite register and goes to the
   corresponding live result label.

Thus a first true after `k` low zeros takes `k+1` borrow steps, `k` transfer-back
steps, and one empty-scratch exit: `2*k+2`. All-zero width `b` takes `b` transfers,
one EOF observation, `b` transfers back, and one exit: `2*b+2`.

The exact-time endpoint should be accompanied by an internal-label invariant for
every earlier iteration. This distinguishes a first handoff from a later return
to the same label after arbitrary caller work. With the disjoint sum labels, no
caller statement executes before the stated endpoint.

Let `D fuel` denote this mathematical handoff count, without requiring any runtime
evaluation of `D`. It satisfies `D [] = 2`, `D (T::tail) = 2`, and
`D (F::tail) = D tail + 2`. For every raw fuel word, `D fuel <= 2*fuel.length+2`.
The positive branch is more sharply bounded by `2*fuel.length`. Neither bound
depends on the mathematical fuel value.

##### Literal core cases

| Initial fuel, with empty scratch | Exit and final fuel | TM2 steps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[]` | zero, `[]` | `2` |
| `[F]` | zero, `[F]` | `4` |
| `[F,F]` | zero, `[F,F]` | `6` |
| `[T]` | positive, `[F]` | `2` |
| `[T,F,F]` | positive, `[F,F,F]` | `2` |
| `[F,T]` | positive, `[T,F]` | `4` |
| `[F,F,T]` | positive, `[T,T,F]` | `6` |
| `[F,F,T,F,T,F,F]` | positive, `[T,T,F,F,T,F,F]` | `6` |
| `F^k ++ T::higher`, arbitrary `higher` | positive, `T^k ++ F::higher` | `2*k+2` |
| `F^b`, arbitrary `b` | zero, the same `F^b` | `2*b+2` |

The seven-bit example is numeric 20 to 19 and has a nonpalindromic retained suffix
`[F,T,F,F]`. It distinguishes correct suffix reuse from reversal. `[T]` and
`[T,F,F]` have the same value and the same first successful component time, but
their later zero-fuel calls take 4 and 8 steps respectively. Numeric equality
does not justify normalizing either the representation or its future timing.

##### Explicit successful intermediate run

Use initial `[F,F,T,T,F]`, empty scratch, arbitrary register and arbitrary caller
stores. The untouched high suffix is `[T,F]`; numeric value goes 12 to 11.

| Iteration | Label | Fuel | Scratch length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | borrow | `[F,F,T,T,F]` | `0` |
| `1` | borrow | `[F,T,T,F]` | `1` |
| `2` | borrow | `[T,T,F]` | `2` |
| `3` | restoreTrue | `[F,T,F]` | `2` |
| `4` | restoreTrue | `[T,F,T,F]` | `1` |
| `5` | restoreTrue | `[T,T,F,T,F]` | `0` |
| `6` | positive caller exit | `[T,T,F,T,F]` | `0` |

After every iteration numbered 1 through 6 the temporary register is reset,
the finite caller state and every caller stack equal their initial contents,
and total stack cells are unchanged.

##### Explicit restored failure

For `[F,F]`, the labels/fuel/scratch lengths are successively
`(borrow,[F,F],0)`, `(borrow,[F],1)`, `(borrow,[],2)`,
`(restoreFalse,[],2)`, `(restoreFalse,[F],1)`,
`(restoreFalse,[F,F],0)`, `(zero exit,[F,F],0)`.
The third step detects EOF and the fourth/fifth steps actually rebuild the fuel.
Rejecting immediately from the emptied borrow state would lose width and violate
the in-place failure contract. The zero exit does not itself halt the machine.

#### Generalized state invariants and counterexamples

The strongest useful phase clients quantify arbitrary fuel suffixes, incoming
registers, scratch lengths, and unrelated typed stores under explicit ownership
and represented-prefix conditions.

- Restoring `m` pending tokens in `restoreTrue` puts `T^m` before the current fuel
  and reaches the positive exit in `m+1` steps. `restoreFalse` similarly puts
  `F^m` before current fuel and reaches the zero exit. Both preserve arbitrary
  old fuel suffixes and caller stores.
- At `borrow` with current fuel `raw` and `m` tokens, the logical original fuel
  is `F^m ++ raw`. If `raw = F^k ++ T::higher`, the final fuel is
  `T^(m+k) ++ F::higher`, the exit is positive, and remaining time is `2*k+m+2`.
  If `raw = F^b`, the final fuel is `F^(m+b)`, the exit is zero, and remaining
  time is `2*b+m+2`. The scratch is empty at both endpoints.
- These generalized counts are not `D (F^m ++ raw)`: the first `m` borrow steps
  have already happened. They equal `D raw + m`.
- Empty scratch is required for a top-level theorem about `decFixedRun raw`.
  A concrete counterexample is `borrow` with fuel `[T]` and one token: it reaches
  positive with `[T,F]` in 3 steps, not `[F]` in 2. It correctly represents an
  in-progress decrement of `[F,T]`. With fuel `[]` and one token it restores
  `[F]` and reaches zero in 3 steps, not the empty-fuel endpoint.
- Test EOF, false-head, true-head, and empty/nonempty scratch cases for every
  arbitrary initial `Option Bool` temporary register and finite caller state.
  In particular, stale `some true`
  must not turn fuel EOF into success or empty scratch into another push.
  Every pop/peek must overwrite its finite observation before branching.

The existing higher suffix stays structurally unchanged. A theorem about only
its numeric value would miss dropped high zeros or a reversed unequal suffix.
The generalized scratch invariant must not describe arbitrary scratch as free
workspace without recording the logical low-zero prefix it represents.

#### One actual certificate-presence dispatch

The inspection phase peeks at the actual decoded certificate stack and stores
only whether it is nonempty. On EOF it goes directly to the equality caller;
on a nonempty word it goes to `borrow`. It does not consume a tag, validate a
direction/path, compare trees, or execute a rotation. Its finite callback may
discard the observed Tag value after testing presence; it must not parse a list.

For a top-level call with empty scratch:

| Certificate and fuel | Handoff | Fuel at handoff | TM2 steps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[]`, arbitrary fuel | equality caller | identical fuel | `1` |
| `tag::tail`, `F^b` | zero/reject caller | identical `F^b` | `2*b+3` |
| `tag::tail`, `F^k ++ T::higher` | positive/move-parser caller | `T^k ++ F::higher` | `2*k+3` |

The entire certificate is unchanged in every row. The universal bound is
`2*fuel.length+3`, with the EOF branch independently sharpened to 1. Every
incoming register is allowed. EOF does not touch fuel or scratch: its one-step
equation may retain arbitrary existing scratch, while a full decrement theorem
must still state the empty-scratch or represented-prefix invariant.

Meaningful distinguishing clients include:

- Empty fuel plus empty certificate goes to equality, whereas the same fuel plus
  one arbitrary tag goes to rejection in 3 steps. Equal initial trees do not
  change either control decision.
- Arbitrarily long all-zero fuel plus empty certificate still takes 1 step and
  preserves that exact word. Equality must not be replaced with acceptance.
- Fuel `[T]` and a valid root move word `[rotateRightTag,endMoveTag]` hand off to
  the move parser with `[F]` in 3 steps. The same is true for one reserved tag,
  a lone direction lacking its delimiter, or a malformed path. Those later
  parser outcomes are not decided by this component.
- For `[F]` and any nonempty raw word, all tags and arbitrary tails remain intact
  and rejection handoff takes 5 steps. Reserved heads do not run a parser first.
- The nonempty-certificate pair `[T]` versus `[T,F,F]` takes 3 steps on the first
  successful dispatch. A fresh dispatch of their actual all-zero returned fuels
  takes 5 versus 9 steps. Any real route from a caller label back to inspection
  must charge its transition; relabeling configurations is not free composition.

#### Prefix-only preservation, workspace, and actual timing data

All owned steps transfer cells or inspect emptiness. At a false borrow one fuel
cell becomes one scratch cell; at a true borrow one fuel bit is replaced; restore
transfers a scratch cell back; EOF and certificate peek change no stack cells.
For every component-prefix configuration through and including handoff, the sum
of all stack lengths is exactly its initial value. In particular,
`fuel.length + scratch.length` is constant, and every unrelated stack is equal
to its original content; the finite caller state also remains unchanged.
From empty scratch, the owned workspace is the initial fuel width.
The dispatch certificate itself contributes unchanged length; no
additional marker cell is allocated.

This is a nonvacuous statement about actual intermediate configurations, including
the explicit two-token successful/failure traces above. A final-state-only length
equality would not establish the bound. The fixed finite register is separate
from stack-cell counting; its storage is bounded uniformly by its finite type.

For an ambient arbitrary caller, quantify preservation over iterations
`n <= handoffTime` (and live internal labels for `n < handoffTime`), or over a
precisely internal-only reach relation. Do not quantify unrestricted
`TM2.Reaches ambientProgram start reached`: that relation includes arbitrary
caller steps after handoff. A caller body that pushes one symbol on its own stack
is an immediate counterexample to global stack-cell conservation and to preserved
caller stores. An example should instantiate this caller, establish the precise
handoff endpoint, and then show the extra push on one further actual transition.

Construct Type-valued `StateTransition.EvalsToInTime` records from the actual
iteration proofs, for the same concrete ambient step function and configuration:
core bound `2*fuel.length+2`; dispatch bound `2*fuel.length+3`. This is a uniform
linear component bound, also linear in total represented stack size. The exact
record must target `some exitConfiguration`, not outer `none`.

A meaningful composition client should use `EvalsToInTime.trans` with an actual
one-step caller body on that exact returned configuration. A finite sentinel push
is sufficient to expose the distinction between component time and continuation
time. Any general continuation theorem may assume an actual timed run under the
same `step`, with that assumption explicit; it must not turn an assumed
polynomial-time callback into a proved complete verifier.

No `TM2OutputsInTime`/`TM2ComputableInPolyTime` result for this multi-stack open
component follows merely from those records. Those types require the specified
single input encoding, actual initial configuration, halted output encoding, and
cleanup. This increment deliberately has live handoffs and no such adapter.
In particular, the restored fuel and preserved certificate are not empty
nonoutput stacks in `haltList`.

#### Connected use of the existing verifier

The connection should relate the exact bits returned by the machine, under the
same initial fuel and certificate, to `decFixedRun` and the existing source
branch equations. Do not prove unrelated existential witnesses that may use
different words or a different caller state.

- Positive handoff supplies the same `ys` for the actual machine fuel and
  `(decFixedRun bs).1 = some ys`. Consume `decFixedRun_some_spec` to get equal
  width and `value bs = value ys + 1`.
- Zero handoff with restored `bs` supplies `(decFixedRun bs).1 = none`. For
  arbitrary trees and arbitrary nonempty certificate, consume
  `checkStreamRun_no_fuel` / `checkStreamRun_replicate_false`. The source result
  is false with work `2*b+4` for all-zero width `b`, while the actual dispatched
  component time is `2*b+3`. These are separate quantities.
- EOF handoff connects to `checkStreamRun_nil`, whose continuation is actual
  `eqTreeRun`. The component has not evaluated equality. For example, empty to
  empty at EOF yields source `(true,3)`, while empty to a nonempty tree yields
  `(false,3)`; the same machine dispatch takes 1 step in both.
- Positive handoff on a reserved tag connects to `checkStreamRun_parse_failure`:
  with `T::higher`, the source stream returns `(false,7)` after the actual
  predecessor and parser. The component time is 3, its fuel is `F::higher`, and
  its certificate is still untouched at the parser entry. A lone direction
  instead has source work 9; the dispatch is still the same 3 steps.
- On the actual emitted root-right certificate for `leftTwo` to `rightTwo`,
  fuel `[T]` gives the same 3-step handoff with `[F]`. The existing source stream
  consumes that move and returns `(true,22)`. Using `[T,F,F]` preserves the same
  source acceptance and first handoff time while retaining width three.
  A one-move witness under `F^k ++ T::higher` has stream source work `3*k+22`,
  while its entry-to-parser component time is `2*k+3`.

These examples should use actual measured emitters and public emitter/parser
contracts where helpful. They do not claim an actual compiled parser, rotation,
or equality continuation. Existing standalone framing/decoder machines also have
their own encoded outputs and cleanup conventions; transferring those outputs
into the new owned stacks needs future explicit machine adapters or a combined
program proof, not free host-language projection.

##### Eager binary decoding remains earlier than fuel dispatch

`verifyBitsRun` completely decodes the bit input, parses the input word, then
completely decodes the certificate bits before invoking `checkStreamRun`.
Accordingly the new component preserves a decoded symbol suffix, not an unread
binary suffix. Checking zero fuel before complete certificate bit decoding would
change that operational order.

Use the independently calculated concrete input
`wordBits (inputCode .nil .nil [F])`: six tags, 24 bits. Its input decode costs 26
and its input parse costs 18 in the existing source tariff.

| Raw certificate bits | Existing binary result and source work | Relevant branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one arbitrary bit | `(false,48)` | incomplete certificate block: `26+18+2+2` |
| `wordBits [reservedTag]`, with `11 <= reservedTag.val` | `(false,57)` | successful 6-work certificate decode, then zero-fuel stream: `26+18+6+6+1` |

In the second row only, the decoded nonempty certificate reaches the selected
component: fuel width one, rejected handoff in 5 actual TM2 steps, with that
reserved tag unchanged. The first row never invokes it. An implementation may
not add the source work numbers to component transitions as a machine-clock
claim. Both all-raw source inputs remain within the previously proved universal
source-work bound; that bound does not realize the omitted machine stages.

- The actual one-step EOF dispatch, nonempty positive and zero dispatch, exact

- Actual Type-valued timed records and a nonvacuous timed caller-composition
