#### Recommended representation

Keep a parsed tree as its **existing preorder `treeCode`**, stored head first on
a real finite-alphabet stack. Do not store a `BinaryTree`, list, natural counter,
or source parser in a finite register or transition callback. The mathematical
tree is a ghost value in the representation relation:

```text
RepTree treeStack t  :=  treeStack = treeCode t.
```

The existing prefix uniqueness theorem makes this representation injective.
The future parser need not reconstruct a host-language tree to establish its
correctness. Later rotation/equality components still need actual algorithms
over this representation, with their own bounds; retaining a serialized tree
does not implement those operations for free.

A useful tree-prefix machine can copy the accepted preorder tags and maintain
the number of pending child slots as a stack of `Unit`. This replaces the source
frame stack operationally while retaining an explicit simulation relation to
the actual `parseTreeLoop`/`resumeTreeRun` definitions. No natural slot count is
computed by a callback.

#### Finite owned stacks and register discipline

One possible full input-parser component owns these distinct stacks:

| Stack | Alphabet | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw` | `Tag = Fin 16` | Actual unread input suffix, head first |
| `source` | `Tag` | Completed first tree code |
| `target` | `Tag` | Completed second tree code |
| `fuel` | `Bool` | Actual little-endian threshold bits |
| `treeReverse` | `Tag` | Reversed consumed tree prefix, or transfer scratch |
| `pending` | `Unit` | One token per outstanding child slot |
| `bitsReverse` | `Bool` | Reversed threshold-bit prefix, or transfer scratch |

All unbounded data reside on these stacks or separately indexed caller stacks.
The full parser entry requires the six owned output/scratch stacks other than
`raw` to be empty. Caller stacks and a finite caller state are arbitrary and
preserved. Stack disjointness must be by constructors or explicit hypotheses;
aliasing `raw`, output, or scratch invalidates the argument.

A sufficient fixed temporary register type is a product of `Option Tag`,
`Option Bool`, and `Option Unit`, paired with a finite caller state. These
temporary factors have 17, 3, and 2 values. A smaller choice may suffice, but
there is no reason to introduce unbounded storage. Every alphabet must have its
own finite instance; the narrower input-alphabet field in `FinTM2` does not
establish this automatically.

Callbacks may inspect/replace those finite fields, map a finite bit observation
to `bitZeroTag`/`bitOneTag`, or choose a finite label. They may not close over
the arbitrary input, call `parseTreeRun`, `parseInputRun`, `treeCode`, list
append/reverse/length, `numNodes`, or any unbounded host traversal. Every probe
overwrites its observed field before a branch. Reset only the owned temporary
fields at each goto; preserve the finite caller state.

Use a finite sum of owned phase labels and disjoint caller/live-result labels.
Two copies of the finite tree phases, indexed by source/target mode, avoid an
unbounded continuation or output-stack selector. A fixed finite mode flag
would also be admissible if its preservation/reset contract were explicit.

#### Tree-prefix component: concrete proposed blocks

This local component operates on `raw`, `treeReverse`, `pending`, and one
designated output tree stack. The public entry requires both scratch stacks
empty, while the output may contain an arbitrary old suffix. Its success output
is `treeCode t ++ oldOutput`; failure preserves `oldOutput`.

Each row below is intended to be one finite `TM2.Stmt` block ending at an actual
goto. A block can contain finitely many pops/peeks/pushes. All repeated work uses
gotos. Empty probes, reset, rollback and cleanup are included.

| Phase and observation | Actual finite actions | Next label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `treeInit` | Push one Unit pending slot | `treeScan` |
| `treeScan`, next tag N | Pop N from raw; push N on treeReverse; push one Unit slot | `treeScan` |
| `treeScan`, next tag E | Pop E from raw; push E on treeReverse; pop one pending slot; peek pending | `treeEmit` if empty, otherwise `treeScan` |
| `treeScan`, EOF or any foreign tag | Do not pop raw | `treeUndo` |
| `treeEmit`, treeReverse nonempty | Pop a tag and push it on output | `treeEmit` |
| `treeEmit`, treeReverse empty | Reset temporaries | Live success continuation |
| `treeUndo`, treeReverse nonempty | Pop a tag and push it back onto raw | `treeUndo` |
| `treeUndo`, treeReverse empty | Reset temporaries | `dropPending` |
| `dropPending`, pending nonempty | Pop one Unit | `dropPending` |
| `dropPending`, pending empty | Reset temporaries | Live failure continuation |

At every reachable scan state the pending stack is nonempty. Therefore an E
really closes one current slot. A definition's behavior on an externally
corrupted empty-pending scan state must not be confused with the all-raw-input
entry theorem. An optional defensive branch could reject it, but would change
the finite block details and need its own accounting.

The tree output is produced only after the first complete tree prefix is found.
The `treeUndo` branch restores precisely the consumed prefix, without examining
the unvisited raw suffix. It is not a second parse. Failure therefore returns
the original raw input and old output, with both scratch stacks empty.

#### Relation to the existing source frames

Let `leftSlots frames` be the mathematical number of `needLeft` frames. It is
only a proof-side list count. At a scan boundary relate the machine to ghost
source frames `frames` and a consumed prefix `prefix` by:

```text
originalRaw = prefix ++ currentRaw
prefix = stackPrefix frames
treeReverse = reverse prefix
pending = replicate (1 + leftSlots frames) ()
output = oldOutput
(parseTreeRun originalRaw).value
  = (parseTreeLoop currentRaw frames).value.
```

The last equality records the actual source continuation. It is a logical
invariant, never evaluated by the machine. The source frames may contain
arbitrarily large returned left trees, but they occur only in this relation,
not inside the finite machine's state.

The following helper facts about the existing source resumption are needed:

```text
resumeTreeRun frames t returns done u
  -> leftSlots frames = 0

resumeTreeRun frames t returns next frames'
  -> leftSlots frames = leftSlots frames' + 1.
```

Together with its already proved prefix identities, these explain every branch.
An N adds a `needLeft` source frame and one pending Unit. An E closes the current
slot. If resumption returns `next frames'`, the physical remaining pending length
is `leftSlots frames = 1 + leftSlots frames'`, and the consumed prefix becomes
`stackPrefix frames'`. If resumption returns `done t`, pending becomes empty and
the consumed prefix is exactly `treeCode t`. Thus the machine detects the same
first complete prefix and never scans into the returned suffix.

This is a compressed representation of the actual source continuation, not a
callback invoking resumption as a unit-time primitive. Source resumption may
close several `needRight` frames; its proved prefix/count identities justify why
the finite slot machine can represent the resulting continuation with one slot
pop. The two clocks are deliberately different.

On EOF or a foreign tag, the actual source loop returns none. The physical
rollback and pending cleanup are additional charged machine work; they preserve
the original raw word and do not call the parser on a later suffix.

The count identities, actual one-step equations, generalized emit/undo/cleanup
iteration lemmas, source-state relation, and total exit theorem remain unproved.
They are the precise next mathematical gaps, not assumptions to put in a
polynomial-time field.

#### Conditional tree time and space calculations

For successful code length `L = 2*n+1`, the proposed blocks take:

```text
1 initialization + L scans + L emit transfers + 1 empty-emit exit
  = 2*L+2 = 4*n+4.
```

For failure after `k` accepted N/E tags with `p` pending slots:

```text
1 initialization + k scans + 1 rejection probe
  + k rollback transfers + 1 empty-rollback probe
  + p pending removals + 1 empty-pending exit
  = 2*k+p+4.
```

The represented prefix has `p = 1 + numberOfN(prefix) - numberOfE(prefix)`,
with positive pending count at every scan boundary. In particular `p <= k+1`.
For original input length M this gives failure time at most `3*M+5`, and a
uniform tree-component bound `3*M+5` also covers success.

Independent conditional examples: E followed by any suffix succeeds in 4
transitions; a singleton code succeeds in 8; either two-node code succeeds in
12. Empty input and a leading foreign tag fail in 5; `[N]` fails in 8; `[N,E]`
fails in 9. These are machine counts, distinct from source observations 3,
10,17 and 2,4,7 respectively. They have not been checked against a Lean program.

Transfers conserve `raw + treeReverse + newlyProducedOutput` cells. Pending
never has more than M+1 cells. With arbitrary preserved caller/output storage U,
every configuration through first handoff should therefore have at most
`U + 2*M+1` total stack cells. The malformed word consisting of M N tags reaches
M copied tags and M+1 pending slots before rejection, providing a sharp
nonvacuous represented-space example. Registers contribute only their fixed
finite storage.

The workspace theorem must cover actual intermediate states through the first
handoff, not only the final equality of input lengths. It must not quantify
unrestricted ambient reachability after arbitrary caller code has begun.

#### Whole input parser with rollback on failure

A stronger, convenient future open contract is:

- On source success `some (s,t,bs)`: reach live success with raw empty,
  `source = treeCode s`, `target = treeCode t`, `fuel = bs`, all scratch empty.
- On source failure `none`: reach live failure with the original raw input
  restored and all owned output/scratch stacks empty.
- Both exits reset owned temporaries, preserve finite caller state and every
  unowned stack, and do not execute the continuation body.

Rollback is a design proposal supporting a simple exact failure endpoint, not
a new obligation imposed on the currently selected fuel component. A different
explicit failure representation could work, but all its cleanup/adapters and
quantitative costs would still need proof.

Use the tree component first for source, then check a separator, then use it for
target, then check another separator, then parse bits through endInput, then
check EOF. This follows the existing source parser's syntax and failure order.
Unequal-size trees are legal syntax. High zero bits are retained literally.
Reserved tags remain ordinary finite tags whose reached grammar position rejects
them. Final EOF tests only empty/nonempty, not the value of a trailing tag.

##### Additional actual phase outline

`checkSep1` and `checkSep2` each peek raw and, only for separatorTag, pop it and
goto the next phase. Wrong tag/EOF jumps to the appropriate rollback phase.
These are one block each. They do not scan a suffix.

`bitsScan` consumes one bitZeroTag/bitOneTag per block and pushes the corresponding
Bool onto bitsReverse. At endInput it pops that delimiter and goes to bitsEmit.
A foreign tag or EOF is not popped and goes to bitsUndo. `bitsEmit` transfers
one Bool per block from bitsReverse to fuel, with one empty probe to go to the
final EOF check. This reconstruction occurs before checking final EOF, matching
the source's successful bits result before `finishInputRun`. The final EOF
block goes to success on empty raw and to restoreEnd on nonempty raw.

`bitsUndo` transfers each Bool from bitsReverse onto raw using the actual finite
mapping to its bit tag, then its empty probe goes to restoreSep2. `restoreEnd`
pushes endInput and goes to fuelUndo. `fuelUndo` transfers the forward fuel onto
bitsReverse, then its empty probe goes to bitsUndo. These two reversals restore
the original threshold tag order, including every high zero.

For each complete tree output, rollback uses two transfer loops: output to
treeReverse, then treeReverse to raw. Each loop has one empty probe. There is
no traversal primitive hidden inside a push. Between target rollback and source
rollback, restoreSep1 pushes the already consumed first separator. Before target
rollback when appropriate, restoreSep2 pushes the second separator. Each such
constant restore is one explicit block. The end of source rollback is the live
failure exit. Every listed goto is an actual transition; changing labels in a
mathematical configuration is not free execution.

##### First-failure routing

| Source failure stage | Physical restoration path |
| --- | --- |
| Source tree | Its own treeUndo/dropPending restores original raw, then live failure |
| First separator | Restore source code directly; separator was not consumed |
| Target tree | Its tree failure restores target-start raw; restore first separator, then source |
| Second separator | Restore target code, first separator, then source; second separator was not consumed |
| Bits before endInput | Restore partial bitsReverse, second separator, target, first separator, source |
| EOF after endInput | Restore endInput, fuel via bitsReverse, second separator, target, first separator, source |

The phase label records only this fixed finite stage information. It does not
store the consumed words, lengths, or trees. Parsed material is present on the
actual stacks. A rollback loop manipulates only that material; the unvisited
raw suffix stays as an exact tail throughout restoration.

#### Conditional full-parser step bounds

Let `Ls`, `Lt` be the two actual tree-code lengths, and `b` the number of bit tags
reached. Each tree success costs `2*L+2` as above. Each separator check costs one.
Bit scanning on success costs `b+1`, reversal `b+1`, and final EOF one. There is
no extra uncharged outer entry: full entry is the actual source treeInit block.
The proposed exact successful total is therefore

```text
2*Ls + 2*Lt + 2*b + 9 = 2*M+3,
where M = Ls+Lt+b+3.
```

This gives 13 transitions on the empty-tree/empty-tree/empty-bits input of
length 5, and 31 on the two-node one-bit input of length 14. The source parser's
15 and 46 observations are separate quantities.

The following conditional failure totals include all restoration and empty
probes in the phase outline. A failed tree prefix uses k accepted tags and p
pending slots. A malformed bit prefix uses b accepted bit tags.

| Failure stage | Proposed exact total |
| --- | --- |
| Source tree | `2*k+p+4` |
| First separator | `4*Ls+5` |
| Target tree | `4*Ls+2*k+p+10` |
| Second separator | `4*Ls+4*Lt+11` |
| Bits before delimiter | `4*Ls+4*Lt+2*b+14` |
| Nonempty suffix after endInput | `4*Ls+4*Lt+4*b+18` |

For target failure, M is at least `Ls+1+k` and `p<=k+1`. For second-separator
failure it is at least `Ls+1+Lt`; for bit failure, `Ls+Lt+b+2`; for trailing
material, `Ls+Lt+b+4`. These inequalities give the common linear envelope
`4*M+7` for every raw word and both outcomes under this exact block design.
The conditional constants must be rechecked against the eventual `TM2.step`
definitions. This table is not a substitute for actual iterate equalities.

#### Whole-parser intermediate space and composability

During successful scanning or rollback, input/outputs/reverse stacks transfer
one symbol per represented input symbol. Popped delimiters create a finite debt
of at most three cells, recorded by the phase, and restoration pays back exactly
those cells. Excluding pending, the total owned stack cells should never exceed
M. Pending is at most M+1. Thus the intended prefix workspace bound remains
`2*M+1`, plus arbitrary unchanged caller storage, including a certificate stack.
The all-N malformed input still supplies a sharp intermediate witness.

The proof needs phase-dependent representation predicates recording which
delimiters have been consumed, which stacks contain each exact segment, their
orientations, and how the unvisited raw tail is preserved. Mere final output
length or a bound on ghost trees is insufficient. Copying instead of the stated
pop/push transfers would invalidate the proposed cell accounting.

Quantify over an ambient program agreeing with the owned bodies. Give exact
first-handoff iteration equations, internal owned labels at all earlier
iterations, and preservation/space for iterations through that handoff. An
arbitrary caller may push a cell immediately afterward, so unrestricted
`TM2.Reaches ambientProgram` preservation is false. Timed evidence must be a
Type-valued `StateTransition.EvalsToInTime` construction for the actual ambient
step function, actual initial represented configuration, and `some` live exit
configuration. It should compose by `EvalsToInTime.trans` with real caller steps
at that exact endpoint. A sentinel-push caller is a useful distinguishing case.

Neither such live multi-stack handoff evidence nor the linear counts alone give
`TM2OutputsInTime` or `TM2ComputableInPolyTime` for the complete verifier. Those
require the eventual actual framed single input, a fixed combined machine,
actual output encoding, and final `haltList` cleanup/reset. In particular, a
restored malformed raw word is not an empty nonoutput stack. Final rejection
cleanup must consume it and any remaining certificate without performing an
unauthorized later semantic parse, and charge the corresponding transitions.

#### Required connections and still-open gaps

The existing decoder output is `[]` for failure and `none :: word.map some` for
success, on an `Option Tag` stack. It is not already the raw Tag stack required
here. A real live adapter or a combined-program construction must consume the
success marker, transfer each some-tag in correct order, reject/handle malformed
represented payloads under its stated domain, and account for every transfer.
The currently closed decoder/framing machines halt; an automatic host projection
from their halt output into this component would not be a machine composition.
The strict framed pair's two bit fields likewise need actual extraction/routing
and must preserve the source binary wrapper's order: complete input-bit decoding,
input parsing, complete certificate-bit decoding, then streaming/fuel dispatch.
An input parse failure must not run certificate decoding first.

The source parser theorem should connect to the same represented values:

```text
machineSuccess raw s t bs
  iff (parseInputRun raw).value = some (s,t,bs)
  iff raw = inputCode s t bs.
```

The exact source/target codes and actual bs returned by this future machine must
be what the later fuel, move, rotation, equality, and stream machines consume.
Do not replace them with different existential witnesses, normalized bits, a
ghost `BinaryTree` register, or an assumed polynomial-time callback. An equality
machine for serialized trees may have a different observation order from
`eqTreeRun`; any alternative needs an explicit all-input semantic and numerical
bridge. Positioned rotation requires actual represented subtree traversal and
reconstruction, not a unit-cost source `applyMoveRun` call.

Before claiming this future component, still prove/implement:

1. The finite owned program, all alphabet instances, finite register callbacks,
   and arbitrary-register one-step equations, without input-dependent code.
2. The ghost source-frame count lemmas and complete scan/emit/undo/dropPending
   representation and iteration theorems, including malformed raw inputs.
3. Every whole-input phase invariant and exact rollback endpoint, with actual
   order, separator/delimiter behavior, high-zero width and unequal-size syntax.
4. Actual first-handoff time, represented-workspace bounds for intermediate
   configurations, and numerical composition under ambient callers.
5. Connected literal and arbitrary-tail cases, especially leading reserved tags,
   truncated trees, late malformed bits, trailing tags, nonpalindromic tree/bit
   order, failure rollback, stale temporary registers, and post-handoff callers.
6. The decoder/framing-to-input adapter, later semantic machines, final cleanup,
   and the complete computational-model/certificate-language correspondence.

No theorem, independent review, full-library validation, durable save, or
FDSA-5-93 qualification is claimed by this paper-only draft. The distinct
FDSA-5-92 and every other canonical outstanding obligation remain open.

### Next represented tree/input parser machine: implementation plan

Prepared 2026-11-21 after recovery of checkpoint 101. This is a paper-only
implementation plan, not a new source implementation, compiler result, review
axis, acceptance receipt, or qualification of FDSA-5-93. The earlier complete
23432-byte future draft remains preserved in requirements6 and the ordinary
paper. This note refines its pending proof and composition details; it does not
silently replace that draft, the fixed fuel/dispatch contracts, or any complete
verifier requirement. No repository file or compiler input was changed here.

#### 1. Selected next scope and sequential construction

**Implement the actual open tree-prefix machine first**, together with its
source connection, all-input time and reached-space proofs, and connected cases.
It is the difficult reusable part of the full input parser. Give it a finite
destination index so the subsequent input parser invokes the *same* tree core
for source and target while sharing the actual raw and scratch stacks. This
avoids a free relocation of data between two independently packaged machines.

The proposed sequence is concrete:

1. `TreeParserMachine.lean`: five finite tree phases, a ghost source-frame
   relation, actual reversal/rollback/cleanup, exact first-handoff timing,
   caller preservation, and a linear bound on every reached stack configuration.
   `Examples/RotationCertificateTreeParserMachine.lean` connects the cases below.
2. `InputParserMachine.lean`: specialize the finite destination index to source
   and target; supply separator/bit/EOF and rollback caller bodies in the same
   machine. Prove the complete all-raw connection to `parseInputRun`, exact
   stage counts, and the first-handoff `4*M+7` / `2*M+1` bounds. Its connected
   examples must include each failure stage and actual caller execution.
3. Open binary-framing/decoder routing and finite stack/label renaming:
   construct actual combined statement bodies that put the input word on this
   machine's raw stack, leave the certificate bits for the later decoder, and
   pass the returned literal fuel to the unchanged fuel/dispatch component.
   These are actual composition obligations, not host-language projections.
4. The remaining move parser, represented rotations/equality, stream loop,
   output/cleanup, quantitative simulation, and language/NP correspondence
   remain mandatory. They are not supplied by stages 1 or 2.

Root should release a bounded source scope through the existing loop before
stage 1. The anticipated narrow source delta is its producer, connected client,
normal aggregate import, and the ordinary mathematical record; no change to
TreeParser, InputParser, FixedWidthMachine, or FuelDispatchMachine is necessary
for the design below. Required source-frame helper lemmas can live in the new
machine module. Stage 2 follows only after the first core's actual interface is
available. There is no prerequisite to create a general parser framework.

Existing syntax is fixed: `E=emptyTag=0`, `N=nodeTag=1`, `S=separatorTag=2`,
`Z=bitZeroTag=3`, `O=bitOneTag=4`, and `I=endInputTag=5`, all in `Fin 16`.
Trees use preorder `E` and `N ++ leftCode ++ rightCode`. A complete input is
`treeCode s ++ [S] ++ treeCode t ++ [S] ++ bitTags bs ++ [I]` with final EOF.
The actual source parser stops at the first failed phase, permits unequal tree
sizes, and retains every threshold bit, including redundant high zeros.

`parseTreeRun_iff` recognizes exactly a first tree prefix and its actual suffix.
`parseTreeRun_prefix_injective` supplies tree/suffix uniqueness.
`parseInputRun_iff` recognizes exactly the complete `inputCode`.
`parseInputRun_code_append` establishes that any nonempty trailing material is
rejected by the EOF check without traversing that material. Their measured
costs remain distinct from the machine counts in this note.

The pinned `TM2.step` executes one finite `Stmt` body up to a `goto` or `halt`.
`push`, `peek`, `pop`, `load`, and `branch` are nested in that finite body.
All unbounded repetition below is an actual goto. Lists, source trees, lengths,
slot counts, mathematical prefixes, and recursive specifications appear only
in theorem parameters, invariants, ranks, or endpoint descriptions.

#### 3. Exact open tree-core API

Use a finite destination type `D`, finite protected-stack index `K`, finite
caller-label type `Λ`, finite caller-register type `R`, and a finite alphabet
`Γ k` for **each** protected stack. The useful specializations are `D=Unit`
for one-tree clients and `D=TreeSide` with two constructors for full input
parsing. The finite destination parameter is needed for the two actual calls;
it is not a collection of parsers stored as data.

Proposed public types, written schematically:

```lean
inductive LocalStack (D : Type)
  | raw | reverse | pending | output (destination : D)
inductive Phase | init | scan | emit | undo | dropPending
inductive Result | success | failure

abbrev StackId D K := LocalStack D ⊕ K
abbrev External D Λ := (D × Result) ⊕ Λ
abbrev Label D Λ := (D × Phase) ⊕ External D Λ
abbrev Temporaries := Option Tag × Option Unit
abbrev Registers R := Temporaries × R
```

`raw`, `reverse`, and every `output d` have alphabet `Tag`; `pending` has
alphabet `Unit`; protected `k` has alphabet `Γ k`. Thus the core has
`3+|D|+|K|` stacks, `7*|D|+|Λ|` labels, and `34*|R|` register values.
State finiteness is obtained only after choosing the indicated finite types.
Every alphabet gets its own finite instance; FinTM2's input-alphabet field
alone would not establish this.

The API should expose `block destination phase`, `program caller`, `cfg`,
`step caller`, `next caller`, `phaseLabel`, `resultLabel`, `callerLabel`, and
`reset`. `reset` clears only the two owned temporary fields and preserves `R`.
`program caller` executes the owned block at every `(destination,phase)` and
the fixed caller body at every external label. As in FixedWidthMachine,
`program_eq_of_agrees` recovers an arbitrary ambient program agreeing on owned
blocks. The caller is supplied **before the raw word or any other unbounded
data** and remains the same throughout the universal run theorem.

`cfg label regs raw rev pending outputs ctx` exposes every actual stack.
Here `outputs : D → Word` and `ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)` are configuration data,
not finite registers. Success for destination `d` updates that physical output
to `treeCode t ++ outputs d`; every other output is preserved. Failure preserves
all outputs. The entry requires empty `rev` and `pending`; outputs and protected
stacks may be arbitrary. Output alphabets may contain foreign tags below the
new code: those suffixes are never parsed.

A fixed `FinTM2` specialization can package these finite types and the same
`program caller`, choosing raw as input, `output d` as the designated output,
`(d,init)` as main, and a fixed reset caller state. Its actual `.step` is the
step used in the open theorems. Do not claim a `haltList` output from the live
result label. Generic phase theorems need only the equality assumptions used
by TM2; the finite specialization discharges all finiteness obligations once,
outside the quantification over raw input.

#### 4. Actual tree statement bodies

The following table fixes the algorithm and timing granularity. Each row is
one `TM2.step`, with the listed actions nested in one finite statement body.
The destination is part of the finite label; no input-dependent code is built.

| Phase and observed case | Finite actions | Next label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| init | Push one Unit onto pending; reset temporaries | scan for same destination |
| scan, head N | Peek raw; pop N; push N on reverse; push one Unit on pending; reset | scan |
| scan, head E, pending tail nonempty | Peek raw; pop E; push E on reverse; pop pending; peek pending; reset | scan |
| scan, head E, pending tail empty | Same finite actions | emit |
| scan, EOF or head neither N nor E | Peek without popping raw; reset | undo |
| emit, reverse nonempty | Pop reverse; push the actual tag on selected output; reset | emit |
| emit, reverse empty | Empty pop/probe; reset | live selected success |
| undo, reverse nonempty | Pop reverse; push the actual tag on raw; reset | undo |
| undo, reverse empty | Empty pop/probe; reset | dropPending |
| dropPending, pending nonempty | Pop one Unit; reset | dropPending |
| dropPending, pending empty | Empty pop/probe; reset | live selected failure |

Implement scan by a raw `peek`, finite comparisons against N/E, and the
corresponding finite branch. The E branch pops pending and then peeks its
actual new head. No callback asks a list for emptiness or length. The source
invariant ensures pending was nonempty at represented scan states. The total
TM2 definition on a corrupted scan state with empty pending may take the emit
branch after E; this is explicitly outside the represented entry semantics.
It is nevertheless covered by the raw one-step/rank/space laws below.

Every peek/pop overwrites the finite field it subsequently tests. Stale
temporary registers therefore cannot affect a result. Tag pushes during emit
and undo use the tag just popped, not a reconstructed ghost code. The longest
scan branch can be written with ten primitive statement constructors along
the executed path, including its branches, reset, and goto; the bound is fixed
independently of data. Check the eventual concrete body against that statement
count if this constant is used by a later lower-level simulation.

#### 5. The missing proof route is now explicit

##### 5.1 Actual transfer/cleanup lemmas

First prove the individual one-step equations with arbitrary registers and
all arbitrary stacks. Then prove by list induction:

* `emit_iterate`: `rev.length+1` steps transfer `rev.reverse` onto the selected
  old output and reach its live success label; raw and pending are unchanged.
* `undo_iterate`: `rev.length+1` steps transfer `rev.reverse` onto raw and reach
  `dropPending`; outputs and pending are unchanged.
* `dropPending_iterate`: `pending.length+1` steps empty that stack and reach
  live failure; all other stacks are unchanged.

These are generalized phase endpoints, not only empty-accumulator lemmas.
The empty probes and actual final gotos are included. Prefix versions establish
the exact intermediate reverse/output orientations by the same induction.

##### 5.2 Ghost source-frame connection

Define proof-side `leftSlots` by counting `TreeFrame.needLeft`; `needRight _`
contributes zero. Prove, by induction on the existing source frames and using
the actual `resumeTreeRun` definition:

```text
resumeTreeRun frames t = done u   => leftSlots frames = 0
resumeTreeRun frames t = next fs  => leftSlots frames = 1 + leftSlots fs
```

Here the displayed equalities refer to the returned `.1` projection. Reuse
the already proved `resumeTreeRun_prefix` for the corresponding prefix equality.
The needRight case invokes the induction hypothesis on the actual constructed
parent, and the needLeft case is immediate. These are mathematical lemmas,
not machine callbacks that perform source resumption in one transition.

The central generalized scan theorem starts with:

```text
raw = arbitrary remaining word
reverse = (stackPrefix frames).reverse
pending = replicate (1 + leftSlots frames) ()
selected output = arbitrary old output
```

It connects directly to `(parseTreeLoop raw frames).1`. On `some (t,rest)`,
the final raw is `rest` and the selected output is `treeCode t ++ oldOutput`.
On `none`, final raw is `stackPrefix frames ++ raw` and the output is unchanged.
Both cases empty reverse/pending and reset owned temporaries; all protected
stacks and caller state remain exact.

Prove this theorem by induction on `raw`, generalizing `frames`, registers,
and old/protected stores. N adds `needLeft` and appends N to the ghost prefix.
E uses the two resume lemmas: done makes the physical pending tail empty and
the accumulated prefix equal to `treeCode t`; next makes that physical tail
exactly `replicate (1+leftSlots nextFrames) ()`, allowing the induction
hypothesis. EOF/foreign directly uses undo then dropPending. Thus the compressed
slot implementation simulates the actual source continuation without storing
any `BinaryTree` or source frame in machine registers.

At entry, init supplies the slot for `frames=[]`. This yields the unconditional
all-raw tree theorem. It also explains why no valid prefix is scanned past its
first completed tree, and why malformed raw suffixes are never reparsed during
restoration.

##### 5.3 An exact rank for every owned configuration

Use a proof-only structurally recursive function `scanSteps raw p k`, where
`p` is current pending length and `k` is current reverse length:

```text
scanSteps [] p k = k+p+3
scanSteps (a::raw) p k =
  if a=N then 1 + scanSteps raw (p+1) (k+1)
  else if a=E then
    if p<=1 then k+3
    else 1 + scanSteps raw (p-1) (k+1)
  else k+p+3.
```

It recurses on the actual tail only as a **proof-side rank definition**.
Nothing in `block`, its callbacks, or finite registers refers to this function.
The `p=0` branch reflects the deliberately total machine behavior on an
unrepresented corrupted phase state.

Set the remaining rank of a configuration at a given phase to:

| Phase | Remaining steps |
| --- | --- |
| init | `1 + scanSteps raw (pending.length+1) reverse.length` |
| scan | `scanSteps raw pending.length reverse.length` |
| emit | `reverse.length+1` |
| undo | `reverse.length+pending.length+2` |
| dropPending | `pending.length+1` |
| external or halted | `0` |

Every owned transition decreases this rank **exactly by one**, even without
the representation invariant. Prove this from the finite one-step equations,
splitting pending as empty/singleton/at least two in the E branch. The rank is
positive exactly at owned labels. It gives actual prefix execution and first
handoff without an assumption that the program terminates. The already public
`FixedWidthMachine.ranked_prefix` and `ranked_prefix_eq` have precisely the
generic signatures needed; they may be reused without changing that module.
A local short induction is also sufficient if importing that helper would
create an unwanted dependency. Do not postulate its progress hypothesis:
derive it from these actual blocks.

Define `runSteps raw = 1 + scanSteps raw 1 0`. The generalized source theorem
uses rank `scanSteps raw (1+leftSlots frames) (stackPrefix frames).length`.
The endpoint proof and the rank proof refer to the same transition function.

##### 5.4 Exact and uniform tree counts

For a tree code of length L and arbitrary suffix:

```text
runSteps (treeCode t ++ rest) = 2*L+2 = 4*t.numNodes+4.
```

A useful stronger count lemma, proved by tree induction, is

```text
scanSteps (treeCode t ++ rest) (p+1) k =
  if p=0 then 2*L+k+1
  else L + scanSteps rest p (k+L).
```

It says a whole tree consumes exactly one pending slot while preserving every
outer slot. The node case first adds a slot, then applies the child hypotheses.
This is a count lemma about the concrete rank, independent of source-event
costs or a machine callback evaluating `treeCode`.

For exact failure counts, define an independent proof relation `OpenPrefix w p`:
the empty prefix has one pending slot; append N to increase p by one; append E
only while at least two slots remain, decreasing p by one. Every such prefix
is still incomplete and has no earlier completed tree. If
`raw = prefix ++ rest`, `OpenPrefix prefix p`, and `rest=[]` or its head is
neither N nor E, then

```text
runSteps raw = 2*prefix.length+p+4.
```

This includes init, every accepted tag, rejection probe, rollback, both empty
cleanup probes, and p actual Unit removals. Also `0<p<=prefix.length+1`.
The generalized scan/source proof gives this decomposition for every source
failure; the decomposition is ghost evidence, not a runtime parser.

The simpler unconditional bound can be proved directly by induction on raw:

```text
scanSteps raw p k <= 3*raw.length+k+p+3
runSteps raw <= 3*raw.length+5.
```

Thus exact timing does not depend on classifying every malformed raw word in
advance. On success the source observation is `7*n+3`; on failure it is the
actual existing source observation. Do not identify either with machine time.

#### 6. Actual space, first handoff, and composability

There is a particularly simple space proof that was not resolved in the old
partial draft. Let `cells c` sum the lengths of **all actual stacks**, including
arbitrary old outputs and protected context. Add this phase-dependent credit:

```text
credit(init) = raw.length+1
credit(scan) = raw.length
credit(emit/undo/dropPending/external/halt) = 0
potential c = cells c + credit c.
```

Every owned step is nonincreasing in this potential, for arbitrary registers
and stacks. Init spends its extra credit on the new pending token. N increases
cells by one but decreases raw length by one. E decreases raw length and removes
a pending cell when present. The rejection transition discards remaining scan
credit; undo transfers preserve cells, so returning raw material cannot increase
the zero-credit undo potential. Emit transfers preserve cells; pending cleanup
decreases them. No claim about arbitrary caller steps is needed or valid.

At ordinary entry let M be raw length, O the sum of old output lengths, and U
the total protected storage. The initial potential is `2*M+O+U+1`. For every
actual iterate `j <= runSteps raw`, therefore:

* the reached configuration exists;
* all protected stacks and caller state equal their entry values;
* other destination outputs equal their entry values;
* owned temporaries are reset when `0<j`;
* actual total stack cells are at most `2*M+O+U+1`;
* for `j<runSteps raw` the label is an owned phase for the selected destination;
* at equality the exact live result configuration is reached, before executing
  that caller body.

The bound has a nonvacuous sharp family. For raw `replicate M N`, after `M+1`
steps (init plus all scans) raw is empty, reverse contains M Ns, pending has
M+1 tokens, and cells are exactly `2*M+O+U+1`. The failure probe has not yet run.

Construct Type-valued `StateTransition.EvalsToInTime` data from the exact
iterate equality, first at `runSteps raw`, then weakened to `3*M+5`. Its target
is `some liveCfg`, not `none` and not `haltList`. An ambient caller theorem
uses `program_eq_of_agrees`, or caller-independence for the prefix from the
rank. Quantifying over unrestricted `TM2.Reaches` after the external handoff
would be false: the caller is allowed to alter stacks immediately afterward.

The important source-connected public clients are:

```text
run_of_some: parseTreeRun raw = some(t,rest) -> exact successful live cfg
run_of_none: parseTreeRun raw = none -> exact restored live cfg
run_code: arbitrary suffix and old output, exact 2*L+2 count
run_source: one unconditional endpoint theorem using parseTreeRun raw .1
runInTime / runInLinearTime: actual timed data for the same cfg and step
prefix / prefix_cells_le / caller_independent: through first handoff only
```

Here source result notation again means the `.1` projection. A predicate
`machineSuccess raw t rest` must refer to this **first** handoff at `runSteps`,
not arbitrary reachability, and should satisfy
`machineSuccess raw t rest ↔ (parseTreeRun raw).1=some(t,rest)
↔ raw=treeCode t++rest`.

#### 7. Full input parser in the same physical machine

Specialize destinations to `TreeSide.source | TreeSide.target`. Add protected
owned stacks `fuel : Bool` and `bitsReverse : Bool`, followed by arbitrary
caller stacks. Reuse the tree core's finite temporaries for Bool observations
as specified below. The full parser owns seven stacks in total:
raw, source, target, treeReverse, pending, fuel, bitsReverse. On full entry,
all six except raw are empty. The certificate is an arbitrary protected stack,
not a global variable and not a field inspected by input parsing.

Use the tree core unchanged, including its literal returned stacks. Its live
result labels can be actual full-parser block labels; no extra goto is needed
to identify a continuation. Fix this exact arrangement to preserve the counts:

* source/success executes the first separator block;
* target/success executes the second separator block;
* target/failure executes restoreSep1;
* source/failure is the **full parser's live failure exit**;
* a separate caller label is the full parser's live success exit.

One explicit label type is
`Tree.Label TreeSide (InputPhase ⊕ (Unit ⊕ Λ))`, where the Unit caller label
is full success, and source/failure supplies full failure. The remaining
external Λ labels remain arbitrary caller code. The full handler installs the
three nonterminal tree-result bodies above, the InputPhase bodies below, and
the two real caller exits. Whole-parser Owned must include those nonterminal
tree-result labels while excluding source/failure and full success. This
resolves the former draft's possible hidden extra transition at tree handoff.

Additional phases and literal actions:

| Block | Actual action and routing |
| --- | --- |
| first separator | Peek raw; if S pop it and goto target/init; otherwise goto sourceToReverse |
| second separator | Peek raw; if S pop it and goto bitsScan; otherwise goto targetToReverse |
| bitsScan, Z/O | Pop actual tag; push corresponding finite Bool on bitsReverse; repeat |
| bitsScan, I | Pop I; goto bitsEmit |
| bitsScan, EOF/foreign | Do not pop raw; goto bitsUndo |
| bitsEmit | Pop/push one actual Bool from bitsReverse onto fuel; empty probe goes to EOF |
| EOF | Peek raw; empty goes to live success, nonempty to restoreEnd |
| restoreEnd | Push I on raw; goto fuelUndo |
| fuelUndo | Transfer fuel to bitsReverse one Bool per transition; empty goes to bitsUndo |
| bitsUndo | Transfer bitsReverse onto raw using finite `bitTag`; empty goes to restoreSep2 |
| restoreSep2 | Push S on raw; goto targetToReverse |
| targetToReverse | Transfer target to treeReverse one tag per transition; empty goes to targetToRaw |
| targetToRaw | Transfer treeReverse to raw one tag per transition; empty goes to restoreSep1 |
| restoreSep1 | Push S on raw; goto sourceToReverse |
| sourceToReverse | Transfer source to treeReverse one tag per transition; empty goes to sourceToRaw |
| sourceToRaw | Transfer treeReverse to raw one tag per transition; empty goes to live failure |

The target/failure label contains the same one-step restoreSep1 body; it does
not first goto a second restoreSep1 label and accidentally charge an extra
step. TargetToRaw's empty branch does go to the ordinary restoreSep1 label.
All blocks reset the same two owned temporary fields before each goto.
Consequently, the initial tree init resets every owned field even from arbitrary
incoming registers; no additional initial reset transition or entry premise is
needed.

##### Selected register refinement: no extra Bool scratch

Use exactly the tree core's `Option Tag × Option Unit` temporaries throughout.
A Bool pop/peek stores `Option.map bitTag bit` in the tag field. After the
isSome guard, comparison with `bitOneTag` recovers that single finite Bool.
Tag raw probes overwrite the same field. Unit probes use the Unit field.
Thus the existing tree `reset` already resets every owned field from arbitrary
incoming registers. The caller state R remains arbitrary and is preserved
exactly. This refinement supersedes only
the optional product-register suggestion in the earlier partial draft.

No bits are normalized and no bit count is stored in control. At final EOF,
the actual fuel is already forward-oriented, matching the successful
`parseBitsRun` result before `finishInputRun`. On EOF rejection the two actual
reversals restore those bits in original raw order, including every high zero.

#### 8. Exact full-parser endpoint and failure partition

For every raw Word and arbitrary caller state/context, require:

* If `(parseInputRun raw).1=some(s,t,bs)`, the first live success has raw empty,
  source `treeCode s`, target `treeCode t`, fuel **the same bs**, and all three
  scratch stacks empty.
* If the actual source result is none, the first live failure has raw **equal
  to the original whole word** and every output/scratch stack empty.
* Both endpoints reset all owned finite fields and preserve every caller
  stack and the caller register value. Neither caller body has run.

Use existing source results in their actual order: tree, separator, tree,
separator, bits, EOF. Failure branches are disjoint by the preceding actual
success hypotheses. They are not an existential parse of an unrelated word.

| Failure point | Restoration after the failed component |
| --- | --- |
| first tree | Its own tree undo/pending cleanup reaches full failure directly |
| first separator | sourceToReverse, sourceToRaw; the bad separator was not popped |
| target tree | Tree core restores target-start raw; restoreSep1, source rollback |
| second separator | target rollback, restoreSep1, source rollback |
| bits before I | bitsUndo, restoreSep2, target rollback, restoreSep1, source rollback |
| nonempty raw after I | restoreEnd, fuelUndo, bitsUndo, restoreSep2, target rollback, restoreSep1, source rollback |

Generalize each reversal proof over an arbitrary raw tail, arbitrary reverse
accumulator, and protected stores. For output rollback, the pair of transfer
loops costs `2*code.length+2`, including two empty probes. For EOF rejection,
fuelUndo plus bitsUndo costs `2*bs.length+2`. RestoreSep1/2/End each cost one
actual transition. No append/reverse expression is evaluated by a callback.

An unconditional proof-side endpoint function can pattern-match on
`(parseInputRun raw).1` to describe these final configurations. A proof-side
`inputSteps raw` can follow the finite source phase decomposition and use
`Tree.runSteps` for actual tree phases. Neither function occurs in the program.
The theorem must supply an actual iterate equality at this count; defining a
ghost endpoint/count is not evidence of its execution.

#### 9. Exact full-parser time and representation invariants

Let Ls/Lt be the actual completed tree-code lengths. In a failed tree let k
be the accepted incomplete prefix length and p its positive pending slots.
In a bit phase let b be the number of accepted bit tags.

| Outcome/stage | Exact proposed transitions from full entry |
| --- | --- |
| success | `2*Ls+2*Lt+2*b+9 = 2*M+3` |
| first tree failure | `2*k+p+4` |
| first separator failure | `4*Ls+5` |
| target tree failure | `4*Ls+2*k+p+10` |
| second separator failure | `4*Ls+4*Lt+11` |
| bit failure before I | `4*Ls+4*Lt+2*b+14` |
| EOF rejection after I | `4*Ls+4*Lt+4*b+18` |

The success count is two tree runs, two separator blocks, `b+1` bit scans,
`b+1` bit emit steps, and one EOF block. Entry is source/init, not a free
mathematical reconfiguration. The failure counts follow the table in section
8 with the actual empty probes. They agree with the preserved partial draft.

For every raw word of length M, `inputSteps raw <= 4*M+7`. The lower bounds on
M needed for the failure rows are respectively k, Ls, Ls+1+k, Ls+1+Lt,
Ls+Lt+2+b, and Ls+Lt+4+b, together with `p<=k+1`. The bound is sharp, for
example, at `treeCode s ++ [S] ++ treeCode t` with the second separator missing:
M=Ls+Lt+1 and the actual count is exactly `4*M+7`. It is also attained at
`treeCode s ++ [S]` when the target tree is missing.

Maintain the actual orientation/segment invariants, not only length bounds.
At tree scans the generalized source relation from section 5 applies. At
bitsScan, the original reached threshold field is
`bitTags (bitsReverse.reverse) ++ currentRaw`. At bitsEmit, processed fuel
is a suffix of the original bits while bitsReverse is the reversed un-emitted
prefix, so `bitsReverse.reverse ++ fuel` equals the original bits. In
fuelUndo/bitsUndo and tree rollback, the transfer lemmas retain the exact
unvisited raw tail. This exposes reversal mistakes on nonpalindromic examples.

For space, let `baseCells` count the six non-pending owned stacks, and let d
be the finite number of consumed delimiters recorded by the phase. The exact
invariant is `baseCells + d = M`:

| Phase region | d |
| --- | --- |
| source tree / first separator / source rollback / final failure | 0 |
| target tree / second separator / target rollback / restoreSep1 | 1 before its push |
| bitsScan before I / fuelUndo / bitsUndo / restoreSep2 | 2 before its push |
| bitsEmit / EOF / restoreEnd | 3 before its push |
| final success | 3 |

Each restore block reduces d by one by pushing its actual fixed tag. Each
scan/emit/undo transfer conserves baseCells. No copy operation is hidden in a
transfer. Pending has at most `M+1` cells by the tree prefix invariant; outside
the tree phases it is empty. Consequently, with arbitrary protected storage U,
every configuration through full first handoff has at most `2*M+U+1` cells.
The all-N source-tree failure family retains the sharp intermediate witness.

For first exit and the bound, concatenate the concrete phase-prefix proofs.
When splitting a prefix at a subcomponent handoff, that tree result label is
an owned full-parser label except for source/failure. This is why the two
Owned predicates must be distinguished. A short private iterate-add/prefix
concatenation lemma suffices; no oracle-style component assumption is needed.

Expose exact and linear `StateTransition.EvalsToInTime` constructions to the
same live endpoint for the actual full program, and connect success with

#### 11. The precise composition boundary after input parsing

The existing `BitDecoderMachine` is closed: success is
`none :: word.map some` on an Option Tag output stack; failure is `[]`; other
stacks are empty and registers reset at halt. That output is not already the
raw Tag stack of this component. The existing `BitPairFraming` is also closed:
success is `none :: input.map some ++ none :: cert.map some`, and its parser
strictly recognizes `escapeBits input ++ true :: cert`. Its theorem is not a
machine execution of the downstream verifier.

A concrete next adapter route is to build open variants with the same finite
scan and transfer algorithms, and prove their phase equations directly or by
a checked static statement/label/stack translation. In the framing variant,
emitCert pushes Bool onto a distinct certificate-bit stack; emitFirst pushes
Bool onto the input-bit stack. The old marker-emitting empty branches become
actual reset/goto branches; their step counts remain the same, because marker
pushes were inside those finite blocks. The resulting success endpoint has
both actual forward bit fields and cleared framing scratch in
`2*input.length+2*cert.length+4` transitions. Framing failure hands off with
the owned stores empty after its actual cleanup. These are future theorems;
the existing closed contracts stay unchanged.

Similarly, an open decoder can emit actual Tag onto the parser raw stack and
goto its entry instead of emitting an Option marker and halting. The input
decoder must finish before the input parser; the certificate decoder must not
start until input parsing succeeds. Both decode complete four-bit words, as
the existing `verifyBitsRun` requires. A failed input parse must reach rejection
cleanup without certificate decoding, even when those certificate bits contain
a malformed trailing partial block.

If the existing marked decoder result is retained instead, a real represented-
domain adapter needs a marker step, a pop/push scan of its some-tags into a
Tag reverse stack, an empty probe, and an actual reverse transfer plus empty
probe. On a successful w-tag result that costs `2*w+3`; decoder failure `[]`
can dispatch in one step. A total malformed-representation contract needs its
own explicit reject/cleanup branch. One cannot use `Option.map`, a list map,
or a mathematical output projection as a free runtime adapter.

The exact same returned source code, target code, and fuel word must feed
later components. FixedWidthMachine and FuelDispatchMachine keep their current
contracts and their literal fixed-width fuel. Their different finite sum-index
presentations can be reconciled by a fixed stack/label/register renaming whose
one-step commuting law is proved; it is compile-time syntax translation over
finite statement bodies, not a data-dependent runtime traversal. No such
translation is assumed to exist merely from an equivalence of endpoint data.
If physical stacks differ, actual transfer loops and their time/space are owed.

#### 12. Final cleanup and remaining proof obligations

An open parser failure restores raw; it does not satisfy `haltList` because
that nonoutput stack is nonempty. In the eventual verifier, rejection cleanup
can be a fixed finite sequence of stack-clearing labels. Each label pops one
cell per transition and, on its empty probe, advances to the next fixed stack.
The last empty probe pushes the Boolean result, resets **all** finite registers
to the eventual machine's initial state, and halts. With h nonoutput stacks and
C actual cells to clear, this concrete cleanup takes `C+h` transitions when
the result stack starts empty; clearing an existing result stack must also be
counted if it is not guaranteed empty. Space does not increase until the final
single output cell. No cleanup label performs a semantic parse of the remaining
certificate. This is a concrete future cleanup design, not a current theorem.

Before claiming stage 1, implement/prove every finite block, generalized phase
endpoint, source-frame/slot connection, exact rank decrease, prefix first exit,
potential bound, and actual timed datum above, then connect the independently
fixed cases. Before claiming stage 2, add its actual handler/blocks, all failure
routes, exact word orientations, finite delimiter-debt invariant, source result
connection, and first-handoff timed/space results. Any extra real transition
discovered in implementation must be reflected in the exact counts and the
independent arithmetic; it cannot be hidden by changing a ghost configuration.

Neither stage constructs the full verifier's `TM2OutputsInTime` or
`TM2ComputableInPolyTime`. The later combined program must connect actual
framing, both complete decoders in the prescribed order, this parser, the
unchanged fuel component, actual represented rotations/equality/stream control,
and final output/cleanup. The pinned TM2-to-TM1 semantic simulator does not by
itself provide the missing quantitative overhead theorem. Source polynomial
observations, finite local alphabets, and the polynomial witness bound are
ingredients, not substitutes for that execution and computational-model proof.
The complete FDSA-5-93/NP correspondence, FDSA-5-92, and other canonical
outstanding requirements remain open.

### Independent tree parser machine cases, fixed before implementation

#### Status and scope

Prepared on 2026-11-21 by the independent connected-case author for the same
CTB-24/FDSA-5-93 task and review loop. This is a prospective case specification,
not a compiled Lean file or a review of a new implementation. Neither prospective

changed to prepare it.

The complete design read was `continuation085/InputParserMachine.next.md`,
40,104 bytes, SHA256
`73b0cad2d629be4fd0e02c39645a1954e05ede4e0989c517b940c56cd88218af`.
The present scope is only `TreeParserMachine.lean` and its connected example
owner `Examples/RotationCertificateTreeParserMachine.lean`. The full input
parser, binary adapters, rotations, equality, streaming verifier, final cleanup,
and full verifier-machine/NP correspondence remain subsequent obligations.

Expected syntax and returned data below are derived from the existing preorder
tree grammar and actual source parser. Machine counts are independently derived
from the proposed finite phase table; they are conditional on that table, not

The examples should connect to public contracts and actual finite caller bodies,

#### 1. Notation, actual representations, and quantifier order

Write `E = emptyTag = 0`, `N = nodeTag = 1`, and use tag 15 as one concrete
foreign tag. A foreign tag is any Fin16 value distinct from E and N, including
separators and bit tags. Let `L(t) = (treeCode t).length = 2*t.numNodes+1`.
The nil, singleton, left-two and right-two codes are respectively:

| Tree | Actual tag word |
| --- | --- |
| nil | `[E]` |
| node nil nil | `[N,E,E]` |
| node (node nil nil) nil | `[N,N,E,E,E]` |
| node nil (node nil nil) | `[N,E,N,E,E]` |

For a fixed destination d, an ordinary call starts at `(d,init)` with arbitrary
raw word, arbitrary old output family, arbitrary protected stacks and arbitrary
finite register contents, but **empty reverse and pending stacks**. The result
is a live success/failure label for d. It is not a halted configuration or outer
`none`. On success, exactly the accepted code is prepended to output d and the
actual returned suffix stays on raw. On failure, raw is restored in its entirety
and every old output is unchanged. Both scratch stacks are empty at either
ordinary endpoint, both owned temporaries are reset, and caller state is kept.

Choose finite stack/control/register/alphabet types and the complete caller
program once, before universally quantifying over raw words and contexts. Trees,
source frames, ranks, lengths and parser results are proof-side specifications;
none can be a register, a callback argument inspecting an unbounded store, or an
input-dependent program generator. A generic statement may have arbitrary finite
types, but a concrete finite specialization must discharge every alphabet's
finiteness, not just the designated input alphabet.

A useful specialization has two destinations, two protected stacks (one Bool,
one Tag), one additional caller label, and Bool caller state. It has 7 stack
indices, 15 labels and 68 register values under the proposed representations.
The stacks contain unbounded lists despite these finite index/alphabet counts.
Use distinct output suffixes such as `[15,6]` and `[2,10,11]`, and stale owned
temporaries `(some 15, some ())`, to prevent vacuous preservation examples.

#### 2. Ordinary calls: independently fixed values and costs

Every success row permits arbitrary tail, old outputs, protected lists, finite
caller state and stale temporaries. Every failure row asserts actual restored
raw, unchanged old outputs and cleared scratch, not merely a failure label.

| Raw | Expected first result | Actual TM2 steps |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `[]` | failure; raw `[]` | 5 |
| `foreign :: tail` | failure; the entire original word | 5 |
| `[N]` | failure; raw `[N]` | 8 |
| `[N,E]` | failure; raw `[N,E]` | 9 |
| `[N,N]` | failure; raw `[N,N]` | 11 |
| `[N,N,E]` | failure; raw `[N,N,E]` | 12 |
| `E :: tail` | nil; exact tail remains | 4 |
| `[N,E,E] ++ tail` | singleton; exact tail remains | 8 |
| `[N,N,E,E,E] ++ tail` | left-two; exact tail remains | 12 |
| `[N,E,N,E,E] ++ tail` | right-two; exact tail remains | 12 |
| `replicate k N` | failure; original word restored | `3*k+5` |
| `replicate k N ++ foreign :: tail` | failure; original word restored | `3*k+5` |
| `[N,N,E] ++ foreign :: tail` | failure; original word restored | 12 |

The last row distinguishes rollback order: just before rejection the reverse
stack contains `[E,N,N]`; undo must reconstruct `[N,N,E]` above the blocked
foreign head. That head and arbitrary tail are not popped or traversed. The
foreign-head row rejects even if tail begins with a valid tree. Conversely,
`treeCode t ++ foreign :: tail` succeeds and leaves the foreign head on raw.
This tree parser recognizes a prefix, not complete input syntax.

For a successful code of length L, charge one init step, L scan steps, L actual
reverse-to-output transfers and one empty emit probe: `2*L+2 = 4*n+4`.
For failure after an unfinished accepted prefix w of length k with p remaining
pending slots, charge init 1, scan k, blocked probe 1, undo k, empty undo probe 1,
pending drops p, and empty pending probe 1: `2*k+p+4`.
Here `1 <= p <= k+1`, so every raw word has bound `3*raw.length+5`.
The all-N family attains this uniform bound, including M=0.

Use a nonpalindromic successful output explicitly: left-two with raw tail
`[15,6,N]` and old selected output `[15,6]` must finish with raw `[15,6,N]`
and output `[N,N,E,E,E,15,6]`. Neither reversing the code nor overwriting old
output meets this expectation. Run this case for either of two destinations,
leaving the other destination's distinct old contents exactly unchanged.

#### 3. General transfer phases and represented scan states

The generalized phase contracts are useful independently of ordinary entry.
They must state their actual nonempty domains rather than silently assuming
that arbitrary phase inputs satisfy the ordinary parser invariant.

| Phase entry | Exact work | Required actual endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| emit, reverse rev | `rev.length+1` | live success; output d becomes `rev.reverse ++ old`; reverse empty; raw and pending unchanged |
| undo, reverse rev | `rev.length+1` | live dropPending; raw becomes `rev.reverse ++ raw`; reverse empty; pending and outputs unchanged |
| dropPending, pending ps | `ps.length+1` | live failure; pending empty; all other stacks unchanged |

In particular, emit with a nonempty pending stack preserves it; the ordinary
empty-scratch success theorem needs the reachable scan invariant to establish
that pending was empty on entry to emit. Test arbitrary old suffixes, raw tails,
register values, destinations and protected contexts through these contracts.
For orientation, emit from rev `[E,N,N]` produces `[N,N,E] ++ old`, while undo
from the same rev restores `[N,N,E] ++ raw` without changing old output.

For ghost frames fs, use the existing `stackPrefix fs` and let
`k = (stackPrefix fs).length`, `p = 1 + leftSlots fs`. The represented entry is
**scan**, with reverse `(stackPrefix fs).reverse` and pending `replicate p ()`.
The source computation is `(parseTreeLoop raw fs).1`, not a fresh empty-frame
parse of raw and not an init step. Generalized failure restores
`stackPrefix fs ++ raw`; success emits the complete enclosing tree's code.

If such a scan consumes h more tags before completing, its remaining work is
`k+2*h+1`: h scans, k+h transfers, one empty emit probe. If it consumes h tags
and then blocks with q pending slots, its remaining work is `k+2*h+q+3`.
These are derived phase counts, not runtime length computations.

##### Nonempty ghost-frame examples

| Frames and represented material | Unread raw | Expected output/rest or restored raw | Scan-only steps |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `[needLeft]`: prefix `[N]`, reverse `[N]`, pending 2 | `[E,E] ++ tail` | singleton code above old; rest tail | 6 |
| same | `[]` | failure; raw `[N]` | 6 |
| same | `E :: foreign :: tail` | failure; raw `[N,E] ++ foreign :: tail` | 7 |
| `[needRight nil]`: prefix `[N,E]`, reverse `[E,N]`, pending 1 | `E :: tail` | singleton code above old; rest tail | 5 |
| `[needRight singleton]`: prefix `[N,N,E,E]`, pending 1 | `E :: tail` | left-two code above old; rest tail | 7 |
| `[needRight nil, needLeft]`: prefix `[N,N,E]`, pending 2 | `[E,E] ++ tail` | left-two code above old; rest tail | 8 |
| `[needLeft, needRight nil]`: prefix `[N,E,N]`, pending 2 | `[E,E] ++ tail` | right-two code above old; rest tail | 8 |

The mixed-frame rows have the same pending count and prefix length but different
tree shapes. They distinguish the outer-first `stackPrefix` representation from
the top-first list of source frames; slot counts alone cannot recover the code.

Retain open families, not only these literals:

- `[needLeft]` with unread `treeCode l ++ treeCode r ++ tail` emits the parent
  code in `2*(L(l)+L(r))+2` scan-only steps.
- `[needRight l]` with unread `treeCode r ++ tail` emits the parent code in
  `L(l)+2*L(r)+2` scan-only steps.
- `[needRight l]` with unread `foreign :: tail` fails in `L(l)+5` steps and
  restores `[N] ++ treeCode l ++ foreign :: tail`.

The third family also makes the rollback include a large preexisting accepted
prefix, even though the blocked unread raw is tiny. Generalized workspace and
remaining-time statements must include represented old prefix/pending cells.

#### 4. Entry hypotheses have concrete counterexamples

These are actual executions from deliberately invalid ordinary entries. They
must not weaken the valid-entry theorem, and they must not be mistaken for

| Invalid entry | Actual result | Steps | False conclusion it separates |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| init; raw `[E]`, reverse `[N]`, pending empty | success; output `[N,E] ++ old`, raw empty | 5 | ordinary nil output and 4-step count without empty reverse |
| init; raw empty, reverse `[N]`, pending empty | failure; raw `[N]` | 6 | failure restores original raw without empty reverse |
| init; raw `[E]`, reverse empty, pending `[()]` | failure; raw `[E]`, output old | 7 | ordinary nil succeeds without empty pending |
| init; raw `[E,E]`, reverse empty, pending `[()]` | success; output `[E,E] ++ old`, raw empty | 6 | only the first tree is consumed without empty pending |
| init instead of scan for the valid needLeft state: raw `[E,E]`, reverse `[N]`, pending 2 | failure; restored raw `[N,E,E]`, output old | 10 | generalized scan states can be initialized a second time |
| scan; raw `[N,E]`, reverse and pending empty | success; output `[N,E] ++ old`, raw empty | 5 | arbitrary pending count suffices for source-parser correctness |

In the last row, N creates one slot and E removes it; the emitted word is an

By contrast, an arbitrary **old output** is permitted: ordinary clean entry with

This must not be confused with consuming two trees due to a corrupt pending stack.

#### 5. Prefix execution, sharp workspace, and first return

Fix the caller and actual entry configuration, and quantify over every
`j <= runSteps raw`. A connected prefix client must obtain an actual reached
configuration and actual iterate equality, then use its local owned-step path.
For j strictly before the bound, the label is owned with the selected
destination; at equality it is the exact live result. Caller state, all protected
stacks and all other output destinations are unchanged. Owned temporaries are
reset when `j>0`; they need not already be reset at j=0. Do not assume an abstract
reachability premise with no exhibited run in the sharp example.

Let M be initial raw length, O the sum of old output lengths, and U the sum of
protected lengths. Every such prefix has at most `2*M+O+U+1` actual stack cells.
The proposed phase credit is raw.length+1 in init, raw.length in scan, and zero
otherwise; potential is cells plus credit. Each owned step is nonincreasing,
including arbitrary corrupt scratch states for that local potential statement.
These are not stack-cell conservation claims: init and N allocate a pending
token, E consumes one, and rejection cleanup removes the remaining tokens.

For **every** M, exhibit the exact iterate after M+1 steps on raw `replicate M N`:
label scan, raw empty, reverse `replicate M N`, pending `replicate (M+1) ()`,
old outputs and protected lists unchanged. Cells equal `2*M+O+U+1`. The blocked
EOF probe has not run, and this actual prefix lies before the first failure at
`3*M+5`. This is a sharp family, including M=0 and nonempty old/protected lists.

Caller independence is through this same inclusive first-return interval only.
An ambient program agreeing on all owned blocks must have the same prefix and
endpoint even when its external bodies are entirely different. First-success
recognition should be equivalent to `(parseTreeRun raw).1 = some (t,rest)` and
`raw = treeCode t ++ rest`, using the exact first-handoff configuration and count.
Unrestricted `TM2.Reaches` to a success label is not an adequate recognizer.

#### 6. Actual live callers and constructed timed composition

The required time object is Type-valued `StateTransition.EvalsToInTime` for the
same actual `step caller` and configurations, with target `some liveCfg`.
Construct one datum at exact `runSteps raw` and one at `3*raw.length+5` using
the actual run and proven bound. Its source-result description is a specification,
not an executable oracle. Quantify over arbitrary raw, old outputs, stale
temporaries and protected context with the finite program fixed first.

Use a concrete finite caller and `EvalsToInTime.trans`, not merely the arithmetic
equation adding budgets. The current predecessor client's actual timed
composition provides the compatible pinned interface: pass the same step
function, both budgets, actual start/middle/finish, and both timed records.

##### A. One actual sentinel push and halt

For a fixed destination, let its success continuation push true onto a protected
Bool stack and halt. Other external bodies can halt. Ordinary raw `E :: tail`
reaches its live success configuration in 4 steps with the protected list
unchanged. The fifth step performs the push, producing a real halted
configuration with that list `true :: old`; the sixth iteration is outer none.
Compose the 4-step core datum and 1-step caller datum to get the actual 5-step
datum. The halted configuration may retain raw tail and output and is not assumed
to be `haltList`. This checks live return versus halt versus outer none.

##### B. A finite post-return loop can violate the original space bound

Start with raw empty and every actual stack empty. Let the failure continuation
push true onto a protected Bool stack and goto that same live failure label.
The core reaches failure after 5 steps. After 5+j steps the protected stack is
`replicate j true`; at j=2 there are 2 cells, exceeding the original prefix bound
`2*0+0+0+1 = 1`. The caller is one fixed finite body, not an input-dependent
program. This actual loop separates a first-handoff bound from an invalid global
reachability or termination claim. A single push already refutes unrestricted
protected-stack preservation, even when it does not yet exceed the bound.

##### C. Later success labels can be manufactured by caller code

From raw empty, the true first endpoint at step 5 is failure. A finite failure
continuation can push E onto the selected output and goto that destination's
success label. At step 6 there is a live success label with raw empty and output
`[E]`, although the source parse of the original empty raw failed. It can then
goto init and reenter. This is an explicit counterexample to replacing first
success by arbitrary eventual reachability; the owned program itself is unchanged.

##### D. Two destinations under one actual program

Let success for destination 0 execute one reset/goto body targeting destination
1's init. Let success for destination 1 be the final live continuation. Start
with `treeCode s ++ treeCode t ++ tail`, empty scratch and arbitrary distinct
old output contents. First call costs `2*L(s)+2`; the actual caller jump costs 1;
second call costs `2*L(t)+2`. The final live success at destination 1 is reached
after `2*L(s)+2*L(t)+5`, with output 0 `treeCode s ++ old0`, output 1
`treeCode t ++ old1`, exact raw tail, cleared scratch and preserved context.
For left-two followed by nil the count is **17**.

Compose both constructed core records with the intervening actual one-step
record under one and the same program. The second call must start from the
literal first returned configuration, not an existentially unrelated state.
Its ordinary scratch hypotheses are supplied by the first endpoint. This is
tree-call composition only; it does not parse separators or implement full input.
For this nonallocating caller the original total workspace bound can also be
carried across: the second entry potential is
`2*(M-L(s)) + (O+L(s)) + U + 1 <= 2*M+O+U+1`.
Do not extend this calculation to arbitrary caller bodies.

#### 7. Source and emitter connections without relabeling time

Use existing public `parseTreeRun_code`, `parseTreeRun_iff`,
`parseTreeRun_cost_of_some`, `parseTreeRun_cost_le`,
`parseTreeRun_prefix_injective`, `parseTreeRun_emit`, and `emitTreeRun_value`.
The source frames and `resumeTreeRun_prefix` remain proof-facing invariants.
For malformed source literals, use actual public loop equations or definitional

Feed the actual first value of `emitTreeRun t tail` to the machine. Connect its

own models. A further natural input connection feeds the actual
`emitInputRun source target bs` value to the tree core: it returns source's code
and leaves the literal first separator, target code, bit field and end tag as

or the existing source full-input parse observation 46.

The last row is a useful unbounded counterexample: the source already holds l

## Quantitative TM2-to-TM1 continuation: future proof plan

The complete fixed note below is retained with only a two-level heading-depth
normalization outside code fences. Its raw bytes are preserved in requirements7.
The stated future stages remain prospective until implemented and validated.

### Quantitative TM2-to-TM1 continuation: checked derivation plan

Prepared 21 November 2026 while the exact C6c whole-library check and original
review were running. This is a future proof plan, not a new Lean theorem,
compiled simulation, polynomial-time record, or NP qualification. It supplements
the complete retained verifier obligations and does not replace any of them.

#### Inspected pinned interfaces

The local pinned Mathlib `Computability/TuringMachine/StackTuringMachine.lean`
contains `Turing.TM2to1.trNormal`, `trStAct`, `tr`, `TrCfg`,
`tr_respects_aux₁`, `tr_respects_aux₂`, `tr_respects_aux₃`, `tr_respects`,
`trCfg_init`, and `tr_supports`. The relevant definitions and proofs around
the stack-action translation and simulation were read. The existing simulation
uses unbounded reachability relations; this inspection did not find a numerical
transition bound in those inspected declarations. The distinct
`Computable.lean` time records require an actual `EvalsToInTime` value.

The simulator's normal state translates finite non-stack work within its
statement. A stack action is deferred to a `go` label, which walks from the
bottom marker to the stack top; after the action, `ret` walks back and resumes
the translated remainder. Loads and branches within one TM1 statement do not
add outer `TM1.step` transitions. This is the pinned statement semantics,
not a RAM-operation tariff.

#### Numerical derivation to formalize

For a finite TM2 statement, define a proof-only stack-action bound `A(q)`:
push/peek/pop add one to the continuation bound, load retains it, branch takes
the maximum of its two continuation bounds, and goto/halt have bound zero.
For a fixed finite program, take a maximum over its actual finite label set.
Call this fixed constant `A`. It is chosen from the program before any input.

Suppose an actual TM2 boundary configuration has at most `W` cells in all
its stacks. Before any internal stack action in that one statement, its total
cell count is at most `W+A`, since only pushes can increase it and there are
at most `A` stack actions on an executed branch. No global potential at
statement boundaries alone gives this internal estimate; it needs its own
structural statement proof.

At a stack action whose current stack length is `l`, let `l'` be its length
after that action. Starting at its `go` label at the bottom, the simulator takes
`l` walking steps, one action step, `l'` return steps, and one bottom-return
step that resumes the translated remainder. The subtotal is `l+l'+2`.
For push, peek, and pop this is respectively `2*l+3`, `2*l+2`, and
`l+(l-1)+2`, where natural subtraction handles empty pop. Thus each such
subtotal is at most `2*(W+A)+3`. The initial normal step contributes one.
The proposed uniform one-TM2-step simulation bound is therefore

`1 + A * (2*(W+A) + 3)`.

First establish the exact walking counts by strengthening the existing
`tr_respects_aux₁` and `tr_respects_aux₃` induction arguments to actual iterates
or `EvalsToInTime`. Reuse the already proved stack/tape transformation from
`tr_respects_aux₂`. Then structurally combine them through the actual selected
statement branch and retain the same `TrCfg` endpoint. Do not derive a timed
claim merely by forgetting the path length in `Reaches`.

For an actual TM2 run of at most `T` transitions whose every boundary
configuration has at most `W` cells, compose the typed timed simulation values
to obtain the conservative bound

`T * (1 + A * (2*(W+A) + 3))`.

For fixed program constant `A` and already proved polynomial functions `T(n)`
and `W(n)`, this expression is a polynomial in the encoded input length.
The actual endpoint must be the translated successful halted configuration.
Keep inner halted labels distinct from an additional step returning outer
`none`, and preserve the actual output list throughout.

#### Remaining representation and machine obligations

The translated alphabet is the finite product of a bottom-marker bit and one
optional symbol from each finite stack alphabet. The translated syntactic
label type contains arbitrary continuations, so use the actual finite support
constructed by `trSupp` and proved closed by `tr_supports`; do not assume that
the whole unrestricted syntax type is finite. Any finite-support restriction
must be connected to the exact executed translation by a commuting-step proof.

The bottom encoding `trInit` reverses the TM2 input within the tape
representation. A new encoding convention is not by itself an executed
conversion from the required raw binary language. Account for initialization,
finite symbol coding, representation conversion and output cleanup in the
eventual formal computational-model/NP correspondence. The complete verifier
still needs all of its actual parser, rotation, equality, streaming and adapter
