#### 1. Fixed representation and actual control boundaries

Write E=0, N=1, S=2, Z=3, O=4, I=5 as elements of the existing sixteen-tag
alphabet. Let C(t) be the literal preorder `treeCode t`, B(bs) the forward
`bitTags bs`, and

    W(s,t,bs) = C(s) ++ [S] ++ C(t) ++ [S] ++ B(bs) ++ [I].

The stack interface has seven owned stacks: raw, source output, target output,
tree reverse, pending Unit tokens, fuel Bool, and bits reverse Bool. A finite
dependent family of caller stacks is protected. In particular, the certificate
can be any one of those stacks, with arbitrary contents, before the input parser
runs. Every full-entry theorem starts with the six non-raw owned stacks empty.
The two temporary fields may initially be stale, and the arbitrary finite caller
register value must be preserved. The program and actual caller bodies are fixed
before raw data, protected stacks, or register values are quantified.

Use two actual tree destinations. Source/success executes the first separator
block itself; target/success executes the second separator block itself;
target/failure executes the restoreSep1 push itself. Source/failure is already
the complete parser's live failure exit. A separate external label is the live
success exit. These aliases are essential to the fixed counts. Do not insert an
extra transition at a tree return, erase one by a free reconfiguration, or treat
the target tree's failure label as the complete parser's first exit.

The twelve additional phase labels are bitsScan, bitsEmit, eof, restoreEnd,
fuelUndo, bitsUndo, restoreSep2, targetToReverse, targetToRaw, restoreSep1,
sourceToReverse and sourceToRaw. With h protected stacks and q extra caller
labels, the explicit nested-sum representation therefore has 7+h stacks and
27+q labels: ten tree phases, four tree-result labels, twelve additional phases,
one separate success label and q additional caller labels. Exactly25 labels are
owned by the full parser. The register cardinality remains34 times that of the
caller register type; no Bool register is added. Bool observations are encoded
in the same Option Tag temporary using the existing finite bitTag map.

Concrete finite clients should use two different protected alphabets, one Bool
and one Tag, a Bool caller register initially true, and both temporary fields
initially present. With one extra caller label this gives9 stacks,28 labels and
68 register values. Prove actual Fintype instances and these cardinalities;
printing a type abbreviation is not a finite-instance check.

#### 2. Exact endpoint oracle

The independently fixed value oracle is the existing `parseInputRun`, whose
actual source sequencing is tree, separator, tree, separator, bits, EOF.
For every raw word:

* Success is possible exactly when raw is W(s,t,bs). Its first live endpoint has
  raw empty, source C(s), target C(t), fuel exactly bs, and tree reverse, pending
  and bits reverse empty. The bit list itself is retained, including high zeros.
* Failure restores the entire original raw word and leaves all six non-raw owned
  stacks empty. Neither a completed earlier tree nor accepted bits may remain.
* Both cases reset both temporaries and preserve every protected stack and the
  caller register. The arbitrary caller body has not yet executed.

Use the actual returned source values and tails in order; independent existential
decompositions of an unrelated word are not adequate hypotheses. The main theorem
must exhibit an actual iterate of the installed finite program to this endpoint.
Prove both the source-result iff and the exact-code iff, using the existing
source soundness/injectivity results rather than weakening syntax to equal-sized
trees or normalized numeric fuel.

#### 3. Independently derived transition counts

Let Ls=|C(s)|, Lt=|C(t)| and b=|bs|. A successful tree component costs2L+2. A
rollback of a completed output uses two actual transfer loops and both empty
probes, costing2L+2. Each separator/restore block costs one. A bits scan through
I costs b+1; bits emission including its empty probe costs b+1; EOF costs one.

| Outcome | Exact transitions from full entry | Derivation boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Success | 2Ls+2Lt+2b+9 | Both tree runs, both separator blocks, scan, emission, EOF |
| First-tree failure | 2k+p+4 | Existing tree failure, including init and cleanup |
| First separator failure | 4Ls+5 | Source run, failed probe, two rollback loops |
| Target-tree failure | 4Ls+2k+p+10 | Source run, first separator, target failure, restoreS, source rollback |
| Second separator failure | 4Ls+4Lt+11 | Both completed trees, failed probe, both rollbacks and restoreS |
| Bits fail before I | 4Ls+4Lt+2b+14 | Accepted-bit rollback, both separators restored, both trees rolled back |
| Nonempty raw after I | 4Ls+4Lt+4b+18 | RestoreI, two bit reversals, both separators and trees restored |

In a failed tree, k is the accepted incomplete prefix length and p its positive
remaining slots. This is a represented failure decomposition, not a variable
chosen after observing a desired count. The tree component's alternative exact
`runSteps` form is useful for connecting the actual failed target run directly:
the whole count there is4Ls + Tree.runSteps(targetStartRaw) +6.

For successful raw length M, the count is2M+3, equivalently
4*s.numNodes+4*t.numNodes+2b+13. Every raw word must return within4M+7.
Two independent sharp families are C(s)++[S] (target missing), and
C(s)++[S]++C(t) (second separator missing). The exact corresponding counts are
4Ls+11 and4Ls+4Lt+11, equal to4M+7 in each family. These are real executions
to failure with complete restoration; a numerical inequality alone is not the
sharpness witness.

#### 5. Generalized transfers and intermediate orientations

The producer should expose generalized actual loops over arbitrary accumulator
and unread-tail values, before specializing them to complete-entry invariants.

* bitsEmit from reverse r and fuel f ends with r.reverse++f. Its count is|r|+1

  to raw. Show both intermediate orientations on NNEEE and NENEE and an arbitrary

the transfer's empty probe has not executed; at j=length+1 it has. The label and

Define baseCells as the sum of the six owned non-pending stack lengths, and U as

and is empty outside active tree phases. Consequently every such configuration
has at most2M+U+1 actual cells. Include the live endpoint and transition0.

### Open binary front end and actual parser composition: next preparation

Prepared by root after the complete tree component and before complete input
parser implementation is finished. This is a mathematical construction plan,
not implemented Lean, an executed machine, an independent review, an acceptance
receipt, or a qualification. Requirements1–8 and all subsequent verifier and

already fixed InputParserMachine.next.md; it does not replace it. The input
machine currently being authored retains its independently fixed contracts.

#### 1. Reading and exact boundary

The maintained closed BitPairFraming and BitDecoderMachine definitions, their
generalized phase iterates and exact run counts, the full fixed input-machine
plan, the actual verifyBitsRun sequencing, the fuel-dispatch statements and
the pinned TM2.Stmt/stepAux/step definitions were read. No claim of reading the
whole textbook, whole preparation paper, or all quantitative simulator proofs
is made here. The current closed bodies stay unchanged. Their result stacks
have Option markers; the complete input parser instead needs a real Tag stack.
Removing those markers by a logical projection is not a runtime operation.

The selected route is to add open counterparts of the existing finite framing
and decoder algorithms, with ordinary Bool/Tag output stacks and live caller
exits. Their transfer and empty-probe transitions remain real. Source recognition
continues to use the existing unframe and unpackWordRun definitions. A second
decoder invocation runs only after input parsing succeeds. Framing physically
moves certificate bits; this must not be described as leaving those bits wholly
unobserved from the original framed input. The intended order property is that
input decoding and parsing do not semantically decode or alter the certificate
bit stack returned by framing.

#### 2. Open framing, with two actual output stacks

Use five owned Bool stacks: raw framed input, firstReverse, certReverse,
inputBits and certBits; protect an arbitrary finite dependent caller family.
Use the same five phases scanPrefix, copyCert, emitCert, emitFirst, clearFirst,
two live exits success/failure, and arbitrary caller labels. The finite state
is Option Bool times a preserved caller register. Thus there are5+h stack
identifiers,7+q labels and3*|R| register values. Initial raw is arbitrary and
the other four owned stacks are empty. Stale local register values are allowed.

Every block uses only the finite observed bit. The current scanPrefix and
copyCert algorithms remain literal: false consumes its following value bit and
pushes it to firstReverse; true begins copying the complete actual certificate
tail into certReverse. EOF/dangling false enters clearFirst. emitCert transfers
one Bool to certBits, and its empty probe jumps to emitFirst. emitFirst transfers
one Bool to inputBits, and its empty probe resets local state and jumps to live
success. clearFirst pops each prefix bit; its empty probe resets and jumps to
live failure. Neither output receives a marker. No implicit halt or extra
dispatch transition is introduced.

For an initial raw word z and the unchanged existing runSteps z, require an
actual iterate to the following full configuration:

- unframe z=some(i,c): raw and both reverse stacks empty, inputBits=i,
  certBits=c, local register reset, protected context/caller state unchanged,
  and the live success label before any caller body executes.
- unframe z=none: all five owned stacks empty, reset local register,
  protected context/caller state unchanged, and live failure.

Exact success time is2|i|+2|c|+4. Missing delimiter and dangling final guard
after escaped prefix p both cost2|p|+2. Every raw z costs at most2|z|+2.
These are the existing closed algorithm's transition counts: replacing a marker
push/halt inside a finite final statement by reset/goto leaves one transition,
but this equivalence still needs an actual proof for the new statements.

Generalized phase lemmas retain arbitrary old inputBits/certBits separately.
The output of emitCert is r.reverse++oldCert; emitFirst is p.reverse++oldInput.
copyCert from raw c and certReverse r leads to r.reverse++c++oldCert after
its real copy/emit phases; firstReverse and its output remain explicit. The
generalized full scan requires certReverse empty, just as the old algorithm
requires its own condition. Failure must preserve old outputs rather than erase
them. Do not misstate the complete-entry empty outputs as a universal invariant
of arbitrary intermediate configurations.

All owned physical transitions are nonincreasing in total stack cells: an
escaped scan consumes two and pushes one, successful delimiter consumption
removes one, copies and emits move one, and failure cleanup deletes one. There
are no newly allocated marker cells. Therefore every reached prefix through
first live return has cells<=|z|+U at clean entry, including z=[] and step0.
The old closed N+1 sharp-marker example is not a counterexample to this new
open contract because the new program never creates that marker. Preserve both
old and new contracts rather than changing the old theorem.

Prove a positive exact rank for all owned phase states, one-step decrease,
inclusive first-return prefixes, temporary reset after positive prefixes,
caller/context independence and actual Type-valued timed data. No bound is
asserted after unrestricted caller execution.

#### 3. Open four-bit decoder

Use three owned stacks inputBits:Bool, reverse:Tag and output:Tag, plus protected
caller stacks. The phases remain scan, emit, clear; add two live exits and caller
labels. Keep exactly the existing four Option Bool fields and Option Tag field,
paired with caller state. Finite counts are3+h stacks,5+q labels and1377*|R|
register values, because3^4*17=1377. Quantify the finite program before input.

The four-pop scan block and finite nibble callback remain the actual existing

partial input bits really are consumed by the bounded scan statement.

The pinned TM2.Stmt has push, peek, pop, load, branch, goto and halt, with

- load g p uses r o g o r^-1.
- branch b p q uses b o r^-1 and the two translated finite branches.

#### 1. Physical presentation and proposed public API

Use the completed `TreeParserMachine` directly, abbreviated below as `Tree`.
There is no stack/label translation and no independent second tree program.

```lean
inductive TreeSide | source | target
inductive ExtraStack | fuel | bitsReverse
inductive Phase
  | bitsScan | bitsEmit | eof | restoreEnd | fuelUndo | bitsUndo
  | restoreSep2 | targetToReverse | targetToRaw | restoreSep1
  | sourceToReverse | sourceToRaw

abbrev StackId K := Tree.StackId TreeSide (ExtraStack ⊕ K)
abbrev Label Λ := Tree.Label TreeSide (Phase ⊕ (Unit ⊕ Λ))
abbrev Registers R := Tree.Registers R
abbrev External Λ := Tree.Result ⊕ Λ
```

`extraAlphabet Γ` assigns Bool to either ExtraStack and Γ k to a protected k.
The full alphabet is literally `Tree.alphabet TreeSide (extraAlphabet Γ)`.
Give every extra alphabet its finite instance, together with the two finite
enums and twelve-phase finite instance. This retains 7+h stacks, 27+q labels
and 34·|R| register values. In the eventual finite package, all index, label,
register and protected alphabet types are chosen finite before arbitrary data.

```text

```

Here `outputs : TreeSide → Word`; a public `treeOutputs source target` helper
supplies the two literal output words. This presentation makes generalized

return configurations definitionally accessible. `cfg` is a `Tree.cfg` with
the extended context mapping fuel/bitsReverse/protected k to their actual
lists. The data lists remain configuration stacks, never finite registers.

Expose stack identifiers, `treeLabel d phase`, `treeResultLabel d result`,

result labels are source/failure and the separate Unit success label. Keep

`handler caller` is the actual Tree external handler:

* target/success executes sep2;

* source/failure executes the supplied full failure caller body;
* an additional phase label executes its phase body;

`program caller := Tree.program (handler caller)`, and `step`/`next` use the
same Tree transition and optional lift. Thus completed Tree execution theorems
apply to the actual combined program by choosing this very handler. There is
no free data relocation or extra routing transition at a tree result.

Define `FullOwned` by label cases: every tree phase, the three nonterminal
tree results, and all twelve additional phases are owned. Source/failure,

#### 2. Literal additional statement bodies

Reuse `Tree.reset`, `Tree.jump` and `Tree.storeTag`. Define
`storeBit regs value := Tree.storeTag regs (value.map bitTag)`.
After an actual Bool pop, the finite readback comparison with
`some bitOneTag` recovers the Bool. No extra Bool temporary is introduced.

The separator bodies peek raw into the tag field. On S they pop that actual
cell and jump directly to target/init or bitsScan; otherwise they jump to
sourceToReverse or targetToReverse without consuming raw.

bitsScan peeks raw, recognizes Z/O, pops the actual tag and pushes its finite
Bool onto bitsReverse, then repeats. On I it pops I and goes to bitsEmit. On
EOF/foreign it leaves raw unchanged and goes to bitsUndo. All branch operands
are overwritten finite observations. The order of the surrounding source
components remains tree, separator, tree, separator, bits, EOF.

bitsEmit pops bitsReverse, stores its mapped finite observation, and pushes
the recovered Bool onto fuel; its empty probe goes to EOF. fuelUndo similarly
transfers fuel onto bitsReverse; its empty probe goes to bitsUndo. bitsUndo
pops bitsReverse and pushes the mapped bitTag onto raw; its empty probe goes
to restoreSep2. EOF peeks raw and goes to full success only if empty;
otherwise it goes to restoreEnd. restoreEnd pushes I and goes to fuelUndo.

Use finite parameterized statement helpers for output rollback, with d fixed
in the label. `toReverseBlock d nextLabel` pops output d and pushes the actual
tag onto treeReverse; its empty probe goes to that destination's toRaw phase.
`toRawBlock nextLabel` pops treeReverse and pushes the actual tag onto raw;
its empty probe goes to restoreSep1 for target, or full failure for source.
restoreSep1 and restoreSep2 each push one real S and jump to the corresponding
output rollback phase. Every goto resets the existing two temporary fields.

Each block consists solely of finite pop/peek/push/load/branch/goto structure.
No callback mentions source trees, word/list reversal, lengths, parser results,
the proof-side count below, or an unbounded loop. Each repeated transfer is an

#### 6. A concrete local invariant for all reached space bounds

Let baseCells sum raw, treeReverse, both output lengths, fuel and bitsReverse.
Pending is excluded. Define debt by the fixed finite label table, including
the literal tree-result aliases and the two full exits. Then for every owned
step, regardless of stale temporaries and dirty other stores:

```text
baseCells after + debt after.l = baseCells before + debt before.l.
```

Proof uses the real one-step equations. A transfer conserves baseCells; each
separator/I consumption increases debt by one; each actual restore push
decreases debt by one. The alias target/failure has debt1 before its push and
sourceToReverse has debt0 afterward. This exact conservation is independent
of semantic parsing, and includes the final live states.

To control pending uniformly, a useful reached-state invariant `PendingControl M`
is slightly stronger than the final pending≤M+1 consequence:

* at either tree init: pending=[];
* at a tree scan: pending.length + raw.length ≤ M+1;
* at a tree emit: pending=[];
* at tree undo or dropPending: pending.length ≤ M+1;
* at every other full label, including results/exits: pending=[].

Combine it with `baseCells+debt=M`. Init pushes one token; raw.length≤M follows
from nonnegative other cells/debt, so the next scan inequality holds. A node
scan increases pending by one and decreases raw by one. An empty scan decreases
both where applicable; its emit branch explicitly has empty pending tail.
The rejection branch gives the undo bound directly. Undo does not change pending;
dropPending decreases it and its empty probe has pending=[] at the result.
The sole additional transition into target/init comes from source/success,
where pending is empty. All other additional phases preserve an empty pending
stack. Thus this invariant is inductive on actual FullOwned steps.

This avoids an invalid assertion that pending+raw is nonincreasing during
rollback: raw grows during undo, and only pending≤M+1 is retained there.

then fails on its push. These are proof-side phase cases, not extra entry
requirements or runtime checks.

hold. Every Runs prefix preserves them, giving baseCells+debt=M and pending≤M+1.

including transition0 and full handoff. Pending is empty outside active tree
phases as requested.

#### 5. Static finite-statement transport

The pinned TM2.Stmt has push, peek, pop, load, branch, goto and halt, with
stepAux executing a finite body until goto/halt. There is no supplied general
TM2 statement-renaming theorem among the inspected modules. A small transport
helper is justified by the concrete framing, two decoder, input and fuel clients;
do not introduce a parser framework or an unrelated abstract execution oracle.

Use a bijection e between a component's complete finite stack identifiers
(including its arbitrary protected family) and the complete ambient identifiers,
symbol equivalences a_k:Gamma(k) equiv Gamma'(e k), a register equivalence r,
and an injective label map f. In the concrete layout symbols have the same
Bool/Tag/Unit meanings; a_k are identities after the finite case split. The
protected family fills every other ambient stack, so no anonymous absent stack
or default value is silently inserted into the configuration.

Define the translated finite syntax structurally:

- push k g p becomes push(e k)(a_k o g o r^-1)(translate p).
- peek/pop k g p observe Option of the target symbol, convert that one option
  with a_k^-1, apply g to r^-1 of the register, then re-encode with r.
- load g p uses r o g o r^-1.
- branch b p q uses b o r^-1 and the two translated finite branches.
- goto g uses f o g o r^-1; halt stays halt.

The logical map of configurations has label Option.map f, register r, and the
same physical stack contents expressed at e k with List.map a_k. This is a
compile-time representation relation, not a TM2 instruction or a free transfer
between distinct physical stacks. Prove dependent stack-update compatibility,
head?/tail compatibility, then stepAux commuting by structural induction on
the actual finite Stmt. Derive the step/Option-iterate/time/prefix/cell results
under the exact installed-body agreement at every mapped label. Injectivity of
f distinguishes original states and first exits. A full label equivalence can
be used when convenient; do not assume mapped bodies agree without proving it.

For an open component, ambient bodies at live exits may differ from its local
caller presentation. Either instantiate the component caller with the actual
ambient continuation before transport, or use its first-owned-prefix theorem
and prove installed-body agreement only while that prefix is owned. An all-time
commuting statement with only owned-body hypotheses would be false after the
caller runs. The literal returned mapped configuration must equal the next
component's actual entry; prove every stack/register/label field of that equality.

This transport preserves actual transition count and cell count. It does not
identify stacks that hold different data, turn an Option Tag into a Tag for
free, discard output markers, reset a register, or erase a real empty probe.
The open variants avoid markers by different explicit finite statements.

The actual installed order is:
framing; complete input decoding; full input parsing; complete certificate
decoding; live decoded-certificate fuel-inspection entry. Every earlier failure
goes to the shared rejection handoff before later semantic stages run. Input
syntax permits unequal tree sizes; syntax is not rotation legality. Certificate
decoding remains eager once input parsing succeeds, including any final partial
block after otherwise valid certificate tokens.

Let i,c be the actual fields returned by unframe z, and let w be the actual
word returned by input decoding. Write F=2|i|+2|c|+4 and D(b)=2*(|b|/4)+2.
Require actual same-program iterates and Type-valued timed records for:

| Outcome | Exact first front-end exit count |
|---|---|
| Framing failure | Existing framing runSteps z |
| Input decoder failure | F+D(i) |
| Input parser failure | F+D(i)+Input.inputSteps w |
| Certificate decoder failure | F+D(i)+Input.inputSteps w+D(c) |
| All four stages succeed | The same sum, at actual fuel inspection entry |

The later rows require the actual preceding success equations and returned
values. They may not choose independent decompositions to manufacture a count.
The initial register state, reset fields and protected stacks must be threaded
through the same endpoints. EvalsToInTime.trans uses the second bound plus the
first in its result; normalize the arithmetic explicitly without altering the
intermediate configuration or transition function.

For fully encoded fields i=wordBits(inputCode s t bs), c=wordBits moves, let
M=|inputCode s t bs| and W=|moves|. Then |z|=8M+4W+1, the input parse succeeds
in2M+3, and the front end reaches fuel inspection in exactly12M+10W+11
transitions. This includes framing8M+8W+4, input decoding2M+2, input parsing
2M+3 and certificate decoding2W+2. It does not yet execute the inspection,
decrement, move parsing, rotation, equality or final cleanup.

A coarse uniform bound sufficient for later polynomial composition is8N+13
for N=|z|: framing<=2N+2, each reached decoder<=N+2, and input parsing<=4N+7.
Skipped stages only reduce the upper bound. All these sizes follow from the
actual returned field/decoded-word length equations; prove those equations
instead of assuming arbitrary component inputs have length<=N.

During input decoding/parsing, the certificateBits stack is literally the same
c returned by framing. On an input failure its entire contents remain unchanged,
even if c ends with a partial nibble. An actual next-step rejection caller can
start deleting c for cleanup; that deletion is not semantic decoding and lies

#### 7. All-prefix physical workspace across the front end

With clean owned entry and outside protected storage U, target the inclusive
first-front-end-return bound N+U on all actual reached configurations. Framing
is nonincreasing. Its success endpoint has |i|+|c| owned cells. Input decoding
is nonincreasing, returning M+|c| when |i|=4M. During input parsing, the existing
component gives2M+|c|+U+1, and

    2M+|c|+1 <= 8M+|c|+1 = |frame (wordBits w) c| = N.

Thus even an empty decoded input with its one pending token fits the original
framed length; this is not an assertion that the raw Tag parser itself never
allocates. At success, the three consumed syntax delimiters leave M-3 cells
in source/target/fuel, and all input scratch is empty. Certificate decoding then
only decreases total cells. Its real output and the preserved tree/fuel fields
give the next dispatch entry. Frame/decoder temporary state is finite control
and not an uncharged unbounded store.

Prove the space statement by splitting actual global prefixes at the actual
component handoffs and transporting their existing proofs through the proved
configuration equivalences. At a boundary use the same actual reached state,
not independent existential witnesses. The bound includes the live exits but
excludes arbitrary future callers. At the global initial configuration equality
N+U holds, so that bound is sharp already at transition0. Final Boolean-output
cleanup may create one cell even when N=0, and must use its own appropriate
bound, such as N+U+1. Do not silently extend the open front-end bound through it.

### Independent mathematical check of the proposed open binary front end

#### Result and evidence boundary

The final two preparation drafts have consistent physical layouts, generalized
endpoints, exact phase ranks, branch clocks and prefix-space arithmetic within
the scope checked here. I found one incorrect case description and one mismatch
between the two drafts' stated generality. Root corrected both before release;
I independently verified that reversing just those intended edits recovers the
exact original hashes. No remaining numerical or orientation counterexample was
found. This is a mathematical preparation check by the existing helper, **not a
Standards or Spec review, a Lean proof, a build, source acceptance or qualification**.

The checked final inputs are:

| `FrontEndComposition.cases.next.md` | 18,510 | `c431fe3a994a88bdaab2224c916a29b2502c566b1aa5843dcc8295895022c9a1` |

#### Corrections found and independently rechecked

**Decoder case wording.** The original cases draft called the `2/3/4` sentinel
clock an “Empty failure.” Empty decoder input succeeds after two transitions;
nonempty inputs of length one, two or three fail after two. The corrected case
now says “Nonempty short-input failure2/3/4.” The three numbers mean first live
failure, a present halted configuration after its caller executes, then outer
`none`. Replacing only the corrected phrase by the old phrase reconstructs all
18,495 original bytes and SHA-256
`3eaaea46f78b15108932a98c8b7a2b9f60862fc509cae7dd4d3ca5a8df95af84`.

**Generalized framing scope.** The original main draft restricted its generalized
scan theorem to empty certificate reverse storage. The new cases draft correctly
required the stronger theorem for arbitrary old first and certificate reverse
stacks. Root retained the ordinary clean specialization and explicitly added the
stronger success/failure endpoints and counts. Replacing only the edited paragraph
by the originally read paragraph reconstructs all 22,852 original bytes and SHA-256
`3496311df71acadb9a4cd215866d5817043124ab54f09902d3ed4fa86ae86ed6`.
This strengthens the exposed dirty-state contract; it changes none of the fixed
full-input-parser expectations.

For clarity in implementation, the finite `BitDecoderMachine.nibble` is permitted
reuse: its actual definition calls the four-Boolean `decodeTagRun`, whose domain
has sixteen inputs. The prohibition on a source-decoder oracle concerns the
unbounded whole-word `unpackWordRun`, not this bounded finite callback. No additional
draft edit is needed to establish the numerical conclusions below.

#### 1. Physical representations and finite cardinalities

The open framing algorithm has five Bool stacks: raw, first reverse, certificate
reverse, input output and certificate output. Its five phases, two live results,
and one `Option Bool` temporary give `5+h` stacks, `7+q` labels and `3|R|`
register values. The open decoder has Bool input and two Tag stacks, three phases,
two results, four `Option Bool` fields and one `Option Tag`. Its corresponding
counts are `3+h`, `5+q` and `3^4·17|R| = 1377|R|`. These formulas require the
stated finite index/label/register families when packaged as a finite machine.

The proposed global store has fourteen distinct stacks, with exactly the alphabets
specified in the draft. The seven parser-owned stacks are input raw, source,
target, tree reverse, pending, fuel and bits reverse. The other seven global
stacks form part of that component's protected family. No stack is omitted from
the transport, and pending is eligible for later fuel borrowing only at a proved
empty parser endpoint.

The global register is `Tree.Temporaries × Decoder.Registers × R`. Its size is
`(17·2)·(3^4·17)|R| = 46818|R|`. Framing and fuel may borrow decoder field `b0`:
the remaining fields form a finite caller register of size `15606|R|`, and
`3·15606 = 46818`. Their reset preserves that caller component. A decoder resets
its five fields and preserves the tree pair; the input parser resets the tree
pair and preserves all decoder fields. Thus early framing failure can retain
stale unborrowed fields, whereas full success has actually traversed all the
needed resets. No hidden clean-register premise is necessary.

For the fixed two-protected-stack, Bool-register, one-external-label clients:

| Component | Stack identifiers | Labels | Register states |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Open framer | 7 | 8 | 6 |
| Open decoder | 5 | 6 | 2,754 |
| Full front end | 16 | 39 | 93,636 |

These are cardinality calculations, not yet `Fintype.card` theorems about future
Lean types. The old closed machines retain their Option-marker result conventions;
no representation theorem makes marker removal or a physical stack copy free.

#### 2. Generalized framing endpoints and all-owned-state rank

Write `r` and `s` for the initial first/certificate reverse lists and `a,b` for
the initial output suffixes. Scanning `frame(i,c)` pushes the input prefix above
`r` and the certificate above `s`. The final actual outputs are consequently

```
input output       = reverse r ++ i ++ a
certificate output = reverse s ++ c ++ b.
```

Raw and both reverse stacks are empty. The exact count is
`2|i| + 2|c| + |r| + |s| + 4`. For malformed `escapeBits p` or
`escapeBits p ++ [false]`, no certificate-copy phase is reached. Cleanup empties
raw and first reverse in `2|p| + |r| + 2` transitions, preserving `s,a,b`
literally. In particular, the clean theorem must not be used to erase dirty `s`.
For raw `[true]` and initial certificate reverse `[false,true]`, the actual
certificate output is `[true,false]` and the count is six, rather than the clean
four. This is a concrete separator for the missing clean-entry premise.

The cases draft's proof-side rank is correct on **all** configurations at owned
labels, including arbitrary list contents and stale temporaries:

| Phase | Rank |
|---|---|
| `scanPrefix` | `F(raw)+|r|+(if unframe raw is some then |s| else 0)` |
| `copyCert` | `2|raw|+|s|+|r|+3` |
| `emitCert` | `|s|+|r|+2` |
| `emitFirst`, `clearFirst` | `|r|+1` |
| Any nonowned label, including halt | `0` |

Here `F` is the existing framing `runSteps`. On a false/value pair,
`F(false::value::tail)=F(tail)+2`, while first reverse gains one cell; the rank
therefore falls by one. On a delimiter, the target `copyCert` rank is exactly one
less. On EOF or a dangling false, the source rank is `|r|+2` and the clear rank is
`|r|+1`; the dirty certificate term is absent in precisely this branch. A copy
decreases raw by one and increases certificate reverse by one, so its coefficient
two again gives a decrease of one. Empty probes and both transfer/cleanup phases
satisfy the same equation. All owned ranks are positive, and rank zero at a live
local result precedes any caller transition.

Every owned framing transition weakly decreases stack cells. On dirty entries
the bound must include every old owned cell; on clean entry it is `|raw|+U`.
The actual old `jump` resets its temporary on every transition, not only on the
last one. The new program needs the corresponding explicit reset/goto bodies to
justify the required positive-prefix reset theorem. Zero transitions retain the
incoming temporary. These facts follow from the inspected finite blocks, not
from counting logical source events.

#### 3. Decoder endpoints, rank and source-work distinction

Let `m = floor(|raw|/4)`. The scan performs `m` complete-nibble transitions and one
terminal scan transition. Emit or clear then performs `m+|r|` transfers/deletions
and one empty probe. Hence a generalized scan costs `2m+|r|+2`. On success with
decoded word `w`, it returns `reverse r ++ w ++ o`; on a final partial nibble it
returns the old output `o`, with raw and reverse empty. It does not emit the
success marker used by the old closed machine.

The rank `2 floor(|raw|/4)+|r|+2` at scan, `|r|+1` at emit/clear, and zero elsewhere
is positive exactly at owned labels. Consuming four bits decreases the quotient
by one and increases reverse length by one; the rank drops by one. An empty or
one-to-three-bit terminal scan has quotient zero and moves to rank `|r|+1`.
Transfers, deletion and empty probes account for every remaining transition.
No divisibility premise is needed for this all-raw rank or count.

The source `unpackWordRun` tariff is different: `4|w|+2` on success and `2|w|+2`
on a complete-word prefix followed by a nonempty partial nibble. The machine count
is `2|w|+2` in both cases. The actual four-pop statement overwrites each field
before consulting it; its finite nibble callback is only reached after all four
pops succeed. All sixteen tags, including reserved tags, are decoded. Grammar
meaning is deferred to the later parser.

The concrete dirty decoder case is correct: old reverse `[5,9]`, old output
`[15,2]`, and encoded word `[3,12]` yield `[9,5,3,12,15,2]` after eight transitions.
Appending either specified short suffix instead yields `[15,2]` after eight.
The explicit bit strings decode to 3 and 12 in little-endian order. Nonempty
partial endings are consumed, not retained as a suffix.

#### 4. Installed composition and label-map obligations

The thirty-six globally owned labels consist of 25 input-parser labels, five
framing labels, three input-decoder labels and three certificate-decoder labels.
The old input success label becomes certificate scan; it is counted once. Global
rejection and fuel-inspection entry are the two exits, giving `38+q` labels.
The three intermediate success handoffs are **globally owned** even though each
is a rank-zero local exit for the preceding component. A local first-return
theorem alone must not identify them with final front-end termination.

One explicit way to keep each component's complete label map injective is to
take its remaining ambient labels as its caller-label family:

| Component | Local phase/result labels | Required caller complement |
|---|---:|---:|
| Framer | 7 | `31+q` |
| Input decoder | 5 | `33+q` |
| Full input parser | 27 | `11+q` |
| Certificate decoder | 5 | `33+q` |

For instance, the framer's success maps to input-decoder scan and its failure to
global rejection. Neither can also occur in that framer's caller complement.
The input parser maps success to certificate scan and failure to rejection; its
complement contains the five framing phases, three input-decoder phases, the two
other certificate-decoder phases, and inspection entry, plus external labels.
Sharing a rejection destination **between different component maps** is harmless;
identifying two labels within one required injection is not.

The complete stack complements have sizes `9+h` for framing, `11+h` for either
decoder, and `7+h` for the input parser. Static equivalences must include those
protected stacks and their current values. Finite reorderings of stacks and
register fields are legitimate; moving a nonempty list between different physical
stores is not a static equivalence.

The proposed structural translation of `push`, `peek`, `pop`, `load`, `branch`,
`goto` and `halt` is mathematically sound with its stated maps. For peek/pop the
actual target observation is converted using `Option.map a_k.symm`, the source
update is evaluated at `r.symm` of the target register, and its result is mapped
back by `r`. Dependent stack updates require the actual index-equivalence/cast
lemmas. Stack lengths are preserved because symbol maps preserve list length and
the complete stack-index map is a bijection.

The future proof must establish `stepAux` commutation by induction on the finite
statement, then actual `step` and optional-iterate commutation under installed
body agreement. For all-time transport, agreement is needed at every mapped
label. With agreement only on owned bodies, use the first-owned-prefix theorem
or instantiate the actual caller; a caller that pushes then halts distinguishes
the invalid all-time claim immediately. Each mapped return configuration must
equal the next actual entry in every field. No reset, empty probe, marker removal
or physical transfer may be supplied merely by that equality.

#### 5. Exact branch clocks and literal cases

For actual `unframe z = some(i,c)`, let `F=2|i|+2|c|+4` and
`D(b)=2 floor(|b|/4)+2`. The branch sums are correct: framing failure uses its
own `runSteps`; input decoding failure uses `F+D(i)`; input parse failure adds
the actual `Input.inputSteps w`; certificate decoding failure and full success
both add `D(c)`. Every later row needs the actual prior returned values and
success equations. No certificate decoder runs on either input failure.

For `i=wordBits(inputCode s t bs)` and `c=wordBits moves`, put
`M=|inputCode s t bs|` and `W=|moves|`. Encoding gives

```
N = 2*(4M) + 4W + 1 = 8M + 4W + 1
T = (8M+8W+4) + (2M+2) + (2M+3) + (2W+2)
  = 12M + 10W + 11.
```

This ends at live inspection entry. It excludes inspection itself, fuel
predecessor work, move parsing, rotation, tree equality and final cleanup.

| Case | Framed length | Framing | Input decode | Input parse | Certificate decode | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Nil/nil, empty fuel and certificate | 41 | 44 | 12 | 13 | 2 | 71 |
| Two-node input, one fuel bit, actual root-right `[7,10]` | 121 | 132 | 30 | 31 | 6 | 199 |
| Same input, certificate Word `[15]` | 117 | 124 | 30 | 31 | 4 | 189 |
| One input bit, three certificate bits | 6 | 12 | 2 | — | — | 14 |
| Empty input bits, three certificate bits | 4 | 10 | 2 | 5 | — | 17 |
| Valid nil/nil input, three certificate bits | 44 | 50 | 12 | 13 | 2 | 77 |

Both drafts' distinct three-bit certificate examples were checked literally;
their equal lengths give equal clocks, while their returned stacks remain their
different actual lists. Unequal tree sizes remain syntactically admissible.
Certificate `[15]` is decoded successfully but is not a legal move. The existing
closed framing example's 66 output symbols include two markers and do not
describe this open machine's output.

Appending two high zeros to the nonpalindromic fuel `[true,false,false,true,false]`
preserves its numeric value nine but increases its literal length. With nil/nil
trees and certificate `[7,10]`, successful front-end time changes from 151 to 175
and raw length from 89 to 105. With a trailing Tag 15 forcing input EOF rejection,
time changes from 178 to 206 and raw length from 97 to 113. Thus the respective
time increments are **24** and **28**: framing adds 16, input decoding adds four,
and input parsing adds four on success or eight on EOF rejection. Certificate
decode is unchanged or skipped. The source input-parser tariff adds six in both
cases. This preserves the fixed stage-two distinctions rather than identifying
numeric equality, source work and machine time.

For all raw `z`, each reached input/certificate bit field has length at most
`N=|z|`. A reached decoded word has length at most N, using the actual four-bit
length identity. Summing the safe bounds `2N+2`, `N+2`, `4N+7`, `N+2` proves
`T≤8N+13`; skipped stages only remove nonnegative terms. This is deliberately
coarse and makes no successful-parse premise.

#### 6. Prefix space, sequencing and caller clocks

All framing/decoder owned transitions weakly decrease physical cells. During
input parsing, the component's protected space includes the actual certificate
bits, not just the original outside context. If input decoding returned `w` with
length M, then `|i|=4M` and

```
input-prefix cells ≤ 2M + |c| + U + 1
                   ≤ 8M + |c| + U + 1 = N + U.
```

This also covers M=0: the consumed framing delimiter supplies room in the original
bound for the parser's one pending token. On successful input parsing, the two
separators and end marker account for three removed cells, leaving exactly
`M-3` in source, target and fuel. Certificate decoding then only decreases cells.
The composed bound must split actual prefixes at the actual handoffs and keep
the same state at each boundary. It includes final live exits. Equality at step
zero makes `N+U` sharp; it is not an assertion that the raw Tag parser itself is
nonallocating.

Input decoding and parsing preserve certificateBits literally and leave
certificateWord empty. Framing has already traversed and copied those bits, so
“unobserved from the original framed input” would be false. The protected-order
claim is correctly scoped to the post-framing input stages. A rejection caller
may later clear those bits without semantically decoding them.

Pinned `TM2.step` returns `some(stepAux ...)` at a live label, even if the body
ends in `halt`; only a further step from the halted configuration yields outer
`none`. A push-and-halt sentinel therefore gives first-return/present-halt/outer-
none clocks `14/15/16`, `6/7/8`, or `2/3/4` in the specified component cases.
For full nil/nil success the analogous clocks are `71/72/73` if that sentinel is
the installed exit caller. If the actual fuel inspector is installed instead,
its empty-certificate branch reaches live equality entry at 72, with no tree
comparison or Boolean acceptance yet. These are different caller programs.

An allocating caller after front-end failure on raw `[]` increases cells above
the `N+U` bound immediately. A caller that jumps from rejection to a success
label also defeats an eventual-success specification. Both show why ownership
and first return, rather than unrestricted reachability, are essential.
`StateTransition.EvalsToInTime.trans` returns the second bound plus the first;
arithmetic normalization is valid only with the identical transition function
and actual intermediate configuration.

#### 7. Nonformal experiment and remaining implementation work

The accompanying Python experiment executes the proposed framing/decoder blocks
on a shared fourteen-stack store and binds the earlier independently fixed
input-table interpreter to the same seven physical list objects. It uses separate
source functions only as checking oracles, never to choose a machine transition.
It does not execute Lean, the Lean elaborator, or a TM2 interpreter proved correct

/-- Exact first-return count, following the actual source results; never called by a block. -/
def inputSteps (raw : Word) : Nat :=
  match (parseTreeRun raw).1 with
  | none => TreeParserMachine.runSteps raw
  | some (source, afterSource) =>
    match (parseSeparatorRun afterSource).1 with
    | none => 4 * (treeCode source).length + 5
    | some beforeTarget =>
      match (parseTreeRun beforeTarget).1 with
      | none => 4 * (treeCode source).length + TreeParserMachine.runSteps beforeTarget + 6
      | some (target, afterTarget) =>
        match (parseSeparatorRun afterTarget).1 with
        | none => 4 * (treeCode source).length + 4 * (treeCode target).length + 11
        | some beforeBits =>
          match (parseBitsRun beforeBits).1 with
          | none => 4 * (treeCode source).length + 4 * (treeCode target).length +
              2 * bitsConsumed beforeBits + 14
          | some (bs, rest) =>
            if rest = [] then 2 * (treeCode source).length + 2 * (treeCode target).length + 2 * bs.length + 9
            else 4 * (treeCode source).length + 4 * (treeCode target).length + 4 * bs.length + 18

/-- Every raw word follows its actual source-return sequence to the first full live result. -/
theorem run_source_trace (raw : Word) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) :
    Runs caller (inputSteps raw) (entry regs raw ctx) (resultCfg regs raw ctx (parseInputRun raw).1) := by
  simp only [inputSteps, parseInputRun, CallCount.tick, Resources.bind]
  cases first : (parseTreeRun raw).1 with
  | none => exact run_tree_failure_trace caller raw regs ctx first
  | some pair =>
      rcases pair with ⟨source, afterSource⟩
      have rawEq := (parseTreeRun_iff raw source afterSource).mp first
      cases firstSep : (parseSeparatorRun afterSource).1 with
      | none =>
          simpa only [rawEq] using
            run_firstSeparator_failure_trace caller source afterSource regs ctx firstSep
      | some beforeTarget =>
          have firstSepEq := (parseSeparatorRun_iff afterSource beforeTarget).mp firstSep
          cases second : (parseTreeRun beforeTarget).1 with
          | none =>
              simpa only [rawEq, firstSepEq] using
                run_target_failure_trace caller source beforeTarget regs ctx second
          | some pair =>
              rcases pair with ⟨target, afterTarget⟩
              have targetEq := (parseTreeRun_iff beforeTarget target afterTarget).mp second
              cases secondSep : (parseSeparatorRun afterTarget).1 with
              | none =>
                  simpa only [rawEq, firstSepEq, targetEq] using
                    run_secondSeparator_failure_trace caller source target afterTarget regs ctx secondSep
              | some beforeBits =>
                  have secondSepEq := (parseSeparatorRun_iff afterTarget beforeBits).mp secondSep
                  cases threshold : (parseBitsRun beforeBits).1 with
                  | none =>
                      obtain ⟨bs, rest, word, blocked⟩ := parseBitsRun_none_decomposition beforeBits threshold
                      have count : bitsConsumed beforeBits = bs.length := by
                        rw [word, bitsConsumed_of_blocked bs rest blocked]
                      rw [count]
                      simpa only [rawEq, firstSepEq, targetEq, secondSepEq, word] using
                        run_bits_failure_trace caller source target bs rest regs ctx blocked
                  | some pair =>
                      rcases pair with ⟨bs, rest⟩
                      have bitsEq := (parseBitsRun_iff beforeBits bs rest).mp threshold
                      have encoded : raw = inputCode source target bs ++ rest := by
                        rw [rawEq, firstSepEq, targetEq, secondSepEq, bitsEq]
                        simp only [inputCode, List.append_assoc, List.cons_append, List.nil_append]
                      cases rest with
                      | nil =>
                          simp only [List.append_nil] at encoded
                          simpa only [finishInputRun, ite_true, encoded] using
                            run_code_trace caller source target bs regs ctx
                      | cons tag rest =>
                          simpa only [finishInputRun, List.cons_ne_nil, ite_false, encoded] using
                            run_trailing_trace caller source target bs (tag :: rest) regs ctx (by simp)

theorem run_source (raw : Word) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) :
    (next caller)^[inputSteps raw] (some (entry regs raw ctx)) =
      some (resultCfg regs raw ctx (parseInputRun raw).1) :=
  (run_source_trace caller raw regs ctx).iterate caller

theorem run_of_some (raw : Word) (source target : BinaryTree Unit) (bs : Bits)
    (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k))
    (returned : (parseInputRun raw).1 = some (source, target, bs)) :
    (next caller)^[inputSteps raw] (some (entry regs raw ctx)) =
      some (cfg (some (resultLabel .success)) (reset regs) [] [] []
        (treeOutputs (treeCode source) (treeCode target)) bs [] ctx) := by
  rw [run_source, returned]
  rfl

theorem run_of_none (raw : Word) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k))
    (returned : (parseInputRun raw).1 = none) :
    (next caller)^[inputSteps raw] (some (entry regs raw ctx)) =
      some (cfg (some (resultLabel .failure)) (reset regs) raw [] [] (treeOutputs [] []) [] [] ctx) := by
  rw [run_source, returned]
  rfl

theorem run_code (source target : BinaryTree Unit) (bs : Bits) (regs : Registers R)
    (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) :
    (next caller)^[2 * (treeCode source).length + 2 * (treeCode target).length + 2 * bs.length + 9]
      (some (entry regs (inputCode source target bs) ctx)) =
        some (resultCfg regs (inputCode source target bs) ctx (some (source, target, bs))) :=
  (run_code_trace caller source target bs regs ctx).iterate caller

theorem inputSteps_le (raw : Word) : inputSteps raw ≤ 4 * raw.length + 7 := by
  have firstBound := TreeParserMachine.runSteps_le raw
  unfold inputSteps
  cases first : (parseTreeRun raw).1 with
  | none => omega
  | some pair =>
      rcases pair with ⟨source, afterSource⟩
      have sourceLength : raw.length = (treeCode source).length + afterSource.length := by
        rw [(parseTreeRun_iff raw source afterSource).mp first, List.length_append]
      cases firstSep : (parseSeparatorRun afterSource).1 with
      | none => omega
      | some beforeTarget =>
          have firstSepLength := parseSeparatorRun_consumed_length afterSource beforeTarget firstSep
          have targetBound := TreeParserMachine.runSteps_le beforeTarget
          cases second : (parseTreeRun beforeTarget).1 with
          | none => omega
          | some pair =>
              rcases pair with ⟨target, afterTarget⟩
              have targetLength : beforeTarget.length = (treeCode target).length + afterTarget.length := by
                rw [(parseTreeRun_iff beforeTarget target afterTarget).mp second, List.length_append]
              cases secondSep : (parseSeparatorRun afterTarget).1 with
              | none => omega
              | some beforeBits =>
                  have secondSepLength := parseSeparatorRun_consumed_length afterTarget beforeBits secondSep
                  have bitsBound := bitsConsumed_le beforeBits
                  cases threshold : (parseBitsRun beforeBits).1 with
                  | none => omega
                  | some pair =>
                      rcases pair with ⟨bs, rest⟩
                      have bitsLength := parseBitsRun_consumed_length beforeBits bs rest threshold
                      split <;> omega

theorem inputSteps_pos (raw : Word) : 0 < inputSteps raw := by
  have firstPositive := TreeParserMachine.runSteps_pos raw
  unfold inputSteps
  split
  · exact firstPositive
  · split
    · omega
    · split
      · omega
      · split
        · omega
        · split
          · omega
          · split <;> omega

def runInTime (raw : Word) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) :
    StateTransition.EvalsToInTime (step caller) (entry regs raw ctx)
      (some (resultCfg regs raw ctx (parseInputRun raw).1)) (inputSteps raw) where
  steps := inputSteps raw
  evals_in_steps := run_source caller raw regs ctx
  steps_le_m := Nat.le_refl _

def runInLinearTime (raw : Word) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) :
    StateTransition.EvalsToInTime (step caller) (entry regs raw ctx)
      (some (resultCfg regs raw ctx (parseInputRun raw).1)) (4 * raw.length + 7) where
  steps := inputSteps raw
  evals_in_steps := run_source caller raw regs ctx
  steps_le_m := inputSteps_le raw

#### First full result and caller boundary

The indexed Runs relation already records only actual transitions whose start
label is FullOwned. Runs.prefix supplies both the n-step initial trace and the
remaining `inputSteps raw - n` suffix trace. Once run_source_trace is checked,
derive the following public shape, with arbitrary incoming stale registers and
protected context and the six clean nonraw entry stacks built into entry:

```text
run_prefix caller raw regs ctx n (bound : n ≤ inputSteps raw) :
  ∃ reached,
    next caller^[n] (some (entry regs raw ctx)) = some reached ∧
    Runs caller n (entry regs raw ctx) reached ∧
    Runs caller (inputSteps raw-n) reached
      (resultCfg regs raw ctx (parseInputRun raw).1) ∧
    (n < inputSteps raw ↔ FullOwned reached.l)
```

The forward ownership implication is Runs.owned_start applied to the remaining
positive suffix. At equality, the actual endpoint has a nonowned result label.
If the prefix were owned while n is not strictly smaller, bound forces equality
and the endpoint label gives a contradiction. This handles source/success,
target/success and target/failure correctly as nonterminal full-owned labels.

Prove step_caller_independent for arbitrary FullOwned configurations by cases
on the actual label: every such handler branch is fixed and does not invoke
the supplied caller. Induction on Runs then transports the entire exact trace
to another caller. Applying that to the n-step initial trace proves equality
of both actual iterates through the inclusive first handoff. No assertion
about unrestricted later reachability is involved.

`resultCfg regs raw ctx` is injective as a function of Option ParsedInput.
None/some are separated by their distinct actual labels. In the some/some
case, configuration equality gives equality of both literal tree-code outputs
and the literal fuel lists. Those equalities imply equality of the complete
inputCode values; apply the existing parseInputRun_injective to recover both
trees and the bit list. This uses the required source uniqueness result and
does not normalize fuel.

The general firstResult_iff should equate the actual iterate at inputSteps to
resultCfg of an observed Option with equality of the actual parseInputRun value
to that Option. It follows from run_source and resultCfg injectivity. A named
FirstSuccess and the exact inputCode iff are immediate specializations. In
particular, a caller's later jump from failure to success cannot satisfy this
first-result predicate.

#### Exact counts and sharp families

The proof-side inputSteps definition follows the actual source return sequence.
Its all-raw bound is branchwise arithmetic using actual parse consumption
lengths. Useful exact length equalities come from parseTreeRun_iff plus
List.length_append, avoiding an unnecessary conversion through node counts.
The source-draft already contains this proposed proof and Type-valued exact/
linear timed data for the same installed transition.

For code and code-plus-trailing count simplification, use a local exact source
bits equation in the shape

```text
parseBitsRun (bitTags bs ++ endInputTag :: rest)
  = (some (bs,rest), 3*bs.length+2)
```

derived from the existing parseBitsRun_code with append normalization. Then
unfold inputSteps, use both parseTreeRun_code returns and separator equations,
and select the actual EOF branch. Success gives2Ls+2Lt+2b+9, hence2M+3 and
4ns+4nt+2b+13. Nonempty trailing input gives4Ls+4Lt+4b+18 without inspecting
that trailing word.

The two sharp time witnesses are the already written outcome traces at missing

/-- Two owned traces with unowned endpoints stop at the same first handoff. -/
theorem Runs.first_length_eq {n m : Nat} {start left right : Cfg Γ Λ R}
    (first : Runs caller n start left) (second : Runs caller m start right)
    (leftExit : ¬ FullOwned left.l) (rightExit : ¬ FullOwned right.l) : n = m := by
  apply Nat.le_antisymm
  · by_contra larger
    have strict : m < n := by omega
    obtain ⟨reached, executed, owned⟩ := first.owned_prefix caller m strict
    have equal : reached = right := Option.some.inj (executed.symm.trans (second.iterate caller))
    exact rightExit (equal ▸ owned)
  · by_contra larger
    have strict : n < m := by omega
    obtain ⟨reached, executed, owned⟩ := second.owned_prefix caller n strict
    have equal : reached = left := Option.some.inj (executed.symm.trans (first.iterate caller))
    exact leftExit (equal ▸ owned)

    {n : Nat} {final : Cfg Γ Λ R} (trace : Runs caller n (entry regs raw ctx) final)

    (resultCfg_not_owned raw regs ctx (parseInputRun raw).1) exit

/-- A finite presentation of exactly the owned labels; external callers are absent. -/
abbrev OwnedLabels := (TreeSide × TreeParserMachine.Phase) ⊕ (TreeSide ⊕ (Unit ⊕ Phase))

def ownedLabelEquiv : OwnedLabels ≃ {label : Label Λ // FullOwned (some label)} where
  toFun
    | .inl (d, phase) => ⟨treeLabel d phase, fullOwned_tree d phase⟩
    | .inr (.inl d) => ⟨treeResultLabel d .success, by cases d <;> trivial⟩
    | .inr (.inr (.inl _)) => ⟨treeResultLabel .target .failure, True.intro⟩
    | .inr (.inr (.inr phase)) => ⟨phaseLabel phase, fullOwned_phase phase⟩
  invFun
    | ⟨.inl (d, phase), _⟩ => .inl (d, phase)
    | ⟨.inr (.inl (d, .success)), _⟩ => .inr (.inl d)
    | ⟨.inr (.inl (.target, .failure)), _⟩ => .inr (.inr (.inl ()))
    | ⟨.inr (.inr (.inl phase)), _⟩ => .inr (.inr (.inr phase))
    | ⟨.inr (.inl (.source, .failure)), impossible⟩ => False.elim impossible
    | ⟨.inr (.inr (.inr _)), impossible⟩ => False.elim impossible
  left_inv label := by
    cases label with
    | inl pair => rcases pair with ⟨d, phase⟩; rfl
    | inr external =>
        cases external with
        | inl d => cases d <;> rfl
        | inr extra => cases extra with
          | inl token => cases token; rfl
          | inr phase => rfl
  right_inv label := by
    rcases label with ⟨label, owned⟩
    cases label with
    | inl pair => rcases pair with ⟨d, phase⟩; rfl
    | inr external =>
        cases external with
        | inl pair =>
            rcases pair with ⟨d, result⟩
            cases d with
            | source => cases result with
              | success => rfl
              | failure => cases owned
            | target => cases result <;> rfl
        | inr extra => cases extra with
          | inl phase => rfl
          | inr exit => cases owned

instance fullOwnedFintype : Fintype {label : Label Λ // FullOwned (some label)} :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv OwnedLabels ownedLabelEquiv

theorem fullOwned_card : Fintype.card {label : Label Λ // FullOwned (some label)} = 25 := by
  calc
    _ = Fintype.card OwnedLabels := (Fintype.card_congr ownedLabelEquiv).symm
    _ = 25 := by decide

omit [DecidableEq K] in
theorem stackId_card [Fintype K] : Fintype.card (StackId K) = 7 + Fintype.card K := by
  have localCard : Fintype.card (TreeParserMachine.LocalStack TreeSide) = 5 := by decide
  have extraCard : Fintype.card ExtraStack = 2 := by decide
  simp only [StackId, TreeParserMachine.StackId, Fintype.card_sum, localCard, extraCard]
  omega

theorem label_card [Fintype Λ] : Fintype.card (Label Λ) = 27 + Fintype.card Λ := by
  have sideCard : Fintype.card TreeSide = 2 := by decide
  have treePhaseCard : Fintype.card TreeParserMachine.Phase = 5 := by decide
  have resultCard : Fintype.card TreeParserMachine.Result = 2 := by decide
  have phaseCard : Fintype.card Phase = 12 := by decide
  simp only [Label, TreeParserMachine.Label, TreeParserMachine.External, Fintype.card_sum,
    Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_unit, sideCard, treePhaseCard, resultCard, phaseCard]
  omega

theorem registers_card [Fintype R] : Fintype.card (Registers R) = 34 * Fintype.card R := by
  have tagCard : Fintype.card Tag = 16 := by decide
  simp only [Registers, TreeParserMachine.Registers, TreeParserMachine.Temporaries,
    Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_option, Fintype.card_unit, tagCard]
  omega

variable [Fintype K] [Fintype Λ] [Fintype R] [∀ k, Fintype (Γ k)]

  | nil => exact False.elim (nonempty rfl)

    (eof_nonempty_step caller raw [] [] regs (treeOutputs source target) bs [] ctx nonempty)).trans caller

    (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) (nonempty : raw ≠ []) :
    Runs caller (4 * (treeCode source).length + 4 * (treeCode target).length + 4 * bs.length + 18)

      4 * (treeCode source).length + 4 * (treeCode target).length + 4 * bs.length + 18 := by omega

/-- Cells outside the pending stack, including both destination outputs and both Boolean stacks. -/
def outputCells (outputs : TreeSide → Word) : Nat :=
  (outputs .source).length + (outputs .target).length

def baseCells (c : Cfg Γ Λ R) : Nat :=
  (c.stk rawStack).length + (c.stk reverseStack).length +
    outputCells (fun d => c.stk (outputStack d)) +
    (c.stk fuelStack).length + (c.stk bitsReverseStack).length

def sideDebt : TreeSide → Nat | .source => 0 | .target => 1

def phaseDebt : Phase → Nat
  | .bitsScan | .fuelUndo | .bitsUndo | .restoreSep2 => 2
  | .bitsEmit | .eof | .restoreEnd => 3
  | .targetToReverse | .targetToRaw | .restoreSep1 => 1
  | .sourceToReverse | .sourceToRaw => 0

/-- Delimiters consumed but not yet physically restored; purely a control-label annotation. -/
def debt : Option (Label Λ) → Nat
  | some (.inl (d, _)) | some (.inr (.inl (d, _))) => sideDebt d
  | some (.inr (.inr (.inl phase))) => phaseDebt phase
  | some (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl _)))) => 3
  | _ => 0

@[simp] theorem debt_tree (d : TreeSide) (phase : TreeParserMachine.Phase) :
    debt (some (treeLabel (Λ := Λ) d phase)) = sideDebt d := rfl
@[simp] theorem debt_treeResult (d : TreeSide) (result : TreeParserMachine.Result) :
    debt (some (treeResultLabel (Λ := Λ) d result)) = sideDebt d := rfl
@[simp] theorem debt_phase (phase : Phase) :
    debt (some (phaseLabel (Λ := Λ) phase)) = phaseDebt phase := rfl

/-- The scan has one slot credit per unread symbol. Rollback needs only the absolute slot bound. -/
def pendingCondition (M : Nat) (label : Option (Label Λ)) (rawLength : Nat) (pending : List Unit) : Prop :=
  match label with
  | some (.inl (_, .scan)) => pending.length + rawLength ≤ M + 1
  | some (.inl (_, .undo)) | some (.inl (_, .dropPending)) => pending.length ≤ M + 1
  | _ => pending = []

/-- Every additional literal body has an exact mass effect and preserves the protected frame. -/
theorem phase_step_effect (phase : Phase) (raw rev : Word) (pending : List Unit)
    (regs : Registers R) (outputs : TreeSide → Word) (fuel bitsReverse : Bits)
    (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) {after : Cfg Γ Λ R}
    (executed : step caller (cfg (some (phaseLabel phase)) regs raw rev pending
      outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx) = some after) :

      | nil =>

            (bitsScan_step_nil caller rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
          apply cfg_effect
          · rfl
          · intro M _ slots; exact slots
      | cons tag raw =>
          by_cases zero : tag = bitZeroTag
          · subst tag
            apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
              (bitsScan_step_bit caller false raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
            apply cfg_effect
            · simp only [List.length_cons]; omega
            · intro M _ slots; exact slots
          · by_cases one : tag = bitOneTag
            · subst tag
              apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
                (bitsScan_step_bit caller true raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
              apply cfg_effect
              · simp only [List.length_cons]; omega
              · intro M _ slots; exact slots
            · by_cases finished : tag = endInputTag
              · subst tag
                apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
                  (bitsScan_step_end caller raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
                apply cfg_effect
                · simp only [debt_phase, phaseDebt, List.length_cons]; omega
                · intro M _ slots; exact slots
              · apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
                  (bitsScan_step_foreign caller tag raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx finished zero one)
                apply cfg_effect
                · rfl
                · intro M _ slots; exact slots
  | bitsEmit =>
      cases bitsReverse with
      | nil =>
          apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
            (bitsEmit_step_nil caller raw rev pending regs outputs fuel ctx)
          apply cfg_effect
          · rfl
          · intro M _ slots; exact slots
      | cons b bitsReverse =>
          apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
            (bitsEmit_step_cons caller b raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
          apply cfg_effect
          · simp only [List.length_cons]; omega
          · intro M _ slots; exact slots
  | eof =>
      cases raw with
      | nil =>
          apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
            (eof_step_nil caller rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
          apply cfg_effect
          · rfl
          · intro M _ slots; exact slots
      | cons tag raw =>
          apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
            (eof_step_cons caller tag raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
          apply cfg_effect
          · rfl
          · intro M _ slots; exact slots
  | restoreEnd =>
      apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed

      | cons b fuel =>

            (fuelUndo_step_cons caller b raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
          apply cfg_effect
          · simp only [List.length_cons]; omega
          · intro M _ slots; exact slots
  | bitsUndo =>

      | nil =>

          · rfl
          · intro M _ slots; exact slots
      | cons b bitsReverse =>

  | targetToReverse => exact toReverse_step_effect caller .target raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx executed
  | sourceToReverse => exact toReverse_step_effect caller .source raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx executed
  | targetToRaw => exact toRaw_step_effect caller .target raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx executed
  | sourceToRaw => exact toRaw_step_effect caller .source raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx executed

private theorem cfg_step_effect (label : Option (Label Λ)) (raw rev : Word) (pending : List Unit)
    (regs : Registers R) (outputs : TreeSide → Word) (fuel bitsReverse : Bits)
    (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) {after : Cfg Γ Λ R} (owned : FullOwned label)
    (executed : step caller (cfg label regs raw rev pending outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx) = some after) :
    Effect (cfg label regs raw rev pending outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx) after := by
  cases label with
  | none => cases owned
  | some label =>
      cases label with
      | inl pair =>
          rcases pair with ⟨d, phase⟩
          exact tree_step_effect caller d phase raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx executed
      | inr external =>
          cases external with
          | inl pair =>
              rcases pair with ⟨d, result⟩
              cases result with
              | success => exact separator_step_effect caller d raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx executed
              | failure =>
                  cases d with
                  | source => cases owned
                  | target =>
                      apply effect_of_step_eq caller executed
                        (targetFailure_step caller raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx)
                      apply cfg_effect
                      · simp only [debt_treeResult, sideDebt, debt_phase, phaseDebt, List.length_cons]; omega
                      · intro M _ slots; exact slots
          | inr extra =>
              cases extra with
              | inl phase => exact phase_step_effect caller phase raw rev pending regs outputs fuel bitsReverse ctx executed
              | inr exit => cases owned

/-- A local theorem about actual full-owned steps, including states with dirty accumulators. -/
theorem step_effect {before after : Cfg Γ Λ R} (owned : FullOwned before.l)
    (executed : step caller before = some after) : Effect before after := by
  have reconstructed := cfg_eta before
  have explicitStep : step caller
      (cfg before.l before.var (before.stk rawStack) (before.stk reverseStack) (before.stk pendingStack)
        (fun d => before.stk (outputStack d)) (before.stk fuelStack) (before.stk bitsReverseStack)
        (fun k => before.stk (protectedStack k))) = some after := by
    rw [reconstructed]
    exact executed
  have effect := cfg_step_effect caller before.l (before.stk rawStack) (before.stk reverseStack)
    (before.stk pendingStack) before.var (fun d => before.stk (outputStack d))
    (before.stk fuelStack) (before.stk bitsReverseStack) (fun k => before.stk (protectedStack k)) owned explicitStep
  simpa only [reconstructed] using effect

theorem Runs.mass {n : Nat} {start final : Cfg Γ Λ R} (run : Runs caller n start final) :
    baseCells final + debt final.l = baseCells start + debt start.l := by
  induction run with
  | refl c => rfl
  | cons owned executed run ih => exact ih.trans (step_effect caller owned executed).mass

theorem Runs.frame {n : Nat} {start final : Cfg Γ Λ R} (run : Runs caller n start final) :
    ∀ k, final.stk (protectedStack k) = start.stk (protectedStack k) := by
  induction run with
  | refl c => exact fun _ => rfl
  | cons owned executed run ih =>
      intro k
      exact (ih k).trans ((step_effect caller owned executed).frame k)

theorem Runs.registers {n : Nat} {start final : Cfg Γ Λ R} (run : Runs caller n start final) :
    final.var = if n = 0 then start.var else reset start.var := by
  induction run with
  | refl c => rfl
  | @cons n start middle final owned executed run ih =>
      change final.var = reset start.var
      rw [ih, (step_effect caller owned executed).registers]
      split <;> rfl

theorem Runs.pending {n : Nat} {start final : Cfg Γ Λ R} (run : Runs caller n start final)
    {M : Nat} (mass : baseCells start + debt start.l = M) (slots : PendingControl M start) :
    PendingControl M final := by
  induction run generalizing M with
  | refl c => exact slots
  | cons owned executed run ih =>
      have effect := step_effect caller owned executed
      exact ih (effect.mass.trans mass) (effect.pending M mass slots)

/-- Exact preserved state at every prefix, including the first live handoff and the unreset zero prefix. -/
theorem prefix_preserves (raw : Word) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k))
    (n : Nat) (bound : n ≤ inputSteps raw) (reached : Cfg Γ Λ R)
    (executed : (next caller)^[n] (some (entry regs raw ctx)) = some reached) :
    reached.var = (if n = 0 then regs else reset regs) ∧
      (∀ k, reached.stk (protectedStack k) = ctx k) ∧
      baseCells reached + debt reached.l = raw.length ∧ PendingControl raw.length reached := by
  obtain ⟨actual, equation, before, _, _⟩ := run_prefix caller raw regs ctx n bound
  have equal : actual = reached := Option.some.inj (equation.symm.trans executed)
  subst reached
  have initialMass : baseCells (entry (Λ := Λ) regs raw ctx) + debt (entry (Λ := Λ) regs raw ctx).l = raw.length := rfl
  refine ⟨before.registers caller, before.frame caller, (before.mass caller).trans initialMass, ?_⟩
  exact before.pending caller initialMass rfl

theorem pendingControl_bound (M : Nat) (c : Cfg Γ Λ R) (slots : PendingControl M c) :
    (c.stk pendingStack).length ≤ M + 1 := by
  unfold PendingControl pendingCondition at slots
  split at slots <;> simp_all only [List.length_nil] <;> omega

theorem pendingControl_empty (M : Nat) (c : Cfg Γ Λ R) (slots : PendingControl M c)
    (outside : ¬ TreeParserMachine.Owned c.l) : c.stk pendingStack = [] := by
  cases labelEq : c.l with
  | none => simpa only [PendingControl, pendingCondition, labelEq] using slots
  | some label =>
      cases label with
      | inl pair => exact False.elim (outside (by simp only [labelEq, TreeParserMachine.Owned]))
      | inr external => simpa only [PendingControl, pendingCondition, labelEq] using slots

theorem prefix_pending_empty (raw : Word) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k))
    (n : Nat) (bound : n ≤ inputSteps raw) (reached : Cfg Γ Λ R)
    (executed : (next caller)^[n] (some (entry regs raw ctx)) = some reached)
    (outside : ¬ TreeParserMachine.Owned reached.l) : reached.stk pendingStack = [] :=
  pendingControl_empty raw.length reached (prefix_preserves caller raw regs ctx n bound reached executed).2.2.2 outside

section Space
variable [Fintype K]

def contextCells (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) : Nat := ∑ k, (ctx k).length

/-- The cells of all seven owned stacks plus every protected caller stack. -/
def stackCells (c : Cfg Γ Λ R) : Nat :=
  baseCells c + (c.stk pendingStack).length + contextCells (fun k => c.stk (protectedStack k))

theorem prefix_stackCells_le (raw : Word) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k))
    (n : Nat) (bound : n ≤ inputSteps raw) (reached : Cfg Γ Λ R)
    (executed : (next caller)^[n] (some (entry regs raw ctx)) = some reached) :
    stackCells reached ≤ 2 * raw.length + contextCells ctx + 1 := by
  obtain ⟨_, frame, mass, slots⟩ := prefix_preserves caller raw regs ctx n bound reached executed
  have pendingBound := pendingControl_bound raw.length reached slots
  have sameContext : (fun k => reached.stk (protectedStack k)) = ctx := funext frame
  unfold stackCells
  rw [sameContext]
  omega

end Space

section SharpSpace
variable [Fintype K]

/-- An actual prefix attains the universal cell bound for every raw length. -/
theorem nodes_prefix_sharp (count : Nat) (regs : Registers R) (ctx : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) :
    ∃ reached,
      (next caller)^[count + 1] (some (entry regs (List.replicate count nodeTag) ctx)) = some reached ∧
      count + 1 < inputSteps (List.replicate count nodeTag) ∧
      stackCells reached = 2 * count + contextCells ctx + 1 := by
  refine ⟨_, nodes_prefix caller count regs ctx, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [inputSteps_nodes]
    omega
  · change 0 + (List.replicate count nodeTag).length + 0 + 0 + 0 +
      (List.replicate (count + 1) ()).length + contextCells ctx = _
    simp only [List.length_replicate]
    omega

end SharpSpace

import Applications.Resources.BinaryCounter.FixedWidthMachine
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.List

/-!
# Static finite-statement transport for the physical front end

Uncompiled continuation draft. The maps below change the representation of the
same physical stacks and finite control. They do not execute a source parser,
allocate a stack, transfer data between distinct stacks, or erase a real step.
The full concrete fourteen-stack front-end installation remains to be written.

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option warningAsError true

namespace Resources.RotationCertificate.FrontEndMachine.Transport

variable {K K' Λ Λ' R R' : Type} {Γ : K → Type} {Γ' : K' → Type}
variable (names : K ≃ K') (symbols : ∀ k, Γ k ≃ Γ' (names k))
  (registers : R ≃ R') (labels : Λ → Λ')

def stackEquiv : (∀ k, List (Γ k)) ≃ (∀ j, List (Γ' j)) :=
  names.piCongr (fun k => Equiv.listEquivOfEquiv (symbols k))

@[simp] theorem stackEquiv_apply (data : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) (k : K) :
    stackEquiv names symbols data (names k) = (data k).map (symbols k) := by
  exact Equiv.piCongr_apply_apply names (fun k => Equiv.listEquivOfEquiv (symbols k)) data k

def cfg (c : Turing.TM2.Cfg Γ Λ R) : Turing.TM2.Cfg Γ' Λ' R' where
  l := c.l.map labels
  var := registers c.var
  stk := stackEquiv names symbols c.stk

theorem cfg_injective (injective : Function.Injective labels) :
    Function.Injective (cfg names symbols registers labels) := by
  intro before after equal
  have labelEq := congrArg Turing.TM2.Cfg.l equal
  have registerEq := congrArg Turing.TM2.Cfg.var equal
  have stackEq := congrArg Turing.TM2.Cfg.stk equal
  have labelEq' := Option.map_injective injective labelEq
  have registerEq' := registers.injective registerEq
  have stackEq' := (stackEquiv names symbols).injective stackEq
  cases before
  cases after
  cases labelEq'
  cases registerEq'
  cases stackEq'
  rfl

/-- Only finite syntax and finite callbacks are translated. -/
def statement : Turing.TM2.Stmt Γ Λ R → Turing.TM2.Stmt Γ' Λ' R'
  | .push k value tail =>
      .push (names k) (fun regs => symbols k (value (registers.symm regs)))
        (statement tail)
  | .peek k store tail =>
      .peek (names k)
        (fun regs value => registers (store (registers.symm regs) (value.map (symbols k).symm)))
        (statement tail)
  | .pop k store tail =>
      .pop (names k)
        (fun regs value => registers (store (registers.symm regs) (value.map (symbols k).symm)))
        (statement tail)
  | .load update tail =>
      .load (fun regs => registers (update (registers.symm regs))) (statement tail)
  | .branch test yes no =>
      .branch (fun regs => test (registers.symm regs)) (statement yes) (statement no)
  | .goto label => .goto (fun regs => labels (label (registers.symm regs)))
  | .halt => .halt

theorem observed_head (k : K) (data : List (Γ k)) :
    ((data.map (symbols k)).head?).map (symbols k).symm = data.head? := by
  cases data <;> simp

theorem mapped_tail (k : K) (data : List (Γ k)) :
    (data.map (symbols k)).tail = data.tail.map (symbols k) := by
  cases data <;> rfl

variable [DecidableEq K] [DecidableEq K']

theorem stackEquiv_update (data : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) (k : K) (value : List (Γ k)) :
    stackEquiv names symbols (Function.update data k value) =

  funext j
  obtain ⟨other, rfl⟩ := names.surjective j
  by_cases equal : other = k
  · subst other

  · have different : names other ≠ names k := fun h => equal (names.injective h)
    simp only [stackEquiv_apply, Function.update_of_ne equal, Function.update_of_ne different]

/-- The proof follows each actual primitive in the pinned TM2 evaluator. -/
theorem stepAux (body : Turing.TM2.Stmt Γ Λ R) (regs : R) (data : ∀ k, List (Γ k)) :

  | peek k store tail ih =>
      simp only [statement, Turing.TM2.stepAux, Equiv.symm_apply_apply,

  | pop k store tail ih =>
      simp only [statement, Turing.TM2.stepAux, Equiv.symm_apply_apply,
        stackEquiv_apply, observed_head, mapped_tail]
      rw [← stackEquiv_update, ih]

def next (program : Λ → Turing.TM2.Stmt Γ Λ R) :
    Option (Turing.TM2.Cfg Γ Λ R) → Option (Turing.TM2.Cfg Γ Λ R) :=
  fun c => c.bind (Turing.TM2.step program)

theorem next_map (source : Λ → Turing.TM2.Stmt Γ Λ R)
    (ambient : Λ' → Turing.TM2.Stmt Γ' Λ' R')
